**BIRCHWOOD & HALE LLP** **Attorneys at Law --- Real Estate \| Corporate \| Litigation** 191 Peachtree Street NE, Suite 4200 Atlanta, GA 30303 Tel: (404) 555-8200 \| Fax: (404) 555-8201 www.birchwoodhale.com

December 5, 2024

Mr. Marcus Aldaine Managing Director Galleon Capital Advisors LLC 1200 Peachtree Street NE, Suite 3100 Atlanta, GA 30309

**Re: Engagement for Lease Abstraction and Due Diligence Review --- Acquisition of 12-Property Mixed-Use Portfolio from Thornfield Realty Holdings LP; Purchase Price: \$187,500,000**

Dear Mr. Aldaine:

**[1. Purpose of Engagement]{.underline}**

I am writing on behalf of Birchwood & Hale LLP to confirm the firm\'s engagement by Galleon Capital Advisors LLC (\"Galleon\" or \"Client\") in connection with the lease abstraction and due diligence review of seven (7) key commercial leases within the twelve-property mixed-use portfolio (the \"Portfolio\") being acquired by Galleon from Thornfield Realty Holdings LP (\"Thornfield\" or \"Seller\") for a purchase price of One Hundred Eighty-Seven Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$187,500,000) (the \"Acquisition\"). This engagement arises in connection with the Purchase and Sale Agreement executed by the parties on November 15, 2024 (the \"PSA\"). We understand that the due diligence period under the PSA commenced on November 16, 2024 and expires on January 31, 2025, a period of seventy-seven (77) days, with a target closing date of March 15, 2025.

Galleon has requested that Birchwood & Hale extract, organize, and analyze the material terms of seven commercial leases across the Portfolio and deliver a comprehensive lease abstraction report (the \"Report\") that will assist Galleon in evaluating the leased assets, identifying risk items, and informing pre-closing negotiations and decision-making. My colleague Devon Pratt, Senior Associate, will serve as the day-to-day lead attorney on the lease review, and I will provide oversight and be available to address any matters requiring partner-level attention.

**[2. Scope of Engagement]{.underline}**

The scope of the firm\'s engagement is defined as follows:

**(a) Lease Abstraction.** Birchwood & Hale will review and abstract the following seven (7) commercial leases across the Portfolio:

> 1\. **Apex Fulfillment Services Inc.** --- Thornfield Distribution Center, 4200 Logistics Parkway, Charlotte, NC 28214 (approximately 87,500 RSF warehouse/distribution space);
>
> 2\. **Dr. Miriam Soto, DDS, PA** --- Millbrook Medical Plaza, 1585 Millbrook Road, Suite 200, Raleigh, NC 27609 (approximately 3,200 RSF medical/dental office);
>
> 3\. **BrightPath Learning Centers LLC** --- Millbrook Medical Plaza, 1585 Millbrook Road, Suite 100, Raleigh, NC 27609 (approximately 5,800 RSF childcare facility);
>
> 4\. **Southeastern Fire & Safety Equipment Co.** --- Greystone Industrial Park, 770 Greystone Boulevard, Unit 12, Gastonia, NC 28052 (approximately 22,000 RSF industrial/flex space);
>
> 5\. **Verdana Software Solutions Inc.** --- Concord Office Tower, 300 Concord Plaza Drive, 8th Floor, Atlanta, GA 30309 (approximately 18,750 RSF Class A office);
>
> 6\. **The Pint & Platter Restaurant Group LLC** --- Haywood Village Shops, 92 Haywood Street, Unit 4, Asheville, NC 28801 (approximately 4,400 RSF ground-floor retail/restaurant); and
>
> 7\. **United States of America (General Services Administration)**, GSA Lease No. GS-04B-15678 --- Concord Office Tower, 300 Concord Plaza Drive, 5th Floor, Atlanta, GA 30309 (approximately 15,000 RSF government office).

**(b) Rent Roll Cross-Reference.** The firm will cross-reference the lease terms as abstracted against the portfolio rent roll prepared by Thornfield\'s property manager, Karen Osgood, to identify any inconsistencies between the rent roll and the underlying lease documents.

**(c) Rent Escalation Verification.** The firm will independently verify all rent escalation calculations and financial terms stated in each lease, including base rent schedules, percentage rent calculations (if applicable), CPI adjustment mechanics, and any free rent or abatement provisions.

**(d) Risk Identification.** The firm will identify and flag any mathematical discrepancies, ambiguous provisions, missing documentation or protections, approaching deadlines (including option exercise dates, renewal notice periods, and co-tenancy triggers), holdover situations, and other risk items that may affect Galleon\'s valuation of the Portfolio or the closing of the Acquisition.

**(e) Standardized Abstraction Report.** The firm will prepare a standardized lease abstraction report covering the following twelve (12) categories of terms for each lease:

> \(1\) Tenant and Premises; (2) Term; (3) Rent; (4) Lease Type; (5) Operating Expenses; (6) Renewal Options; (7) Termination Rights; (8) Assignment and Subletting; (9) Security Deposit / Guaranty; (10) Tenant Improvements; (11) Special Provisions; and (12) Risk Flags.

**(f) Executive Summary.** The Report will include an Executive Summary providing portfolio-level analysis, including: aggregate current annual base rent (estimated at approximately \$2,347,843.50 across the seven leases); weighted average remaining lease term; tenant concentration analysis; a prioritized listing of risk items; and recommended pre-closing actions for Galleon\'s consideration.

The seven leases subject to this engagement represent approximately 156,650 RSF of the total Portfolio\'s 243,650 RSF across all twelve properties. The remaining five properties are being reviewed under separate workstreams outside the scope of this engagement.

**Scope Limitations.** This engagement does not include: title review (which we understand is being handled by Stonebridge Title & Escrow LLC); environmental due diligence (being handled by Hanover Environmental Consultants Inc.); financial or accounting review of Thornfield\'s books and records (maintained by Crestline Accounting Group LLP); debt placement or financing activities (being handled by Fieldstone Capital Markets LLC); or brokerage matters (listing broker: Ridgeview Realty Brokers Inc.). The firm is not providing tax advice in connection with this engagement, and Galleon is encouraged to consult with its tax advisors as appropriate.

**[3. Deliverables and Timeline]{.underline}**

**Primary Deliverable.** The primary deliverable under this engagement is the comprehensive Lease Abstraction Report (the \"Report\"), to be delivered in Microsoft Word format. The Report will include: (i) individual lease abstractions for each of the seven leases in the twelve-category format described in Section 2(e) above; (ii) a portfolio rent roll cross-check identifying any discrepancies between the lease documents and the rent roll provided by Thornfield\'s property manager; (iii) a risk matrix identifying and prioritizing all flagged items by severity and time-sensitivity; and (iv) specific recommended actions for Galleon\'s consideration prior to the March 15, 2025 target closing date.

**Delivery Deadline.** The firm will use commercially reasonable efforts to deliver the final Report by **December 20, 2024**. This timeline is designed to provide Galleon approximately six (6) weeks within the remaining due diligence period (which expires January 31, 2025) to act on any identified issues, request estoppels or additional documentation from the Seller, and negotiate appropriate protections or purchase price adjustments as warranted.

**Interim Communication.** Devon Pratt will provide weekly status updates to Marcus Aldaine by email regarding the progress of the lease review. In addition, the firm will promptly communicate any material risk items or time-sensitive findings as they arise during the review process and will not wait for delivery of the final Report to flag critical items requiring immediate attention.

**Document Access.** Galleon will arrange for delivery of complete lease files --- including all amendments, exhibits, side letters, subordination, non-disturbance and attornment agreements (SNDAs), estoppel certificates, and guaranties --- to Birchwood & Hale no later than **December 6, 2024**. Delays in the delivery of lease documents or supporting materials may extend the December 20, 2024 delivery timeline, and the firm will notify Galleon promptly if any such delay is anticipated.

**[4. Fee Arrangement]{.underline}**

**Hourly Rates.** Fees for this engagement will be billed on a time-and-materials basis at the following standard hourly rates:

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Professional**                    **Rate**
  ----------------------------------- -----------------------------------
  Lydia Chen, Partner                 \$575/hour

  Devon Pratt, Senior Associate       \$385/hour

  Paralegal Support                   \$195/hour
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------

**Fee Cap.** Total professional fees for the lease abstraction engagement described herein shall not exceed **Forty-Five Thousand Dollars (\$45,000)** (the \"Fee Cap\"), inclusive of all attorney and paralegal time. The Fee Cap does not include out-of-pocket disbursements (e.g., travel expenses, copying, courier services, and database access fees), which will be billed at cost and are estimated not to exceed One Thousand Five Hundred Dollars (\$1,500).

**Scope Adjustments.** The Fee Cap is predicated on the assumption that the scope of the engagement is limited to the seven (7) leases and the rent roll described in Section 2 above. If Galleon requests that the firm review additional leases from the remaining five portfolio properties, or if the scope of the engagement expands materially (for example, to include lease renegotiations, amendment drafting, or estoppel review beyond what is contained in existing lease files), fees for such additional work will be billed outside the Fee Cap at the standard hourly rates set forth above, subject to prior written approval from Galleon.

**Invoicing and Payment.** The firm will issue monthly invoices containing customary detail of time entries and disbursements. Payment is due within thirty (30) days of the invoice date. No retainer is required for this engagement.

**[5. Client Responsibilities]{.underline}**

Galleon agrees to fulfill the following responsibilities in connection with this engagement:

> \(a\) Provide complete and accurate copies of all lease documents, amendments, exhibits, rent rolls, tenant correspondence, and related materials in Galleon\'s possession or obtainable from the Seller (Thornfield Realty Holdings LP, through Renata Thornfield-Kiess, President, or Karen Osgood, Property Manager) in a timely manner;
>
> \(b\) Designate Marcus Aldaine as the primary contact for all matters related to the engagement, with authority to provide instructions and approvals on behalf of Galleon;
>
> \(c\) Respond promptly to requests for additional information, clarification, or direction from the firm\'s engagement team; and
>
> \(d\) Acknowledge that the firm\'s analysis will be based solely on the documents provided to the firm by Galleon or on Galleon\'s behalf. Birchwood & Hale is not responsible for verifying facts, representations, or conditions beyond the four corners of the lease documents and rent roll unless specifically directed to do so in writing by Galleon.

**[6. Confidentiality]{.underline}**

Birchwood & Hale will maintain the confidentiality of all information provided by or on behalf of Galleon in connection with this engagement. Such information will not be disclosed to third parties without Galleon\'s prior written consent, except as may be required by applicable law, court order, or professional obligation. The foregoing confidentiality obligation does not extend to information that is or becomes publicly available through no fault of the firm, or that is independently known to the firm from sources unrelated to this engagement.

**[7. Conflicts Check]{.underline}**

The firm has conducted a conflicts check in connection with this engagement and confirms that Birchwood & Hale does not currently represent Thornfield Realty Holdings LP, Thornfield Management Corp., any of the seven tenants listed in Section 2(a) above, Highpoint National Bank (lender on the Thornfield Distribution Center), or any other party to the Acquisition in a matter adverse to Galleon. Should a conflict of interest arise during the course of the engagement, the firm will promptly notify Galleon and take appropriate steps to address the conflict, which may include withdrawal from the engagement if the conflict cannot be resolved or waived in accordance with applicable rules of professional conduct.

**[8. Limitation of Liability / Disclaimer]{.underline}**

The Report is prepared for the sole use of Galleon Capital Advisors LLC and its authorized representatives in connection with the evaluation of the Portfolio acquisition described herein. The Report is not intended to be relied upon by any third party, including lenders (including Fieldstone Capital Markets LLC in its capacity as debt placement agent), title companies, insurers, or other advisors, without the prior written consent of Birchwood & Hale LLP. The Report constitutes legal analysis based upon the documents provided to the firm and does not guarantee the enforceability of any lease provision, the creditworthiness or financial condition of any tenant, or the accuracy of any representation made by the Seller or any third party. Galleon is encouraged to independently verify all financial information and conduct such additional due diligence as it deems appropriate in connection with the Acquisition.

**[9. Governing Law and Dispute Resolution]{.underline}**

This engagement letter shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Georgia, without regard to its conflicts-of-law principles. Any disputes arising out of or related to this engagement or the services provided hereunder shall be resolved by binding arbitration in Atlanta, Georgia, administered under the Commercial Arbitration Rules of the American Arbitration Association then in effect.

**[10. Acceptance]{.underline}**

Please confirm Galleon\'s agreement to the terms of this engagement by signing and returning a copy of this letter to my attention. This engagement letter, once countersigned, supersedes any prior oral or written understandings between Birchwood & Hale LLP and Galleon Capital Advisors LLC regarding the scope of work described herein.

We look forward to working with you on this important acquisition. Please do not hesitate to contact me or Devon Pratt if you have any questions regarding the terms of this engagement or the lease review process.

Very truly yours,

**BIRCHWOOD & HALE LLP**

**[LEASE AGREEMENT]{.underline}**

**[LEASE AGREEMENT]{.underline}**

**THIS LEASE AGREEMENT** (this \"Lease\") is made and entered into as of the 1st day of March, 2019 (the \"Lease Date\"), by and between **THORNFIELD REALTY HOLDINGS LP**, a North Carolina limited partnership, whose general partner is Thornfield Management Corp., a North Carolina corporation, with its registered office at 500 South Tryon Street, Suite 2200, Charlotte, North Carolina 28202 (\"Landlord\"), and **APEX FULFILLMENT SERVICES INC.**, a Delaware corporation, with its principal office at 4200 Logistics Parkway, Charlotte, North Carolina 28214 (\"Tenant\").

**[RECITALS]{.underline}**

**WHEREAS**, Landlord is the fee simple owner of that certain real property known as Thornfield Distribution Center, consisting of Buildings A, B, and C, situated on approximately twenty-five (25) acres of land located at 4200 Logistics Parkway, Charlotte, Mecklenburg County, North Carolina 28214, as more particularly described on the Site Plan attached hereto as Exhibit A (collectively, the \"Property\");

**WHEREAS**, Landlord\'s general partner is Thornfield Management Corp., a North Carolina corporation, duly authorized to act on behalf of Landlord in all matters relating to the management, leasing, and operation of the Property;

**WHEREAS**, Tenant is Apex Fulfillment Services Inc., a corporation duly organized and existing under the laws of the State of Delaware, qualified to do business in the State of North Carolina, and engaged in the business of third-party logistics, fulfillment, and distribution services;

**WHEREAS**, Tenant desires to lease the entirety of Building C within the Thornfield Distribution Center for use as a warehouse and distribution/fulfillment facility; and

**WHEREAS**, the parties wish to set forth the terms and conditions upon which Landlord shall lease the Premises to Tenant and Tenant shall lease the Premises from Landlord.

**NOW, THEREFORE**, in consideration of the mutual covenants and agreements herein contained, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, Landlord and Tenant agree as follows:

**[ARTICLE I --- DEFINITIONS]{.underline}**

As used in this Lease, the following terms shall have the meanings set forth below. Capitalized terms used but not otherwise defined in this Article shall have the meanings assigned to them elsewhere in this Lease.

**\"Base Rent\"** shall mean the base rental amount payable by Tenant to Landlord during each Lease Year, as set forth in the Rent Schedule attached hereto as Exhibit B, subject to the escalation provisions of Article IV.

**\"Building\"** or **\"Building C\"** shall mean the building designated as Building C within Thornfield Distribution Center, located at 4200 Logistics Parkway, Charlotte, North Carolina 28214, as depicted on the Site Plan attached hereto as Exhibit A.

**\"Commencement Date\"** shall mean June 1, 2019, being the date on which the Lease Term commences and Tenant\'s obligation to pay Base Rent begins.

**\"Common Areas\"** shall mean all areas of the Property that are not exclusively leased to any tenant, including without limitation driveways, internal roadways, shared parking areas, loading zones not exclusively within Building C, landscaped areas, sidewalks, detention ponds, utility corridors, and other areas designated by Landlord from time to time for the common use and benefit of tenants and occupants of the Property.

**\"Expiration Date\"** shall mean May 31, 2029, being the last day of the initial Lease Term, unless sooner terminated or extended in accordance with the terms of this Lease.

**\"Landlord\"** shall mean Thornfield Realty Holdings LP, a North Carolina limited partnership, and its successors and assigns.

**\"Lease Date\"** shall mean March 1, 2019, the date first written above.

**\"Lease Term\"** shall mean the period commencing on the Commencement Date and ending on the Expiration Date, a period of ten (10) Lease Years, unless sooner terminated or extended in accordance with the terms of this Lease.

**\"Lease Year\"** shall mean each successive twelve (12) month period commencing on the Commencement Date. Lease Year 1 shall be the period from June 1, 2019 through May 31, 2020; Lease Year 2 shall be the period from June 1, 2020 through May 31, 2021; and so forth for each successive Lease Year during the Lease Term and any Renewal Term.

**\"Operating Expenses\"** shall mean all costs and expenses incurred by Landlord in operating, maintaining, repairing, managing, and administering the Property, including without limitation: insurance premiums; real estate taxes and assessments; common area maintenance charges; management fees; landscaping; snow and ice removal; utility costs for Common Areas; security services; janitorial and cleaning services for Common Areas; reasonable reserves for capital expenditures; and all other costs and expenses customarily associated with the operation of a first-class industrial/distribution property in the Charlotte, North Carolina metropolitan area.

**\"Permitted Use\"** shall mean third-party logistics, fulfillment, distribution, and warehouse operations, and ancillary office use in connection therewith.

**\"Premises\"** shall mean Building C, consisting of approximately eighty-seven thousand five hundred (87,500) rentable square feet (\"RSF\"), as depicted on the Site Plan attached hereto as Exhibit A.

**\"Property\"** shall mean Thornfield Distribution Center, located at 4200 Logistics Parkway, Charlotte, North Carolina 28214, including Buildings A, B, and C and all Common Areas appurtenant thereto.

**\"Pro Rata Share\"** shall mean Tenant\'s proportionate share of Operating Expenses, calculated as a fraction, the numerator of which is the RSF of the Premises (87,500 RSF) and the denominator of which is the total RSF of all buildings within the Property. As of the Lease Date, the total RSF of the Property is approximately two hundred forty thousand (240,000) RSF, resulting in a Pro Rata Share of approximately 36.46%. The Pro Rata Share shall be adjusted if the total RSF of the Property is modified by addition, demolition, or remeasurement.

**\"Rent Schedule\"** shall mean the schedule of Base Rent set forth in Exhibit B attached hereto.

**\"Tenant\"** shall mean Apex Fulfillment Services Inc., a Delaware corporation, and its permitted successors and assigns.

**\"Tenant Improvement Allowance\"** or **\"TI Allowance\"** shall mean the sum of Fifteen Dollars (\$15.00) per RSF of the Premises, aggregating One Million Three Hundred Twelve Thousand Five Hundred Dollars (\$1,312,500.00), as further described in Article IX and Exhibit C.

**[ARTICLE II --- PREMISES AND LEASE OF PREMISES]{.underline}**

**Section 2.1 --- Lease of Premises.** Landlord hereby leases to Tenant, and Tenant hereby leases from Landlord, the Premises known as Building C, Thornfield Distribution Center, 4200 Logistics Parkway, Charlotte, North Carolina 28214, consisting of approximately eighty-seven thousand five hundred (87,500) RSF of warehouse and distribution space, for the Lease Term and upon the terms and conditions set forth in this Lease.

**Section 2.2 --- Description of Premises.** The Premises include the entirety of Building C as depicted and outlined on the Site Plan attached hereto as Exhibit A, together with all fixtures, improvements, and appurtenances thereto. The Premises include all loading docks, drive-in doors, and other means of ingress and egress located within or serving exclusively Building C.

**Section 2.3 --- Common Area Access.** In addition to the Premises, Tenant shall have the non-exclusive right, in common with Landlord, other tenants, and their respective employees, agents, customers, and invitees, to use all Common Areas of the Property, including driveways, internal roadways, parking areas, and shared loading zones, subject to the reasonable rules and regulations promulgated by Landlord from time to time in accordance with this Lease and Exhibit D attached hereto.

**Section 2.4 --- Condition of Premises.** Tenant acknowledges that it has inspected the Premises and accepts the Premises in their \"as-is\" condition as of the Commencement Date, subject to Landlord\'s obligation to provide the Tenant Improvement Allowance as described in Article IX and Exhibit C. Landlord makes no representation or warranty, express or implied, regarding the condition of the Premises, the fitness of the Premises for any particular purpose, or the suitability of the Premises for Tenant\'s intended use, except as expressly set forth herein.

**[ARTICLE III --- TERM]{.underline}**

**Section 3.1 --- Lease Date.** The Lease Date is March 1, 2019. This Lease shall be effective and binding upon both parties as of the Lease Date.

**Section 3.2 --- Commencement Date.** The Commencement Date shall be June 1, 2019. The Lease Term and Tenant\'s obligation to pay Base Rent shall commence on the Commencement Date.

**Section 3.3 --- Expiration Date.** The Expiration Date shall be May 31, 2029, unless sooner terminated or extended pursuant to the terms of this Lease.

**Section 3.4 --- Original Lease Term.** The original Lease Term shall consist of ten (10) Lease Years, commencing on the Commencement Date and ending on the Expiration Date.

**Section 3.5 --- Pre-Commencement Period.** During the period from the Lease Date through the day immediately preceding the Commencement Date (the \"Pre-Commencement Period\"), Tenant shall have access to the Premises for the purpose of performing tenant improvement work in accordance with Article IX and Exhibit C. No Base Rent shall be due or payable during the Pre-Commencement Period. During the Pre-Commencement Period, Tenant shall comply with all insurance requirements set forth in Article XI and shall indemnify Landlord in accordance with Article XVI.

**Section 3.6 --- Renewal Options.** Tenant\'s renewal options are set forth in Article XII of this Lease.

**[ARTICLE IV --- BASE RENT]{.underline}**

**Section 4.1 --- Payment of Base Rent.** Tenant shall pay Base Rent to Landlord monthly in advance, due and payable on the first (1st) day of each calendar month during the Lease Term, without demand, notice, deduction, offset, or abatement of any kind, except as expressly provided in this Lease.

**Section 4.2 --- Initial Base Rent.** Base Rent for the initial Lease Year (Lease Year 1: June 1, 2019 through May 31, 2020) shall be Five Dollars and Fifty Cents (\$5.50) per RSF per annum, resulting in an annual Base Rent of Four Hundred Eighty-One Thousand Two Hundred Fifty Dollars (\$481,250.00) and a monthly Base Rent of Forty Thousand One Hundred Four Dollars and Seventeen Cents (\$40,104.17).

**Section 4.3 --- Annual Escalation.** Base Rent shall escalate annually at a rate of three percent (3%) per annum, compounded annually. Base Rent for each Lease Year shall be calculated by multiplying the Base Rent per RSF for the immediately preceding Lease Year by 1.03, rounded to the nearest one-thousandth of a dollar. The resulting per RSF rate shall be multiplied by 87,500 RSF to determine the annual Base Rent, and divided by twelve (12) to determine the monthly Base Rent. The complete Rent Schedule setting forth the Base Rent for each Lease Year is attached hereto as Exhibit B and incorporated herein by reference.

**Section 4.4 --- Prorations.** If the Commencement Date or Expiration Date falls on a day other than the first or last day of a calendar month, respectively, Base Rent for such partial month shall be prorated on a per diem basis calculated by dividing the applicable monthly Base Rent by the number of days in such calendar month and multiplying by the number of days of the Lease Term occurring in such month.

**Section 4.5 --- Late Fees.** If any installment of Base Rent or any other amount due under this Lease is not received by Landlord within five (5) business days after the date on which such payment is due, Tenant shall pay to Landlord a late fee equal to five percent (5%) of the overdue amount. Such late fee shall be in addition to, and not in lieu of, any other remedy available to Landlord under this Lease or at law.

**Section 4.6 --- Interest on Past-Due Amounts.** Any amount owed by Tenant under this Lease that is not paid when due shall bear interest from the date due until the date paid at a rate of one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month, or the maximum rate permitted by applicable law, whichever is less.

**Section 4.7 --- Payment Address.** All payments of Base Rent and other amounts due under this Lease shall be made to Landlord at: Thornfield Realty Holdings LP, 500 South Tryon Street, Suite 2200, Charlotte, North Carolina 28202, Attention: Accounts Receivable, or at such other address or by such other method as Landlord may designate by written notice to Tenant from time to time.

**[ARTICLE V --- TRIPLE NET LEASE; OPERATING EXPENSES]{.underline}**

**Section 5.1 --- Triple Net Lease.** This Lease is a triple net lease (\"NNN\"). In addition to the Base Rent specified in Article IV, Tenant shall be responsible for the payment of all Operating Expenses attributable to the Premises, including Tenant\'s Pro Rata Share of Property-wide Operating Expenses, all as more particularly set forth in this Article V.

**Section 5.2 --- Operating Expenses Defined.** Operating Expenses include, without limitation: (a) all real estate taxes, assessments, and governmental charges levied against the Property; (b) property insurance premiums for the Property; (c) common area maintenance charges, including repairs, cleaning, lighting, and general upkeep of Common Areas; (d) management fees payable to Landlord or its property manager, not to exceed five percent (5%) of gross rental revenues collected from the Property; (e) utility costs for Common Areas, including electricity, water, sewer, and gas; (f) landscaping and grounds maintenance; (g) snow and ice removal; (h) security services for the Property; and (i) reasonable reserves for capital expenditures relating to the Common Areas and building systems, as determined by Landlord in its reasonable discretion.

**Section 5.3 --- No Cap on Operating Expenses.** Tenant\'s obligation to pay its Pro Rata Share of Operating Expenses is not subject to any annual cap, ceiling, or limitation on year-over-year increases. Tenant acknowledges and agrees that Operating Expenses may increase from year to year without limitation, and Tenant shall be responsible for its Pro Rata Share of all such increases.

**Section 5.4 --- Estimated Monthly Payments.** Prior to the commencement of each calendar year (or partial calendar year), Landlord shall deliver to Tenant a written estimate of Tenant\'s Pro Rata Share of Operating Expenses for such year. Tenant shall pay one-twelfth (1/12) of the estimated annual amount on a monthly basis, concurrently with its payment of Base Rent.

**Section 5.5 --- Annual Reconciliation.** Within one hundred twenty (120) days after the end of each calendar year, Landlord shall deliver to Tenant a written reconciliation statement setting forth the actual Operating Expenses for such year and Tenant\'s Pro Rata Share thereof. If Tenant\'s estimated payments exceeded Tenant\'s actual Pro Rata Share, Landlord shall credit the overpayment against Tenant\'s next monthly payment(s). If Tenant\'s estimated payments were less than Tenant\'s actual Pro Rata Share, Tenant shall pay the deficiency within thirty (30) days after receipt of the reconciliation statement.

**Section 5.6 --- Audit Right.** Tenant shall have the right, at Tenant\'s sole cost and expense, to audit Landlord\'s books and records relating to Operating Expenses once per calendar year, upon not less than thirty (30) days\' prior written notice to Landlord. Such audit shall be conducted during normal business hours at Landlord\'s office and shall be completed within sixty (60) days of commencement. If the audit reveals that Landlord has overcharged Tenant by more than five percent (5%) for any calendar year, Landlord shall reimburse Tenant for the reasonable cost of the audit.

**[ARTICLE VI --- PERMITTED USE AND EXCLUSIVE USE]{.underline}**

**Section 6.1 --- Permitted Use.** Tenant shall use and occupy the Premises solely for the Permitted Use: third-party logistics, fulfillment, distribution, and warehouse operations, together with ancillary office use incidental thereto, and for no other purpose without the prior written consent of Landlord.

**Section 6.2 --- Exclusive Use Covenant.** Landlord covenants and agrees that, during the Lease Term and any Renewal Term, Landlord shall not lease, permit, or suffer any space in Buildings A, B, or C of the Thornfield Distribution Center to be used for fulfillment, logistics, distribution, or warehousing operations by any party other than Tenant. This exclusive use right extends to all three buildings (A, B, and C) of the Property and shall be binding upon Landlord, its successors, and assigns.

**Section 6.3 --- Compliance with Laws.** Tenant shall, at its sole cost and expense, comply with all applicable federal, state, and local laws, ordinances, rules, regulations, codes, and orders in connection with its use and occupancy of the Premises, including without limitation all environmental, health, safety, and zoning laws and regulations.

**Section 6.4 --- Prohibited Uses.** Tenant shall not use or permit the use of the Premises for any purpose that would: (a) increase the rate of insurance premiums applicable to the Building or the Property beyond the rate applicable to the Permitted Use; (b) violate any certificate of occupancy, zoning restriction, or other governmental requirement applicable to the Property; or (c) create a nuisance or unreasonable disturbance to other occupants of the Property or adjacent properties.

**[ARTICLE VII --- ASSIGNMENT AND SUBLETTING]{.underline}**

**Section 7.1 --- Restriction on Transfer.** Tenant shall not assign, transfer, mortgage, pledge, or encumber this Lease, or sublet all or any portion of the Premises, or permit the use or occupancy of the Premises by any party other than Tenant, without the prior written consent of Landlord. Landlord\'s consent shall not be unreasonably withheld.

**Section 7.2 --- Affiliate Transfers.** Notwithstanding Section 7.1, Tenant may, without Landlord\'s prior consent, assign this Lease or sublet all or any portion of the Premises to an Affiliate. For purposes of this Lease, \"Affiliate\" means any entity that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with Tenant, where \"control\" means ownership of fifty percent (50%) or more of the voting interests of the subject entity. Tenant shall deliver written notice of any such Affiliate transfer to Landlord within ten (10) business days after the effective date of such assignment or sublease, and the assignee or subtenant shall expressly assume in writing all of Tenant\'s obligations under this Lease.

**Section 7.3 --- No Release of Tenant.** In the event of any permitted assignment, whether to an Affiliate or with Landlord\'s consent, Tenant shall not be released from its obligations under this Lease unless Landlord expressly agrees in writing to such release. Tenant shall remain jointly and severally liable with the assignee for the full and faithful performance of all terms, covenants, and conditions of this Lease.

**Section 7.4 --- Documentation.** No assignment or subletting shall be effective until Tenant has delivered to Landlord a fully executed copy of the assignment or sublease agreement, together with the assignee\'s or subtenant\'s written assumption of Tenant\'s obligations hereunder and evidence of insurance coverage as required under Article XI.

**[ARTICLE VIII --- SUBORDINATION]{.underline}**

**Section 8.1 --- Subordination to Mortgages.** This Lease shall be subject and subordinate to all mortgages, deeds of trust, ground leases, and other security instruments now or hereafter placed upon the Property, the Building, or any part thereof, and to all renewals, modifications, consolidations, replacements, and extensions thereof (collectively, \"Superior Instruments\"). Tenant\'s subordination under this Section shall be self-operative and no further instrument or act shall be required to effectuate such subordination. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Tenant shall, within ten (10) business days after Landlord\'s written request, execute and deliver any instrument, certificate, or document that Landlord, any mortgagee, any beneficiary under a deed of trust, or any prospective lender may reasonably request to confirm or evidence the subordination of this Lease to any such Superior Instrument.

**Section 8.2 --- Mortgagee Election of Superiority.** Any mortgagee or beneficiary under any Superior Instrument may, at its sole election, make this Lease superior to the lien of its mortgage or deed of trust by giving written notice thereof to Tenant, and this Lease shall thereupon be deemed superior to such mortgage or deed of trust without the need for any further instrument.

**Section 8.3 --- Attornment Upon Foreclosure.** In the event of a foreclosure, deed in lieu of foreclosure, trustee\'s sale, or other transfer of the Property or Building by reason of the exercise of any remedy under any Superior Instrument, Tenant shall, if requested to do so by the purchaser, transferee, or new owner (the \"Successor Owner\"), attorn to and recognize the Successor Owner as Landlord under this Lease for the then-remaining balance of the Lease Term and any Renewal Term, upon the same terms and conditions as set forth in this Lease. Tenant shall, within ten (10) business days after request by any Successor Owner, execute and deliver any instrument reasonably requested to evidence such attornment.

**Section 8.4 --- Failure to Execute.** Tenant\'s failure to execute and deliver any subordination confirmation, attornment agreement, or other instrument requested under this Article VIII within the required time period shall constitute a default under this Lease and shall entitle Landlord to exercise all remedies available under Article XV.

**[ARTICLE IX --- TENANT IMPROVEMENTS]{.underline}**

**Section 9.1 --- Tenant Improvement Allowance.** Landlord shall provide Tenant with a Tenant Improvement Allowance of Fifteen Dollars (\$15.00) per RSF of the Premises, for a total Tenant Improvement Allowance of One Million Three Hundred Twelve Thousand Five Hundred Dollars (\$1,312,500.00) (87,500 RSF × \$15.00/RSF). The TI Allowance shall be disbursed in accordance with the Tenant Improvement Work Letter attached hereto as Exhibit C and incorporated herein by reference.

**Section 9.2 --- Excess Costs.** Tenant shall be solely responsible for all costs of tenant improvements in excess of the TI Allowance. In no event shall Landlord be obligated to disburse any amount in excess of the TI Allowance.

**Section 9.3 --- TI Recapture.** In the event of a Tenant default under this Lease occurring prior to the expiration of Lease Year 5 (i.e., prior to May 31, 2024), Tenant shall reimburse Landlord for the unamortized portion of the TI Allowance. The TI Allowance shall be amortized on a straight-line basis over the initial ten (10) year Lease Term at a rate of One Hundred Thirty-One Thousand Two Hundred Fifty Dollars (\$131,250.00) per Lease Year (\$1,312,500.00 divided by 10). The unamortized balance at any point during the first five (5) Lease Years shall be calculated as follows: \$1,312,500.00 minus (\$131,250.00 multiplied by the number of full Lease Years elapsed as of the date of default). The recapture obligation set forth in this Section 9.3 shall terminate automatically at the end of Lease Year 5 and shall have no further force or effect thereafter.

**Section 9.4 --- Ownership of Improvements.** All tenant improvements constructed within the Premises, whether funded by the TI Allowance or at Tenant\'s sole expense, shall become the property of Landlord upon installation and shall not be removed by Tenant at the expiration or earlier termination of this Lease, unless Landlord directs Tenant to remove the same, in which case Tenant shall remove such improvements and restore the Premises to their original condition at Tenant\'s sole cost.

**Section 9.5 --- No Representations.** Except as expressly set forth in this Article IX and Exhibit C, Landlord makes no representations or warranties regarding the condition, fitness, or suitability of the Premises.

**[ARTICLE X --- MAINTENANCE AND REPAIRS]{.underline}**

**Section 10.1 --- Tenant Obligations.** Tenant shall, at its sole cost and expense, keep and maintain the interior of the Premises in good condition, order, and repair throughout the Lease Term, including without limitation all HVAC systems serving the Premises, loading docks and dock equipment within the Premises, interior walls, flooring, plumbing fixtures, electrical systems, lighting, and all equipment and systems necessary for Tenant\'s operations.

**Section 10.2 --- Landlord Obligations.** Landlord shall be responsible for structural repairs and maintenance to Building C, including the roof, foundation, exterior load-bearing walls, and building envelope. Landlord shall also be responsible for capital replacements of building systems, including HVAC units, roof membrane replacement, and similar capital items; provided, however, that the costs of such capital replacements shall be amortized over their useful life in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles and included in Operating Expenses as provided in Article V.

**Section 10.3 --- Notice of Repairs.** Tenant shall promptly notify Landlord in writing of any needed structural repairs or any condition that may give rise to Landlord\'s maintenance obligations under Section 10.2.

**[ARTICLE XI --- INSURANCE]{.underline}**

**Section 11.1 --- Tenant\'s Insurance.** Tenant shall procure and maintain throughout the Lease Term the following insurance coverage: (a) commercial general liability insurance with limits of not less than One Million Dollars (\$1,000,000) per occurrence and Three Million Dollars (\$3,000,000) in the aggregate; (b) property insurance covering Tenant\'s personal property, inventory, trade fixtures, and tenant improvements in an amount sufficient to cover the full replacement cost thereof; (c) workers\' compensation insurance as required by the laws of the State of North Carolina; and (d) business automobile liability insurance with a combined single limit of not less than One Million Dollars (\$1,000,000) per accident.

**Section 11.2 --- Additional Insured.** Landlord, Thornfield Management Corp., and their respective officers, directors, employees, and agents shall be named as additional insureds on Tenant\'s commercial general liability policy.

**Section 11.3 --- Certificates.** Tenant shall deliver to Landlord certificates of insurance evidencing all required coverage prior to the Commencement Date and annually thereafter, and upon each renewal or replacement of any policy.

**Section 11.4 --- Waiver of Subrogation.** Landlord and Tenant each hereby waive any and all rights of recovery against the other party, and against the officers, directors, employees, agents, and representatives of the other party, for loss or damage to the waiving party\'s property to the extent that such loss or damage is covered by (or would have been covered by, had the required insurance been maintained) any property insurance policy required under this Lease. Each party shall cause its insurance carrier to endorse all applicable policies to permit such waiver.

**Section 11.5 --- Landlord\'s Insurance.** Landlord shall maintain property insurance on the Building (shell and structure) and commercial general liability insurance for Common Areas in amounts customary for comparable properties in the Charlotte, North Carolina metropolitan area. Premiums for such insurance shall be included in Operating Expenses and passed through to Tenant as part of Tenant\'s NNN obligations under Article V.

**[ARTICLE XII --- RENEWAL OPTIONS]{.underline}**

**Section 12.1 --- Grant of Renewal Options.** Subject to the terms and conditions of this Article XII, Tenant shall have two (2) consecutive options to renew this Lease (each, a \"Renewal Option\"), each for an additional period of five (5) years (each, a \"Renewal Term\"). The first Renewal Term, if exercised, shall commence on June 1, 2029 and expire on May 31, 2034. The second Renewal Term, if exercised, shall commence on June 1, 2034 and expire on May 31, 2039.

**Section 12.2 --- Renewal Rent.** Base Rent during each Renewal Term shall be ninety-five percent (95%) of the then-prevailing fair market rent for comparable warehouse and distribution space in the Charlotte, North Carolina metropolitan area (the \"Fair Market Rent\"), as determined in accordance with Section 12.4. All other terms and conditions of this Lease shall remain in effect during each Renewal Term, except as otherwise modified by this Article XII.

**Section 12.3 --- Exercise of Renewal Options.** Tenant shall exercise each Renewal Option by delivering to Landlord written notice of Tenant\'s intent to renew (the \"Renewal Notice\") not less than twelve (12) months prior to the then-current Expiration Date. For the first Renewal Option, the Renewal Notice must be delivered no later than May 31, 2028. For the second Renewal Option, the Renewal Notice must be delivered no later than May 31, 2033. Time is of the essence with respect to the delivery of each Renewal Notice. Failure to timely deliver the Renewal Notice shall result in the irrevocable lapse of the applicable Renewal Option and all subsequent Renewal Options.

**Section 12.4 --- Fair Market Rent Determination.** Within thirty (30) days after Landlord\'s receipt of a Renewal Notice, Landlord and Tenant shall endeavor in good faith to agree upon the Fair Market Rent for the applicable Renewal Term. If Landlord and Tenant are unable to agree upon the Fair Market Rent within such thirty (30) day period, the Fair Market Rent shall be determined as follows: (a) within fifteen (15) days after the expiration of such thirty (30) day period, each party shall appoint a qualified commercial real estate appraiser with at least ten (10) years of experience in the Charlotte, North Carolina industrial real estate market; (b) the two appraisers so appointed shall, within fifteen (15) days after their appointment, select a third qualified appraiser meeting the same qualifications; (c) each of the three appraisers shall independently determine the Fair Market Rent and submit a written report within thirty (30) days of the third appraiser\'s appointment; and (d) the Fair Market Rent shall be the average of the two appraisals that are closest in value. The cost of the third appraiser shall be shared equally by Landlord and Tenant; each party shall bear the cost of its own appointed appraiser.

**Section 12.5 --- Personal to Tenant.** The Renewal Options are personal to Apex Fulfillment Services Inc. and may not be exercised by, or assigned to, any assignee, subtenant, or other transferee.

**Section 12.6 --- Conditions to Exercise.** Each Renewal Option may be exercised only if, at the time of exercise and at the commencement of the applicable Renewal Term: (a) Tenant is not in default under any provision of this Lease beyond any applicable cure period; and (b) Tenant is in occupancy of the Premises.

**[ARTICLE XIII --- RIGHT OF FIRST REFUSAL TO PURCHASE]{.underline}**

**Section 13.1 --- Grant of Right of First Refusal.** Landlord hereby grants to Tenant a right of first refusal (the \"ROFR\") to purchase Building C (or, if Building C is included in a larger transaction, to purchase Building C on the terms allocable thereto) on the terms and conditions set forth in this Article XIII.

**Section 13.2 --- Triggering Event.** If, at any time during the Lease Term or any Renewal Term, Landlord receives a bona fide written offer from a third party (a \"Third-Party Offer\") to purchase Building C, whether individually, as part of a sale of the entire Property, or as part of a multi-property or portfolio transaction in which Building C is included, Landlord shall, prior to accepting or executing any agreement with such third party, promptly deliver to Tenant a written notice (the \"ROFR Notice\") containing the material terms and conditions of the Third-Party Offer. The ROFR Notice shall include, at a minimum, the following: (a) the identity of the proposed purchaser; (b) the proposed purchase price (or, in the case of a portfolio transaction, the allocable purchase price for Building C, as reasonably determined by Landlord); (c) the proposed closing date; (d) all material contingencies, conditions, and other terms of the Third-Party Offer; and (e) a complete copy of the Third-Party Offer or the relevant portions thereof relating to Building C.

**Section 13.3 --- Portfolio Transactions.** In the event that the Third-Party Offer involves the acquisition of Building C as part of a portfolio or multi-property transaction, the ROFR shall apply to Building C\'s allocable share of the overall purchase price. The allocable purchase price for Building C shall be determined by Landlord in good faith, taking into account the relative value, size, condition, and income-generating capacity of Building C as compared to the other properties included in the transaction. Tenant shall have the right to dispute Landlord\'s allocation by written notice delivered within the Exercise Period (as defined in Section 13.4), and any such dispute shall be resolved by a mutually agreed-upon independent MAI appraiser, whose determination shall be final and binding.

**Section 13.4 --- Exercise Period.** Tenant shall have thirty (30) days from receipt of the ROFR Notice (the \"Exercise Period\") within which to deliver written notice to Landlord of Tenant\'s irrevocable election to purchase Building C on the same terms and conditions as the Third-Party Offer (or, in the case of a portfolio transaction, on the allocable terms for Building C as set forth in the ROFR Notice, subject to Section 13.3). If Tenant does not deliver written notice of its election to exercise the ROFR within the Exercise Period, the ROFR shall be deemed waived with respect to such Third-Party Offer, and Landlord shall be free to consummate the sale of Building C to the third party on terms no more favorable to the third party than those set forth in the ROFR Notice.

**Section 13.5 --- Closing.** If Tenant timely exercises its ROFR, the parties shall proceed to close the purchase of Building C on the terms stated in the Third-Party Offer (or the allocable terms for Building C, as applicable), with closing to occur no later than sixty (60) days after the date of Tenant\'s exercise notice, unless a later closing date is specified in the Third-Party Offer.

**Section 13.6 --- Reinstatement of ROFR.** If Tenant does not exercise its ROFR with respect to a particular Third-Party Offer and Landlord does not close the sale with the third party within one hundred eighty (180) days after the expiration of the Exercise Period, or if the material terms of the Third-Party Offer are modified in any manner that is more favorable to the third party than the terms set forth in the ROFR Notice, then the ROFR shall be automatically reinstated and Landlord shall be required to deliver a new ROFR Notice to Tenant before proceeding with any sale.

**Section 13.7 --- Personal to Tenant.** The ROFR is personal to Apex Fulfillment Services Inc. and shall not be transferred to, or exercised by, any assignee, subtenant, or other transferee.

**Section 13.8 --- Memorandum of ROFR.** At Tenant\'s request, Landlord shall execute and deliver a memorandum of this ROFR in recordable form for filing in the Mecklenburg County Register of Deeds, at Tenant\'s sole cost and expense.

**[ARTICLE XIV --- HOLDOVER]{.underline}**

**Section 14.1 --- Holdover Tenancy.** If Tenant remains in possession of the Premises after the Expiration Date or earlier termination of this Lease without Landlord\'s prior written consent, Tenant shall be deemed a holdover tenant on a month-to-month basis, subject to all of the terms and conditions of this Lease, except that Base Rent during such holdover period shall be equal to one hundred fifty percent (150%) of the Base Rent in effect during the final month of the Lease Term (or Renewal Term, as applicable).

**Section 14.2 --- Landlord\'s Rights.** Landlord\'s acceptance of holdover rent shall not constitute consent to any holdover tenancy, a renewal of this Lease, or a waiver of Landlord\'s right to terminate Tenant\'s occupancy upon thirty (30) days\' prior written notice. Landlord shall retain all rights and remedies available at law or in equity, including the right to recover damages resulting from Tenant\'s holdover.

**[ARTICLE XV --- DEFAULT AND REMEDIES]{.underline}**

**Section 15.1 --- Events of Default.** Each of the following shall constitute an Event of Default under this Lease:

> \(a\) Tenant\'s failure to pay Base Rent or any other monetary obligation under this Lease within five (5) business days after written notice from Landlord that such amount is past due;
>
> \(b\) Tenant\'s failure to perform or comply with any non-monetary obligation under this Lease within thirty (30) days after written notice from Landlord specifying the nature of such failure; provided, however, that if such failure is of a nature that cannot reasonably be cured within thirty (30) days, Tenant shall not be in default if Tenant commences the cure within such thirty (30) day period and diligently prosecutes the cure to completion within a reasonable time not to exceed ninety (90) days;
>
> \(c\) The filing of a petition by or against Tenant under any chapter of the United States Bankruptcy Code, or Tenant\'s making of a general assignment for the benefit of creditors, or the appointment of a receiver or trustee for all or substantially all of Tenant\'s assets or the Premises, or Tenant\'s admission in writing of its inability to pay its debts as they become due;
>
> \(d\) Tenant\'s abandonment of the Premises for a period of thirty (30) or more consecutive days while in default of any monetary obligation hereunder.

**Section 15.2 --- Landlord\'s Remedies.** Upon the occurrence of an Event of Default, Landlord shall have the following remedies, which shall be cumulative and not exclusive:

> \(a\) Terminate this Lease by written notice to Tenant, re-enter and recover possession of the Premises, and recover from Tenant all damages, including unpaid rent accrued through the date of termination, the present value (discounted at a rate of six percent (6%) per annum) of the excess of Base Rent and other charges for the balance of the Lease Term over the fair market rental value of the Premises for such period, the unamortized TI Allowance if the default occurs prior to the end of Lease Year 5 as provided in Article IX, and all costs and expenses incurred by Landlord in connection with such default, including reasonable attorneys\' fees and brokerage commissions incurred in reletting;
>
> \(b\) Terminate Tenant\'s right to possession of the Premises without terminating this Lease, re-enter and relet the Premises for the account of Tenant, and recover from Tenant the difference between the rent due hereunder and the net rent actually received from reletting, after deducting all costs of reletting; or
>
> \(c\) Pursue any other remedy available to Landlord at law or in equity.

**Section 15.3 --- Mitigation.** Landlord shall use commercially reasonable efforts to mitigate its damages in the event of a Tenant default, including reasonable efforts to relet the Premises.

**Section 15.4 --- Attorneys\' Fees.** In any action or proceeding arising out of or related to this Lease, the prevailing party shall be entitled to recover its reasonable attorneys\' fees, court costs, and other expenses of litigation from the non-prevailing party.

**[ARTICLE XVI --- INDEMNIFICATION AND WAIVER]{.underline}**

**Section 16.1 --- Tenant\'s Indemnification.** Tenant shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Landlord and its partners, officers, directors, employees, agents, and representatives from and against any and all claims, demands, liabilities, losses, damages, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys\' fees) arising out of or in connection with Tenant\'s use and occupancy of the Premises, or any act, omission, or negligence of Tenant or its employees, agents, contractors, or invitees, except to the extent caused by Landlord\'s negligence or willful misconduct.

**Section 16.2 --- Landlord\'s Indemnification.** Landlord shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Tenant and its officers, directors, employees, agents, and representatives from and against any and all claims, demands, liabilities, losses, damages, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys\' fees) arising out of or in connection with Landlord\'s negligence or willful misconduct in the maintenance, repair, or operation of the Common Areas and structural elements of Building C.

**Section 16.3 --- Waiver of Consequential Damages.** In no event shall either party be liable to the other for any indirect, special, incidental, or consequential damages arising out of or related to this Lease, regardless of the form of action and whether or not such damages were foreseeable.

**[ARTICLE XVII --- ESTOPPEL CERTIFICATES]{.underline}**

**Section 17.1 --- Obligation to Deliver.** Tenant shall, within ten (10) business days after receipt of a written request from Landlord, execute and deliver to Landlord, any mortgagee, or any prospective purchaser an estoppel certificate in the form reasonably requested by Landlord, certifying: (a) that this Lease is in full force and effect and has not been modified (or, if modified, specifying the modifications); (b) the Commencement Date and Expiration Date; (c) the current Base Rent and any prepaid rent; (d) whether, to Tenant\'s knowledge, Landlord or Tenant is in default under this Lease and, if so, specifying the nature of such default; and (e) such other matters as Landlord, any mortgagee, or any prospective purchaser may reasonably request.

**Section 17.2 --- Deemed Acknowledgment.** Tenant\'s failure to execute and deliver an estoppel certificate within the ten (10) business day period specified above shall constitute Tenant\'s irrevocable acknowledgment that the statements set forth in Landlord\'s proposed form of estoppel certificate are true and correct.

**[ARTICLE XVIII --- NOTICES]{.underline}**

**Section 18.1 --- Method of Delivery.** All notices, demands, requests, consents, approvals, and other communications required or permitted under this Lease shall be in writing and shall be deemed duly given and received: (a) upon personal delivery; (b) on the next business day following deposit with a nationally recognized overnight courier service for next-business-day delivery; or (c) on the third (3rd) business day following deposit in the United States mail, certified mail, return receipt requested, postage prepaid.

**[ARTICLE XIX --- MISCELLANEOUS PROVISIONS]{.underline}**

**Section 19.1 --- Governing Law.** This Lease shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of North Carolina, without regard to its conflict of laws principles.

**Section 19.2 --- Entire Agreement.** This Lease, including all Exhibits attached hereto, constitutes the entire agreement between the parties with respect to the subject matter hereof and supersedes all prior negotiations, representations, warranties, commitments, offers, and agreements, whether oral or written, relating to the leasing of the Premises.

**Section 19.3 --- Amendments.** This Lease may not be amended, modified, or supplemented except by an instrument in writing executed by both Landlord and Tenant.

**Section 19.4 --- Severability.** If any provision of this Lease is held to be invalid, illegal, or unenforceable, the validity, legality, and enforceability of the remaining provisions shall not in any way be affected or impaired thereby, and such invalid provision shall be reformed to the minimum extent necessary to render it valid and enforceable.

**Section 19.5 --- Waiver.** The waiver by either party of any breach of any term, covenant, or condition of this Lease shall not be deemed a waiver of any subsequent breach of the same or any other term, covenant, or condition. No waiver shall be effective unless made in writing and signed by the waiving party.

**Section 19.6 --- Successors and Assigns.** Subject to the restrictions on assignment set forth in Article VII, this Lease shall be binding upon and inure to the benefit of the parties hereto and their respective heirs, executors, administrators, successors, and assigns.

**Section 19.7 --- Recording.** Tenant shall not record this Lease or any memorandum hereof without the prior written consent of Landlord. Landlord agrees to cooperate with Tenant in the preparation and recording of a memorandum of lease, if requested by Tenant, at Tenant\'s sole cost and expense.

**Section 19.8 --- Force Majeure.** Neither party shall be in default for any delay or failure to perform any obligation under this Lease (other than Tenant\'s obligation to pay Base Rent and other monetary obligations) if such delay or failure results from causes beyond the reasonable control of such party, including without limitation acts of God, fire, flood, earthquake, hurricane, tornado, epidemic, pandemic, war, terrorism, riot, civil disturbance, government action or inaction, labor strikes, or material shortages. The affected party shall give prompt written notice to the other party of the occurrence and expected duration of any force majeure event.

**Section 19.9 --- Quiet Enjoyment.** Landlord covenants and agrees that, conditioned upon Tenant\'s payment of Base Rent and performance of all other obligations under this Lease, Tenant shall peaceably and quietly hold, occupy, and enjoy the Premises during the Lease Term and any Renewal Term, free from interference by Landlord or any person claiming by, through, or under Landlord, subject to the terms and conditions of this Lease and any matters to which this Lease is subordinate pursuant to Article VIII.

**Section 19.10 --- Broker Disclosure.** Landlord and Tenant acknowledge that Ridgeview Realty Brokers Inc. acted as listing broker in connection with this Lease. Tenant represents and warrants to Landlord that Tenant has not dealt with any other broker, finder, or agent in connection with this Lease. Landlord shall pay any commission owed to Ridgeview Realty Brokers Inc. pursuant to a separate commission agreement between Landlord and such broker. Each party shall indemnify the other against any claims for brokerage commissions or finder\'s fees arising from such party\'s breach of its representations in this Section.

**Section 19.11 --- Counterparts and Electronic Signatures.** This Lease may be executed in any number of counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original and all of which together shall constitute one and the same instrument. Signatures transmitted by electronic means (including PDF, DocuSign, or similar platforms) shall be treated as original signatures for all purposes.

**Section 19.12 --- Confidentiality.** The terms and conditions of this Lease are confidential. Neither party shall disclose the terms of this Lease to any third party without the prior written consent of the other party, except: (a) to the extent required by applicable law, regulation, or court order; (b) to such party\'s attorneys, accountants, financial advisors, lenders, and prospective purchasers or investors, who shall be bound by obligations of confidentiality; or (c) in connection with the enforcement of such party\'s rights under this Lease.

**[ARTICLE XX --- PARKING]{.underline}**

**Section 20.1 --- Parking Rights.** Tenant shall have the non-exclusive right to use the parking areas serving Building C as depicted on the Site Plan attached hereto as Exhibit A.

**Section 20.2 --- Minimum Parking Allocation.** Landlord shall maintain a minimum of fifty (50) surface parking spaces adjacent to Building C for the use of Tenant and its employees, contractors, visitors, and invitees, including designated spaces for tractor-trailer staging and loading operations.

**Section 20.3 --- No Charge.** No additional charge shall be assessed for parking during the initial Lease Term. Parking charges during any Renewal Term shall be at the then-prevailing rates, if any, established by Landlord.

**[ARTICLE 2 --- PREMISES]{.underline}**

**Section 2.1 --- Demise of Premises**

Landlord hereby leases to Tenant, and Tenant hereby leases from Landlord, the Premises described as Suite 200, located on the second (2nd) floor of Millbrook Medical Plaza, 1585 Millbrook Road, Raleigh, NC 27609, consisting of approximately 3,200 rentable square feet (RSF), as more particularly shown on the floor plan attached hereto as Exhibit A and incorporated herein by reference. The Premises shall include access to and the non-exclusive right to use the Common Areas in common with other tenants and occupants of the Building.

**Section 2.2 --- Measurement**

The RSF of the Premises has been determined in accordance with the Building Owners and Managers Association (BOMA) Standard Method of Measurement (ANSI/BOMA Z65.1-2017). Landlord and Tenant agree that the Premises contains 3,200 RSF and such measurement shall be conclusive and binding for all purposes under this Lease, including without limitation the calculation of Base Rent, the TI Allowance, and Tenant\'s proportionate share of Operating Expenses and Real Estate Taxes.

**Section 2.3 --- Condition of Premises**

Tenant accepts the Premises in its \"as-is\" condition as of the Lease Date, subject to the completion of Tenant Improvements pursuant to Article 8 of this Lease. Landlord makes no representations or warranties regarding the condition of the Premises, including without limitation the suitability of the Premises for Tenant\'s intended use, except as expressly set forth herein.

**[ARTICLE 3 --- TERM]{.underline}**

**Section 3.1 --- Lease Term**

The Lease Term shall commence on November 1, 2021 (the \"Commencement Date\") and shall expire on October 31, 2028 (the \"Expiration Date\"), for a total initial term of seven (7) Lease Years, unless sooner terminated or extended in accordance with the provisions of this Lease. Tenant\'s obligation to pay Rent shall commence on the Commencement Date.

**Section 3.2 --- Delivery of Possession**

Landlord shall deliver possession of the Premises to Tenant on the Commencement Date in the condition required by this Lease. If Landlord fails to deliver possession of the Premises to Tenant by the Commencement Date for any reason, Rent shall abate on a per diem basis until possession is delivered to Tenant, but the Expiration Date shall not be extended by reason of such delay. Landlord shall not be liable to Tenant for any damages resulting from any delay in delivery of possession.

**[ARTICLE 4 --- RENT]{.underline}**

Tenant shall pay Base Rent to Landlord in monthly installments, in advance, on the first day of each calendar month during the Lease Term, without notice, demand, deduction, or setoff. If the Commencement Date falls on a day other than the first day of a calendar month, Base Rent for the first partial month shall be prorated on a per diem basis. All Rent payments shall be made payable to Landlord and delivered to such address or account as Landlord may designate from time to time in writing.
