**Section 4.2 --- Additional Rent / Operating Expense Escalations**

This Lease is a Modified Gross Lease. Landlord shall pay all Operating Expenses and Real Estate Taxes attributable to the Building during the Base Year (calendar year 2022). Beginning in calendar year 2023 and continuing each calendar year thereafter during the Lease Term, Tenant shall pay, as Additional Rent, Tenant\'s proportionate share of the amount by which actual Operating Expenses and Real Estate Taxes for such calendar year exceed the actual Operating Expenses and Real Estate Taxes incurred during the Base Year.

Tenant\'s proportionate share shall be calculated as a fraction, the numerator of which is the RSF of the Premises (3,200 RSF) and the denominator of which is the total RSF of the Building. Landlord shall provide Tenant with a written estimate of Tenant\'s proportionate share of the anticipated escalation for each calendar year, and Tenant shall pay one-twelfth (1/12) of such estimated amount monthly, in advance, together with each installment of Base Rent.

Within one hundred twenty (120) days following the end of each calendar year, Landlord shall provide Tenant with a detailed annual statement of actual Operating Expenses and Real Estate Taxes for such calendar year. If the actual amount due from Tenant exceeds the total estimated payments made by Tenant during such calendar year, Tenant shall pay the deficiency within thirty (30) days of receipt of such statement. If the estimated payments exceed the actual amount due, Landlord shall credit such overpayment against the next installments of Additional Rent due, or if the Lease Term has expired, refund such overpayment within thirty (30) days.

Tenant shall have the right, at Tenant\'s sole cost and expense, to audit Landlord\'s books and records relating to Operating Expenses and Real Estate Taxes upon thirty (30) days\' prior written notice, during normal business hours, at Landlord\'s office. Such audit right must be exercised, if at all, within twelve (12) months following Tenant\'s receipt of the annual statement for the applicable calendar year.

**Section 4.3 --- Late Charges and Interest**

If any payment of Rent or other sum due under this Lease is not received by Landlord within five (5) business days of the date on which such payment is due, Tenant shall pay to Landlord a late charge equal to five percent (5%) of the overdue amount. Such late charge is intended to compensate Landlord for the administrative costs associated with handling late payments and is not a penalty. In addition, any amount not paid within thirty (30) days of the date on which such payment is due shall bear interest at the lesser of (a) twelve percent (12%) per annum, or (b) the maximum rate permitted by applicable law, from the due date until paid in full.

**Section 4.4 --- Holdover Rent**

If Tenant holds over after the Expiration Date or the earlier termination of this Lease without Landlord\'s prior written consent, Tenant shall pay holdover rent equal to one hundred fifty percent (150%) of the Base Rent in effect during the last month of the Lease Term, plus all Additional Rent, and such holdover tenancy shall be deemed a month-to-month tenancy subject to all other terms and conditions of this Lease. Landlord\'s acceptance of holdover rent shall not constitute consent to any holdover tenancy nor a waiver of Landlord\'s right to recover possession of the Premises or to pursue any other remedy available at law or in equity.

**[ARTICLE 5 --- USE]{.underline}**

**Section 5.1 --- Permitted Use**

Tenant shall use and occupy the Premises solely for the purpose of operating a medical and dental office (the \"Permitted Use\") and for no other purpose without Landlord\'s prior written consent, which consent may be granted or withheld in Landlord\'s sole discretion. Tenant shall comply with all applicable federal, state, and local laws, ordinances, rules, regulations, and orders governing the operation of a dental and medical practice at the Premises, including without limitation all licensing and permitting requirements of the State of North Carolina.

**Section 5.2 --- Hazardous Materials and Biohazardous Waste**

Tenant acknowledges that the operation of a dental practice involves the generation of biohazardous waste, dental amalgam waste, and other regulated materials. Tenant shall be solely responsible for the proper handling, storage, transportation, and disposal of all biohazardous materials, dental amalgam waste, sharps, pharmaceutical waste, and any other hazardous or regulated materials generated in connection with Tenant\'s use and occupancy of the Premises, in strict compliance with all applicable federal, state, and local environmental, health, and safety laws and regulations, including without limitation the Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (RCRA), the Occupational Safety and Health Act (OSHA), and the North Carolina Solid Waste Management Act.

Tenant shall not store or dispose of any hazardous or biohazardous materials in the Building\'s common waste systems, plumbing, or drainage facilities. Tenant shall maintain at all times within the Premises appropriate containers and equipment for the temporary storage of biohazardous and regulated waste and shall contract with a licensed waste disposal service for the regular removal of such materials from the Premises.

Landlord shall have the right, upon reasonable prior notice to Tenant (except in the case of an emergency, in which case no prior notice shall be required), to inspect the Premises to verify Tenant\'s compliance with this Section 5.2 and all applicable environmental and health laws. If Landlord determines that Tenant\'s use or disposal of hazardous or biohazardous materials has resulted in contamination of the Premises, the Building, or the surrounding property, Landlord may require Tenant to undertake remediation of any such condition at Tenant\'s sole cost and expense, in accordance with all applicable laws and to Landlord\'s reasonable satisfaction.

**[ARTICLE 6 --- UTILITIES AND SERVICES]{.underline}**

**Section 6.1 --- Building Services**

Landlord shall furnish the following services to the Premises during the Lease Term:

> \(a\) Heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (\"HVAC\") during normal business hours, which shall be Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., and Saturday, 8:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m., excluding Building holidays as designated by Landlord from time to time. After-hours HVAC service shall be available upon Tenant\'s written or electronic request submitted to the Property Manager, at a rate established by Landlord from time to time and communicated to Tenant in writing;
>
> \(b\) Water and sewer service to the Premises;
>
> \(c\) Elevator service during Building operating hours, and at least one elevator available at all times for after-hours access;
>
> \(d\) Electricity to the Premises sufficient for normal medical and dental office use, including standard lighting, computers, and dental equipment operating within standard electrical loads.

Tenant shall be responsible for all janitorial and cleaning services within the Premises, including the proper sanitization of treatment rooms and clinical areas in compliance with all applicable health and safety regulations. Landlord shall provide janitorial services for the Common Areas only.

**[ARTICLE 7 --- INSURANCE]{.underline}**

**Section 7.1 --- Tenant\'s Insurance**

Throughout the Lease Term, Tenant shall maintain, at Tenant\'s sole cost and expense, the following insurance coverage with insurers licensed to do business in the State of North Carolina and rated at least A-VII by A.M. Best:

> \(a\) **Commercial General Liability Insurance** with limits of not less than One Million Dollars (\$1,000,000) per occurrence and Three Million Dollars (\$3,000,000) in the aggregate, covering bodily injury, personal injury, and property damage arising from Tenant\'s use and occupancy of the Premises, including contractual liability coverage;
>
> \(b\) **Professional Liability Insurance** (dental malpractice insurance) with limits of not less than Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$500,000) per occurrence and One Million Dollars (\$1,000,000) in the aggregate;
>
> \(c\) **Workers\' Compensation Insurance** providing statutory benefits as required by the laws of the State of North Carolina, and Employer\'s Liability Insurance with limits of not less than Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$500,000) per accident;
>
> \(d\) **Business Personal Property Insurance** covering Tenant\'s furniture, fixtures, equipment, inventory, dental instruments, and other personal property located within the Premises for their full replacement cost, on a special form (all-risk) basis.

All policies required under subsections (a) and (d) above shall name Landlord, Thornfield Management Corp., and Landlord\'s designated Property Manager as additional insureds. Tenant shall deliver certificates of insurance evidencing the required coverages to Landlord prior to the Commencement Date and annually thereafter upon renewal. Each policy shall require the insurer to provide Landlord with at least thirty (30) days\' prior written notice of cancellation, non-renewal, or material change in coverage.

**Section 7.2 --- Landlord\'s Insurance**

Landlord shall maintain, at Landlord\'s cost (included in Operating Expenses), (a) property insurance for the Building and Common Areas providing fire and extended coverage (special form) in an amount not less than the full replacement cost of the Building, and (b) commercial general liability insurance for the Building and Common Areas with limits reasonably determined by Landlord. The cost of Landlord\'s insurance premiums shall be included in Operating Expenses for purposes of calculating Tenant\'s proportionate share of escalations.

**Section 7.3 --- Waiver of Subrogation**

Each Party hereby waives all rights of recovery against the other Party for any loss or damage to the extent covered by, or required to be covered by, such Party\'s insurance policies maintained pursuant to this Article 7. Each Party shall cause its respective insurer to issue a waiver of subrogation endorsement in favor of the other Party and its agents, employees, officers, and partners. This waiver shall be effective regardless of whether or not the applicable insurance policy contains a waiver of subrogation endorsement.

**[ARTICLE 8 --- TENANT IMPROVEMENTS]{.underline}**

**Section 8.1 --- Tenant Improvement Allowance**

Landlord shall provide Tenant with a Tenant Improvement Allowance (\"TI Allowance\") of Twelve Dollars (\$12.00) per RSF, for a total of Thirty-Eight Thousand Four Hundred Dollars (\$38,400.00), calculated as \$12.00 multiplied by 3,200 RSF. The TI Allowance shall be applied toward the cost of designing, permitting, and constructing Tenant\'s improvements to the Premises (the \"Tenant Improvements\") in accordance with plans and specifications approved by Landlord pursuant to Section 8.2.

Any costs of the Tenant Improvements in excess of the TI Allowance shall be Tenant\'s sole responsibility. Any unused portion of the TI Allowance shall not be refunded or credited against Rent, but shall be forfeited. The TI Allowance shall be deemed amortized on a straight-line basis over the seven (7) year Lease Term for purposes of any early termination recapture calculation as described in Article 20 (amortization of \$38,400.00 over 7 years = \$5,485.71 per year).

**Section 8.2 --- Construction and Approval**

Tenant shall submit detailed plans and specifications for the Tenant Improvements to Landlord for approval within thirty (30) days of the Lease Date. Landlord\'s approval shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed, and Landlord shall respond to Tenant\'s submission within fifteen (15) business days of receipt. All Tenant Improvements shall be performed by licensed contractors approved by Landlord (such approval not to be unreasonably withheld) and in compliance with all applicable building codes, regulations, and permit requirements.

All work shall be performed in a good and workmanlike manner and shall not interfere with the operations of other tenants of the Building. Tenant shall obtain all necessary governmental permits and approvals prior to commencing construction. Upon completion, all Tenant Improvements (other than Tenant\'s trade fixtures, dental equipment, and personal property) shall become the property of the Landlord and shall remain upon and be surrendered with the Premises at the expiration or earlier termination of the Lease.

**[ARTICLE 9 --- MAINTENANCE AND REPAIRS]{.underline}**

**Section 9.1 --- Landlord\'s Obligations**

Landlord shall maintain and repair the structural elements of the Building, including the roof, foundation, exterior walls, and load-bearing components, the Common Areas, and the Building\'s mechanical, electrical, plumbing, and HVAC systems serving the Premises and the Building generally, except to the extent damage thereto is caused by the negligence or willful misconduct of Tenant, its agents, employees, contractors, patients, or invitees. The cost of such maintenance and repair shall be included in Operating Expenses, subject to the exclusions set forth in the definition of Operating Expenses in Section 1.1.

**Section 9.2 --- Tenant\'s Obligations**

Tenant shall maintain the interior of the Premises in good order, condition, and repair throughout the Lease Term, including without limitation all non-structural repairs, interior painting, flooring, ceiling tiles, interior doors, light fixtures, plumbing fixtures within the Premises, and all of Tenant\'s fixtures, equipment, and personal property. Tenant shall keep the Premises in a clean, safe, and sanitary condition consistent with the operation of a medical and dental practice and in compliance with all applicable health and safety regulations.

**[ARTICLE 10 --- PARKING]{.underline}**

**Section 10.1 --- Parking Allocation**

Landlord shall provide Tenant with twelve (12) dedicated parking spaces in the parking garage adjacent to the Building, at no additional charge during the initial Lease Term. The parking ratio provided to Tenant is approximately 3.75 spaces per 1,000 RSF. Tenant\'s parking spaces shall be identified by signage or pavement markings designated by Landlord, and Landlord shall designate the specific location of such spaces. Tenant shall not use parking spaces in excess of the allocated twelve (12) spaces without Landlord\'s prior written consent. Tenant shall comply with all parking rules and regulations established by Landlord from time to time and shall ensure that Tenant\'s employees, patients, and invitees observe such rules.

**[ARTICLE 11 --- ASSIGNMENT AND SUBLETTING]{.underline}**

**Section 11.1 --- Restriction**

Tenant shall not assign this Lease or sublet all or any portion of the Premises, nor shall Tenant permit any other person or entity to occupy the Premises or any part thereof, without the prior written consent of Landlord, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed. Any purported assignment or subletting without Landlord\'s prior written consent shall be void and of no force or effect and shall constitute an Event of Default under this Lease.

**Section 11.2 --- Conditions to Consent**

In connection with any request for Landlord\'s consent to an assignment or subletting, Tenant shall provide Landlord with the following information at least thirty (30) days prior to the proposed effective date of the assignment or sublease:

> \(a\) The identity and financial statements (for the most recent three fiscal years) of the proposed assignee or subtenant;
>
> \(b\) The terms and conditions of the proposed assignment or sublease, including a complete copy of the proposed instrument;
>
> \(c\) Evidence satisfactory to Landlord that the proposed assignee or subtenant will use the Premises solely for the Permitted Use and is duly licensed and qualified to operate a medical or dental practice in the State of North Carolina.

Landlord may consider the creditworthiness of the proposed assignee or subtenant, the nature of the proposed use, the experience of the proposed assignee or subtenant in operating a medical or dental practice, and the impact of the proposed assignment or subletting on the Building and its other tenants. No assignment or subletting shall release Tenant from any of its obligations under this Lease unless Landlord expressly agrees to such release in writing. Tenant shall reimburse Landlord for all reasonable out-of-pocket costs and expenses (including attorneys\' fees) incurred in connection with reviewing any proposed assignment or sublease.

**[ARTICLE 12 --- SUBORDINATION AND ATTORNMENT]{.underline}**

**Section 12.1 --- Subordination**

This Lease is and shall be subordinate to any mortgage, deed of trust, or ground lease now or hereafter placed upon or encumbering the Building or any part thereof, and to all renewals, modifications, consolidations, replacements, and extensions thereof, provided that the holder of any such mortgage or deed of trust (the \"Mortgagee\") shall agree not to disturb Tenant\'s possession of the Premises so long as Tenant is not in default under this Lease beyond any applicable notice and cure period. Landlord shall use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain a subordination, non-disturbance, and attornment agreement (\"SNDA\") from any current or future Mortgagee, in a form reasonably acceptable to Tenant, within sixty (60) days of the Commencement Date (with respect to any existing mortgage or deed of trust) or within sixty (60) days of the recording of any future mortgage or deed of trust.

**Section 12.2 --- Attornment**

Upon the request of any Mortgagee or any successor to Landlord\'s interest in the Building, Tenant shall attorn to such party as landlord under this Lease for the balance of the Lease Term upon the same terms and conditions set forth herein, and Tenant shall execute such instruments as may be reasonably required to evidence such attornment.

**[ARTICLE 13 --- INDEMNIFICATION]{.underline}**

**Section 13.1 --- Tenant Indemnification**

Tenant shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Landlord and its partners, officers, directors, agents, employees, and the Property Manager from and against any and all claims, actions, liabilities, losses, damages, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys\' fees and court costs) arising from or in connection with (a) Tenant\'s use and occupancy of the Premises, (b) the conduct of Tenant\'s business or any activity, work, or thing done, permitted, or suffered by Tenant in or about the Premises, (c) any breach or default by Tenant in the performance of any obligation of Tenant under this Lease, or (d) any negligent or wrongful act or omission of Tenant, its agents, employees, contractors, patients, or invitees, except to the extent caused by the gross negligence or willful misconduct of Landlord.

**Section 13.2 --- Landlord Indemnification**

Landlord shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Tenant and its officers, agents, and employees from and against any and all claims, actions, liabilities, losses, damages, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys\' fees) arising from the negligent or wrongful acts or omissions of Landlord, its agents, or employees in connection with the ownership, operation, and maintenance of the Building and Common Areas, except to the extent caused by the negligence or willful misconduct of Tenant.

**[ARTICLE 14 --- DAMAGE AND DESTRUCTION]{.underline}**

If the Premises or the Building is damaged by fire or other casualty, Landlord shall, subject to the provisions of this Article, repair and restore the same with reasonable diligence. If Landlord reasonably estimates that repairs can be completed within one hundred eighty (180) days following the date of the casualty, Landlord shall proceed with such repairs, and this Lease shall remain in full force and effect. If Landlord reasonably estimates that repairs will require more than one hundred eighty (180) days, either Party may terminate this Lease upon thirty (30) days\' prior written notice to the other Party, given within sixty (60) days following the date of the casualty.

If the Building is damaged to the extent of fifty percent (50%) or more of its replacement cost, Landlord may, at its option, terminate this Lease upon sixty (60) days\' written notice to Tenant, regardless of the extent of damage to the Premises. Rent shall abate proportionately during any period in which the Premises or a material portion thereof is rendered untenantable as a result of such casualty. Landlord shall not be required to repair or restore Tenant\'s personal property, trade fixtures, or dental equipment.

**[ARTICLE 15 --- CONDEMNATION]{.underline}**

If all or a material portion of the Premises is taken by the exercise of the power of eminent domain or by conveyance in lieu thereof (a \"Taking\"), either Party may terminate this Lease by written notice to the other Party given within thirty (30) days following the date on which title vests in the condemning authority. If a partial Taking does not materially interfere with Tenant\'s ability to use the Premises for the Permitted Use, this Lease shall continue in full force and effect, and the Base Rent shall be equitably reduced in proportion to the area of the Premises taken.

Landlord shall be entitled to receive the entire condemnation award or payment made in connection with any Taking, except that Tenant shall have the right to file a separate claim (to the extent permitted by law) for compensation for the loss of Tenant\'s personal property, trade fixtures, dental equipment, relocation expenses, and the unamortized value of any Tenant Improvements paid for by Tenant in excess of the TI Allowance.

**[ARTICLE 16 --- DEFAULT AND REMEDIES]{.underline}**

**Section 16.1 --- Events of Default**

The occurrence of any one or more of the following events shall constitute an \"Event of Default\" under this Lease:

> \(a\) Failure by Tenant to pay any installment of Rent or any other sum due under this Lease within ten (10) days after written notice from Landlord of such non-payment;
>
> \(b\) Failure by Tenant to perform or observe any other covenant, term, or condition of this Lease within thirty (30) days after written notice from Landlord specifying such failure; provided, however, that if such failure is of a nature that cannot reasonably be cured within thirty (30) days, Tenant shall not be in default if Tenant commences cure within such thirty (30) day period and thereafter diligently and continuously pursues such cure to completion;
>
> \(c\) The filing by or against Tenant of a petition in bankruptcy, the appointment of a receiver or trustee for Tenant\'s assets, or Tenant\'s making of a general assignment for the benefit of creditors, and such filing, appointment, or assignment is not dismissed or vacated within sixty (60) days;
>
> \(d\) Abandonment of the Premises by Tenant for a period of fifteen (15) or more consecutive days.

**Section 16.2 --- Remedies**

Upon the occurrence of an Event of Default, Landlord shall have the following remedies, which shall be cumulative and in addition to any other remedies available at law or in equity:

> \(a\) Landlord may terminate this Lease by written notice to Tenant, in which case Tenant shall immediately surrender the Premises. If Tenant fails to surrender, Landlord may re-enter the Premises and remove Tenant and Tenant\'s property in accordance with applicable law;
>
> \(b\) Landlord may re-enter the Premises without terminating this Lease and may relet the Premises or any part thereof for such term, at such rental, and upon such conditions as Landlord deems appropriate. Tenant shall be liable for the deficiency between the Rent due under this Lease and the net rent collected upon reletting, after deduction of all costs of reletting, including brokers\' commissions, renovation costs, and reasonable attorneys\' fees;
>
> \(c\) Landlord may recover from Tenant all unpaid Rent that has accrued through the date of termination, the cost of recovering possession of the Premises, and damages measured by the difference between the Rent under this Lease and the fair market rental value of the Premises for the remaining Term, discounted to present value at eight percent (8%) per annum.

**[ARTICLE 17 --- SURRENDER AND RESTORATION]{.underline}**

Upon the expiration or earlier termination of this Lease, Tenant shall peaceably surrender the Premises to Landlord in the same condition as received, reasonable wear and tear and damage by fire or other casualty excepted. Tenant shall remove all of its personal property, trade fixtures, dental equipment, and signage from the Premises on or before the Expiration Date or the effective date of termination. Any property of Tenant not removed from the Premises within ten (10) days following the Expiration Date or the effective date of termination shall be deemed abandoned by Tenant, and Landlord may dispose of such property without liability to Tenant. Tenant shall repair all damage to the Premises caused by the removal of Tenant\'s property, at Tenant\'s sole cost and expense, and shall leave the Premises in a broom-clean condition.

**[ARTICLE 19 --- RENEWAL OPTION]{.underline}**

**Section 19.1 --- Grant of Option**

Provided that (a) Tenant is not in default under this Lease at the time of exercise of the renewal option and (b) no Event of Default exists at the commencement of the Renewal Term, Tenant shall have one (1) option to renew this Lease for an additional period of five (5) years (the \"Renewal Term\"), commencing on November 1, 2028 and expiring on October 31, 2033, on the same terms and conditions as this Lease, except that (i) Base Rent during the Renewal Term shall be at the then-prevailing fair market rent for comparable medical and dental office space in the Raleigh, North Carolina market, as reasonably determined by Landlord, and (ii) there shall be no further renewal options unless otherwise agreed in writing. Tenant shall exercise this option by delivering written notice to Landlord no later than nine (9) months prior to the Expiration Date (i.e., by no later than January 31, 2028). Time is of the essence with respect to Tenant\'s exercise of this renewal option.

**Section 19.2 --- Fair Market Rent Determination**

If Landlord and Tenant are unable to agree on the fair market rent for the Renewal Term within sixty (60) days following Landlord\'s receipt of Tenant\'s exercise notice, the fair market rent shall be determined by arbitration as follows. Within thirty (30) days after the expiration of such sixty (60) day negotiation period, each Party shall select and engage, at its own cost, a licensed commercial real estate appraiser with at least ten (10) years of experience in the Raleigh, North Carolina office market. Each appraiser shall independently determine the fair market rent for the Premises within forty-five (45) days of engagement. If the two appraisals differ, the two appraisers shall jointly select a third appraiser meeting the same qualifications. The third appraiser shall, within thirty (30) days of selection, independently determine the fair market rent. The fair market rent shall be the average of the two closest of the three appraisals. The cost of the third appraiser shall be shared equally by the Parties.

**[ARTICLE 20 --- EARLY TERMINATION]{.underline}**

**Section 20.1 --- Tenant\'s Early Termination Right**

Tenant shall have the right to terminate this Lease effective as of the end of Lease Year 4 (October 31, 2025), upon the satisfaction of each of the following conditions:

> \(a\) **Notice.** Tenant shall deliver written notice to Landlord of its intent to terminate this Lease no later than six (6) months prior to the effective termination date (i.e., by no later than April 30, 2025). Time is of the essence with respect to delivery of such notice.
>
> \(b\) **Termination Payment.** Simultaneously with the delivery of the termination notice, Tenant shall pay to Landlord an early termination fee (the \"Termination Payment\") equal to the sum of the following:
>
> \(i\) **Unamortized Tenant Improvement Costs:** The unamortized balance of the TI Allowance as of the effective termination date, calculated on a straight-line basis over the seven (7) year Lease Term. The TI Allowance of \$38,400.00, amortized at \$5,485.71 per year (\$38,400.00 divided by 7 years). At the end of Lease Year 4, four (4) years of amortization have elapsed and three (3) years remain. The unamortized balance equals \$38,400.00 multiplied by 3/7, which equals **\$16,457.14**.
>
> \(ii\) **Three (3) Months\' Base Rent:** Three (3) months of Base Rent at the rate in effect for the Lease Year in which the termination becomes effective. >
> **Total Termination Payment: \$16,457.14 + \$24,200.00 = \$40,657.14.**
>
> \(c\) **Payment Terms.** The Termination Payment shall be paid in full, in immediately available funds (by wire transfer or certified check), at the time the termination notice is delivered to Landlord. Landlord shall hold the Security Deposit as security for the faithful performance by Tenant of all terms, covenants, and conditions of this Lease. Landlord may, but shall not be required to, apply all or any portion of the Security Deposit to cure any default by Tenant under this Lease, including but not limited to the payment of any rent or other amounts due and unpaid, the repair of damage to the Premises caused by Tenant, or the payment of any other sum which Landlord may expend or be required to expend by reason of Tenant\'s default. If Landlord applies any portion of the Security Deposit, Tenant shall, within ten (10) days after written notice from Landlord, deposit with Landlord an amount sufficient to restore the Security Deposit to its original amount. Landlord shall not be required to hold the Security Deposit in a separate account or in an interest-bearing account, and Landlord shall not be required to pay interest on the Security Deposit. The Security Deposit, or any balance remaining after application by Landlord as permitted herein, shall be returned to Tenant within thirty (30) days after the expiration of the Lease Term and Tenant\'s complete vacation and surrender of the Premises in the condition required by this Lease, less any amounts applied by Landlord in accordance with this Article 6.

**[ARTICLE 7 --- USE OF PREMISES]{.underline}**

**[Section 7.1 --- Permitted Use]{.underline}**

Tenant shall use and occupy the Premises solely for the operation of a childcare, daycare, and early childhood education facility (the \"Permitted Use\") and for no other purpose whatsoever without the prior written consent of Landlord, which consent may be withheld in Landlord\'s sole and absolute discretion. Tenant shall comply with all applicable federal, state, and local laws, rules, regulations, and ordinances governing the operation of a childcare and daycare facility, including but not limited to the licensing requirements of the North Carolina Division of Child Development and Early Education, and shall maintain in full force and effect at all times during the Lease Term all licenses and permits required for the Permitted Use.

**[Section 7.2 --- Exclusive Use]{.underline}**

During the Lease Term and any Renewal Term, Landlord shall not lease, permit, or suffer any other space within Millbrook Medical Plaza to be used for the operation of a childcare, daycare, or early childhood education facility. This exclusive use covenant shall run with the Property and shall be binding upon Landlord and Landlord\'s successors and assigns with respect to the Building and the Property. In the event Landlord breaches this Section 7.2, Tenant\'s sole remedy shall be to seek injunctive relief and to recover actual damages incurred by Tenant as a result of such breach.

**[Section 7.3 --- Compliance with Law]{.underline}**

Tenant shall, at its sole cost and expense, comply with all applicable laws, ordinances, rules, regulations, codes, and governmental requirements relating to the use, occupancy, and condition of the Premises, including without limitation all applicable fire codes, building codes, health and sanitation regulations, zoning ordinances, and the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990, as amended (\"ADA\"). Tenant shall obtain and maintain at all times during the Lease Term all permits, licenses, and governmental approvals required for the Permitted Use, and shall promptly furnish copies thereof to Landlord upon request.

**[ARTICLE 8 --- MAINTENANCE AND REPAIRS]{.underline}**

**[Section 8.1 --- Tenant\'s Obligations]{.underline}**

Tenant shall, at its sole cost and expense, keep and maintain the interior of the Premises in good order, condition, and repair throughout the Lease Term, including but not limited to interior walls, ceilings, floors, floor coverings, doors, windows (excluding exterior glazing), plumbing fixtures and connections within the Premises, electrical fixtures and wiring within the Premises, lighting, and all mechanical systems, including heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (\"HVAC\") systems, exclusively serving the Premises. Tenant shall be responsible for the regular maintenance, service, and repair of all HVAC equipment serving the Premises, including regular filter replacement and seasonal preventive maintenance performed in accordance with the manufacturer\'s specifications and recommendations. Tenant shall enter into a maintenance contract with a qualified HVAC service provider, a copy of which shall be provided to Landlord upon request. Tenant shall promptly make all repairs and replacements necessary to maintain the interior of the Premises in good condition, ordinary wear and tear and damage by fire or other casualty excepted.

**[Section 8.2 --- Landlord\'s Obligations]{.underline}**

Landlord shall be responsible for the maintenance, repair, and replacement of the structural elements of the Building, including but not limited to the roof, foundation, exterior walls, structural columns, load-bearing walls, and the building envelope (collectively, the \"Structural Elements\"). Landlord shall maintain the roof in watertight condition throughout the Lease Term. The costs of structural repairs and replacements shall not be included in Operating Expenses except to the extent of capital expenditures amortized as permitted in Section 5.2 of this Lease. Landlord shall perform all structural repairs and replacements in a workmanlike manner and shall use commercially reasonable efforts to minimize disruption to Tenant\'s operations.

**[ARTICLE 9 --- INSURANCE]{.underline}**

**[Section 9.1 --- Tenant\'s Insurance]{.underline}**

Tenant shall procure and maintain in full force and effect at all times during the Lease Term, at Tenant\'s sole cost and expense, the following insurance coverages:

> \(a\) **Commercial General Liability Insurance** with limits of not less than One Million Dollars (\$1,000,000.00) per occurrence and Two Million Dollars (\$2,000,000.00) in the aggregate, covering bodily injury, personal injury, and property damage arising out of or in connection with Tenant\'s use and occupancy of the Premises, including products/completed operations and contractual liability coverage;
>
> \(b\) **Property Insurance** covering all of Tenant\'s personal property, trade fixtures, inventory, equipment, and leasehold improvements located within the Premises, written on an \"all risks\" or \"special form\" basis, in an amount not less than the full replacement cost thereof;
>
> \(c\) **Workers\' Compensation Insurance** as required by the laws of the State of North Carolina, including employer\'s liability coverage with limits of not less than Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$500,000.00) per accident;
>
> \(d\) **Business Income Insurance** (including extra expense coverage) in an amount sufficient to cover not less than twelve (12) months of Tenant\'s gross earnings and continuing expenses, including the payment of rent under this Lease.

All policies required under this Section 9.1 shall name Landlord, Thornfield Management Corp., and any mortgagee of the Property designated by Landlord as additional insureds. All policies shall be issued by insurance companies licensed to do business in the State of North Carolina with an A.M. Best rating of not less than A-VII. Certificates of insurance evidencing the foregoing coverages shall be delivered to Landlord prior to the Commencement Date and annually thereafter, and shall provide that such policies shall not be cancelled or materially modified without at least thirty (30) days\' prior written notice to Landlord.

**[Section 9.2 --- Landlord\'s Insurance]{.underline}**

Landlord shall maintain property insurance on the Building (excluding Tenant\'s personal property, trade fixtures, and leasehold improvements) and commercial general liability insurance covering the Common Areas, in such amounts and with such coverages as Landlord deems reasonably appropriate. The cost of such insurance shall be included in Insurance Costs and passed through to Tenant as Additional Rent in accordance with Article 5 of this Lease.

**[Section 9.3 --- Waiver of Subrogation]{.underline}**

Each party hereby waives any and all rights of recovery, claim, action, or cause of action against the other party, its agents, officers, employees, and representatives, for any loss or damage to property to the extent that such loss or damage is covered by insurance required to be carried under this Lease or by insurance actually carried by the waiving party, whichever is greater, notwithstanding that such loss or damage may result from the negligence or fault of the other party. Each party shall cause its respective insurance carrier(s) to include a waiver of subrogation endorsement or clause in all applicable policies, permitting the foregoing waiver.

**[ARTICLE 10 --- ENVIRONMENTAL PROVISIONS]{.underline}**

**[Section 10.1 --- Tenant\'s Environmental Obligations]{.underline}**

Tenant shall comply with all applicable federal, state, and local environmental laws, statutes, regulations, ordinances, and governmental requirements relating to the use and occupancy of the Premises and the operation of a childcare facility therein, including but not limited to the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act (\"CERCLA\"), the Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (\"RCRA\"), the Toxic Substances Control Act (\"TSCA\"), and analogous state laws. Tenant shall be responsible for the proper handling, storage, use, and disposal of all cleaning chemicals, sanitizers, craft materials, and any other substances or materials that may be classified as hazardous or regulated under applicable environmental laws (collectively, \"Hazardous Materials\"). Tenant shall not cause or permit any Hazardous Materials to be generated, manufactured, stored, released, discharged, or disposed of on, under, or from the Premises, except in de minimis quantities that are customarily used in the ordinary course of childcare operations and that are used, stored, and disposed of in full compliance with all applicable environmental laws.

**[Section 10.2 --- Phase I ESA]{.underline}**

Prior to the Commencement Date, Landlord provided Tenant with a copy of a Phase I Environmental Site Assessment of the Property prepared by Hanover Environmental Consultants Inc. and dated November 15, 2016 (the \"Phase I Report\"). The Phase I Report identified no recognized environmental conditions (\"RECs\"), controlled recognized environmental conditions (\"CRECs\"), or historical recognized environmental conditions (\"HRECs\") affecting the Property. Landlord represents and warrants that, to Landlord\'s actual knowledge as of the Lease Date, the Phase I Report remains accurate and complete in all material respects and that no conditions have arisen since the date of the Phase I Report that would constitute a REC affecting the Property.

**[Section 10.3 --- Indemnification]{.underline}**

Tenant shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Landlord, Landlord\'s partners, officers, directors, agents, and employees from and against any and all claims, actions, demands, liabilities, losses, damages, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys\' fees and court costs) arising from or related to (a) Tenant\'s violation of any applicable environmental law, (b) the presence, release, or threatened release of any Hazardous Materials on, under, or from the Premises that are introduced by Tenant, its agents, employees, contractors, or invitees, or (c) any environmental contamination or remediation obligation attributable to Tenant\'s use and occupancy of the Premises. This indemnification obligation shall survive the expiration or earlier termination of this Lease.

**[ARTICLE 11 --- ASSIGNMENT AND SUBLETTING]{.underline}**

**[Section 11.1 --- Landlord Consent Required]{.underline}**

Tenant shall not assign, transfer, mortgage, pledge, hypothecate, or encumber this Lease or any interest herein, nor sublet all or any portion of the Premises, nor permit the use or occupancy of the Premises by any party other than Tenant, without the prior written consent of Landlord in each instance. Landlord\'s consent to any proposed assignment or subletting may be withheld in Landlord\'s reasonable discretion, based upon factors including but not limited to the proposed assignee\'s or subtenant\'s financial condition, creditworthiness, business reputation, intended use of the Premises, and compatibility with the character and operation of the Building.

**[Section 11.2 --- Landlord Recapture Right]{.underline}**

Upon receipt of Tenant\'s request for consent to an assignment or subletting, together with all information and documentation required under Section 11.3, Landlord shall have the option, exercisable within thirty (30) days after receipt of Tenant\'s notice and all required documentation, to terminate this Lease as to the space proposed to be assigned or sublet (or as to the entire Premises in the case of a proposed assignment of this Lease) effective as of the proposed commencement date of the assignment or sublease (the \"Recapture Right\"). If Landlord exercises the Recapture Right, this Lease shall terminate as of the effective date specified in Landlord\'s notice (or, in the case of a proposed sublease of less than the entire Premises, the Premises shall be reduced by the space proposed to be sublet, and the Base Rent and Tenant\'s Pro Rata Share shall be equitably adjusted). Upon exercise of the Recapture Right, Landlord may lease the recaptured space directly to the proposed assignee or subtenant, or to any other party, on whatever terms and conditions Landlord deems appropriate, without any obligation or liability to Tenant, and Tenant shall have no right to share in any rent, premium, or other consideration received by Landlord in connection therewith. If Landlord does not exercise the Recapture Right within the thirty (30) day period, Landlord\'s consent to the proposed assignment or subletting shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed, subject to the conditions set forth in Section 11.3 below.

**[Section 11.3 --- Conditions of Consent]{.underline}**

Any consent by Landlord to an assignment or subletting shall be subject to the following conditions, each of which must be satisfied prior to the effective date of the assignment or sublease:

> \(a\) The proposed assignee or subtenant shall satisfy Landlord\'s reasonable financial, operational, and creditworthiness standards and shall demonstrate the ability to fulfill all obligations under this Lease (or the sublease, as applicable);
>
> \(b\) Tenant shall remain primarily liable under this Lease, jointly and severally with the assignee, for the payment of all rent and the performance of all obligations hereunder, unless Landlord expressly agrees in writing to release Tenant;
>
> \(c\) The assignment or sublease shall be on terms and conditions substantially consistent with the terms of this Lease, and the proposed use shall be limited to the Permitted Use or another use approved by Landlord;
>
> \(d\) Tenant shall provide Landlord with not less than thirty (30) days\' prior written notice of the proposed assignment or subletting, together with complete information regarding the proposed assignee or subtenant, including audited financial statements for the most recent three (3) fiscal years, a business plan, references, and the proposed terms of the assignment or sublease;
>
> \(e\) Tenant shall pay to Landlord, as additional rent, fifty percent (50%) of any consideration received by Tenant from the assignee or subtenant in excess of the rent payable by Tenant under this Lease (net of Tenant\'s reasonable costs of the assignment or subletting, including brokerage fees, legal fees, and tenant improvement costs).

**[Section 11.4 --- Affiliate Transfers]{.underline}**

Notwithstanding the provisions of Sections 11.1, 11.2, and 11.3 above, Tenant may, without Landlord\'s consent and without triggering Landlord\'s Recapture Right, assign this Lease or sublet all or any portion of the Premises to an Affiliate of Tenant, provided that (a) Tenant gives Landlord written notice of such transfer at least fifteen (15) days prior to the effective date thereof, (b) the Affiliate assumes in writing all obligations of Tenant under this Lease, and (c) Tenant remains primarily liable for all obligations under this Lease. As used herein, \"Affiliate\" shall mean any entity that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with Tenant, where \"control\" means the ownership of fifty percent (50%) or more of the voting interests or the power to direct the management and policies of such entity.

**[ARTICLE 12 --- RENEWAL OPTIONS]{.underline}**

**[Section 12.1 --- Grant of Options]{.underline}**

Provided that Tenant is not then in default beyond any applicable notice and cure period under this Lease at the time of exercise or at the commencement of the applicable Renewal Term, Tenant shall have three (3) consecutive options to renew the Lease Term for a period of five (5) years each (each, a \"Renewal Term\"), on the same terms and conditions as set forth in this Lease, except as to Base Rent, which shall be determined in accordance with Sections 12.3 and 12.4 below.

**[Section 12.2 --- Exercise of Options]{.underline}**

Tenant shall exercise each Renewal Option by delivering irrevocable written notice to Landlord not later than twelve (12) months prior to the expiration of the then-current Lease Term or Renewal Term, as applicable. Time is of the essence with respect to the exercise of each Renewal Option. Failure by Tenant to timely deliver written notice of exercise in accordance with this Section 12.2 shall constitute an irrevocable waiver of the applicable Renewal Option and all subsequent unexercised Renewal Options. The exercise of each Renewal Option is personal to BrightPath Learning Centers LLC and may not be exercised by any assignee or subtenant of Tenant (other than a permitted Affiliate transferee under Section 11.4).

**[Section 12.3 --- Renewal Rent]{.underline}**

> \(a\) **First Renewal Term (Years 16--20):** The Base Rent for each year of the First Renewal Term shall be the lesser of (i) the then-prevailing fair market rent for comparable childcare and daycare space in the Raleigh, North Carolina metropolitan area, determined in accordance with Section 12.4, and (ii) the Base Rent resulting from three percent (3%) annual compounding from the Year 15 Base Rent. If the parties cannot agree upon the fair market rent within thirty (30) days following Tenant\'s exercise of the First Renewal Option, the fair market rent shall be determined by arbitration in accordance with Section 12.4.
>
> \(b\) **Second Renewal Term (Years 21--25) and Third Renewal Term (Years 26--30):** The Base Rent for each year of the Second and Third Renewal Terms shall be the then-prevailing fair market rent for comparable childcare and daycare space in the Raleigh, North Carolina metropolitan area, determined in accordance with Section 12.4.

**[Section 12.4 --- Fair Market Rent Determination]{.underline}**

If the parties are unable to agree upon the fair market rent for the applicable Renewal Term within thirty (30) days following Tenant\'s exercise of the applicable Renewal Option, then each party shall, within fifteen (15) days thereafter, appoint a licensed MAI-designated appraiser with at least ten (10) years of experience appraising commercial properties in the Raleigh, North Carolina metropolitan area. The two appraisers so appointed shall attempt to agree upon the fair market rent within thirty (30) days following their appointment. If the two appraisers are unable to agree upon the fair market rent within such thirty (30) day period, they shall jointly appoint a third licensed MAI-designated appraiser meeting the same qualifications, and the fair market rent shall be the average of the two appraisals that are closest in value. The costs and fees of the third appraiser shall be borne equally by Landlord and Tenant. Each party shall bear the costs and fees of its own appointed appraiser. Pending the determination of fair market rent, Tenant shall pay Base Rent at the rate in effect during the last year of the immediately preceding Lease Term or Renewal Term, with an adjustment (credit or payment) to be made within thirty (30) days following the final determination.

**[ARTICLE 13 --- LANDLORD\'S ACCESS]{.underline}**

Landlord and its authorized agents, employees, and contractors shall have the right to enter the Premises during normal business hours upon not less than twenty-four (24) hours\' prior written or oral notice to Tenant for the purpose of (a) inspecting the Premises, (b) performing repairs, maintenance, or alterations to the Premises or the Building, (c) showing the Premises to prospective tenants during the last twelve (12) months of the Lease Term or any Renewal Term, (d) showing the Premises to prospective purchasers, lenders, or insurers at any time during the Lease Term, and (e) any other reasonable purpose related to Landlord\'s ownership and operation of the Building. In the event of an emergency threatening imminent damage to the Premises, the Building, or persons therein, Landlord may enter the Premises at any time without prior notice. Given the nature of the Permitted Use as a childcare facility serving minor children, Landlord agrees to coordinate all access with Tenant\'s on-site manager so as to minimize disruption to childcare operations and to ensure the safety and security of all children present on the Premises. All persons entering the Premises on behalf of Landlord shall comply with Tenant\'s reasonable sign-in and identification procedures.

**[ARTICLE 14 --- DAMAGE AND DESTRUCTION]{.underline}**

**[Section 14.1 --- Landlord\'s Obligation to Restore]{.underline}**

If the Premises or the Building are damaged or destroyed by fire or other casualty, Landlord shall, subject to the provisions of this Article 14, commence restoration of the Premises and the Building within sixty (60) days after the date of such damage or destruction and shall diligently pursue such restoration to completion within one hundred eighty (180) days thereafter. Landlord\'s restoration obligation shall be limited to the Structural Elements and the base building improvements and shall not include Tenant\'s personal property, trade fixtures, leasehold improvements, or any other property of Tenant. If Landlord reasonably determines that restoration cannot be completed within one hundred eighty (180) days after the date of damage or destruction, either party may terminate this Lease by delivering written notice to the other party within thirty (30) days after Landlord\'s notice of such determination, and this Lease shall terminate as of the date specified in such notice.

**[Section 14.2 --- Rent Abatement]{.underline}**

During any period in which the Premises or any portion thereof are rendered untenantable by reason of fire or other casualty, Base Rent and Additional Rent shall abate proportionately based on the ratio of the untenantable area to the total RSF of the Premises. Such abatement shall commence on the date of the casualty and shall continue until the earlier of (a) the date on which the Premises are restored to a tenantable condition or (b) the date on which this Lease is terminated pursuant to Section 14.1.

**[ARTICLE 15 --- CONDEMNATION]{.underline}**

If all or a material portion of the Premises is taken or condemned for any public or quasi-public purpose by any lawful authority by exercise of the right of eminent domain, or by agreement between Landlord and such authority in lieu of or in anticipation of such exercise (a \"Taking\"), either Landlord or Tenant may terminate this Lease by delivering written notice to the other party within thirty (30) days after the date of such Taking, and this Lease shall terminate as of the date on which possession is required to be delivered to the condemning authority. If less than a material portion of the Premises is taken and the remaining portion of the Premises is reasonably usable by Tenant for the Permitted Use, this Lease shall continue in full force and effect but the Base Rent shall be equitably reduced in proportion to the area of the Premises so taken. Tenant shall be entitled to make a separate claim against the condemning authority for the value of Tenant\'s trade fixtures, personal property, and moving expenses, and for business interruption losses, but Tenant shall have no right to claim or receive any portion of any award made to Landlord for the value of the leasehold interest, the Building, or the land. As used herein, a \"material portion\" shall mean a Taking of twenty-five percent (25%) or more of the RSF of the Premises.

**[ARTICLE 16 --- DEFAULT AND REMEDIES]{.underline}**

**[Section 16.1 --- Events of Default]{.underline}**

The occurrence of any one or more of the following events shall constitute an \"Event of Default\" under this Lease:

> \(a\) Tenant fails to pay any installment of Base Rent, Additional Rent, or any other sum due under this Lease within five (5) business days after Landlord delivers written notice to Tenant that such payment is past due;
>
> \(b\) Tenant fails to perform or observe any other term, covenant, or condition of this Lease and such failure continues for a period of thirty (30) days after Landlord delivers written notice to Tenant specifying the nature of such failure; provided, however, that if the nature of such failure is such that it cannot reasonably be cured within thirty (30) days, Tenant shall not be in default if Tenant commences the cure within such thirty (30) day period and thereafter diligently and continuously pursues such cure to completion within a reasonable time;
>
> \(c\) Tenant files a voluntary petition in bankruptcy or is adjudicated bankrupt or insolvent, or makes a general assignment for the benefit of creditors, or a receiver or trustee is appointed for substantially all of Tenant\'s assets or Tenant\'s interest in this Lease, or any proceeding is commenced under any bankruptcy or insolvency law by or against Tenant and is not dismissed within sixty (60) days;
>
> \(d\) Tenant abandons or vacates the Premises for a period of thirty (30) or more consecutive days without maintaining the Premises in accordance with this Lease;
>
> \(e\) Tenant\'s childcare license issued by the North Carolina Division of Child Development and Early Education is revoked, suspended, or otherwise rendered ineffective for a period of more than sixty (60) consecutive days.

**[Section 16.2 --- Landlord\'s Remedies]{.underline}**

Upon the occurrence and continuation of an Event of Default, Landlord shall have the following remedies, which shall be cumulative and in addition to any other remedies available at law or in equity:

> \(a\) Landlord may terminate this Lease by delivering written notice of termination to Tenant, whereupon Tenant shall immediately surrender possession of the Premises to Landlord. Upon termination, Landlord may recover from Tenant all unpaid rent accrued through the date of termination, the cost of recovering possession of the Premises, the cost of any reletting, and all damages incurred by Landlord as a result of Tenant\'s default;
>
> \(b\) Landlord may re-enter and take possession of the Premises without terminating this Lease and may relet the Premises, or any portion thereof, on behalf of Tenant for such term, at such rent, and upon such other terms and conditions as Landlord may deem advisable, with the right to make alterations and repairs to the Premises. Tenant shall remain liable for all rent and other amounts due under this Lease, less the net proceeds of any reletting;
>
> \(c\) Landlord may recover as damages the present value of all future Base Rent and Additional Rent that would have been payable during the remainder of the Lease Term, discounted to present value at the rate of six percent (6%) per annum, less the fair market rental value of the Premises for the same period, similarly discounted, together with all other damages incurred by Landlord, including reasonable attorneys\' fees and court costs.

Landlord shall use commercially reasonable efforts to mitigate its damages following any Event of Default, in accordance with applicable North Carolina law.

**[ARTICLE 17 --- SUBORDINATION AND ATTORNMENT]{.underline}**

This Lease shall be subject and subordinate to any mortgage, deed of trust, or ground lease now existing or hereafter placed upon the Property or any portion thereof, and to all renewals, modifications, consolidations, replacements, and extensions thereof (each, a \"Superior Instrument\"). Tenant agrees to execute and deliver, within ten (10) days after request, any instrument or certificate that Landlord or the holder of any Superior Instrument may reasonably require to confirm such subordination. Tenant further agrees to attorn to any successor landlord, including any purchaser at a foreclosure sale or any grantee under a deed in lieu of foreclosure, and to recognize such successor as Landlord under this Lease. Landlord shall use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain from any current or future holder of a Superior Instrument a subordination, non-disturbance, and attornment agreement (an \"SNDA\") in such holder\'s customary form, providing that Tenant\'s possession of the Premises shall not be disturbed so long as Tenant is not in default under this Lease, and Landlord shall deliver such SNDA to Tenant within thirty (30) days after Tenant\'s written request therefor.

**[ARTICLE 18 --- NOTICES]{.underline}**

All notices, demands, requests, consents, approvals, and other communications required or permitted under this Lease shall be in writing and shall be delivered by (a) personal hand delivery, (b) nationally recognized overnight courier service (such as FedEx or UPS Next Day), or (c) United States Certified Mail, return receipt requested, postage prepaid, addressed as follows:

Notices shall be deemed effective (i) upon receipt, if delivered by personal hand delivery; (ii) on the next business day following deposit with a nationally recognized overnight courier service; or (iii) on the third (3rd) business day following deposit in the United States Mail in accordance with this Article 18.

**[ARTICLE 19 --- MISCELLANEOUS PROVISIONS]{.underline}**

**[Section 19.1 --- Entire Agreement]{.underline}**

This Lease, including all Exhibits attached hereto and incorporated herein by reference, constitutes the entire agreement between Landlord and Tenant with respect to the subject matter hereof and supersedes all prior negotiations, representations, warranties, commitments, proposals, and understandings, whether written or oral, relating thereto. No amendment, modification, or supplement to this Lease shall be valid or binding unless set forth in a written instrument executed by both Landlord and Tenant.

**[Section 19.2 --- Governing Law]{.underline}**

This Lease shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of North Carolina, without giving effect to any choice of law or conflict of law principles that would result in the application of the laws of any other jurisdiction.

**[Section 19.3 --- Severability]{.underline}**

If any provision of this Lease or the application thereof to any person or circumstance is held to be invalid, illegal, or unenforceable, the validity, legality, and enforceability of the remaining provisions of this Lease shall not be affected or impaired thereby, and the parties shall negotiate in good faith to replace the invalid provision with a valid provision that achieves, to the greatest extent possible, the economic, business, and other purposes of the invalid provision.

**[Section 19.4 --- Successors and Assigns]{.underline}**

This Lease shall be binding upon and inure to the benefit of the parties hereto and their respective heirs, executors, administrators, successors, and permitted assigns, subject to the provisions of Article 11 governing assignments and subletting.

**[Section 19.5 --- Waiver]{.underline}**

No waiver by either party of any breach of or default under any provision of this Lease shall be deemed a waiver of any other breach or default, whether of the same or a different provision, and no waiver shall be effective unless in writing and signed by the waiving party. No failure or delay by either party in exercising any right or remedy under this Lease shall operate as a waiver thereof.

**[Section 19.6 --- Broker Representation]{.underline}**

Landlord represents and warrants to Tenant that Ridgeview Realty Brokers Inc. acted as Landlord\'s broker in connection with this Lease and that Landlord shall be solely responsible for the payment of all brokerage commissions due to Ridgeview Realty Brokers Inc. Tenant represents and warrants to Landlord that no broker, agent, or finder acted on behalf of Tenant in connection with this Lease. Each party hereby indemnifies and holds the other party harmless from and against any and all claims, losses, damages, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys\' fees) arising from any breach of the foregoing representations or from any claim for commissions or fees by any broker, agent, or finder claiming to have acted on behalf of the indemnifying party.

**[Section 19.7 --- Force Majeure]{.underline}**

Except for the payment of Base Rent, Additional Rent, and any other monetary obligations under this Lease, neither party shall be liable for any delay or failure in the performance of any obligation under this Lease to the extent that such delay or failure is caused by fire, flood, earthquake, hurricane, tornado, pandemic, epidemic, governmental action or inaction, labor disputes, strikes, lockouts, material shortages, acts of terrorism, war, civil disturbance, or any other cause or event beyond the reasonable control of the affected party (each, a \"Force Majeure Event\"). The time for performance of any such obligation shall be extended by the duration of the Force Majeure Event.

**[Section 19.8 --- Quiet Enjoyment]{.underline}**

So long as Tenant is not in default under this Lease beyond any applicable notice and cure period, Landlord covenants and agrees that Tenant shall peaceably and quietly have, hold, and enjoy the Premises for the full Lease Term and any Renewal Term without hindrance, disturbance, or molestation by Landlord or any person lawfully claiming by, through, or under Landlord.

**[Section 19.9 --- Recording]{.underline}**

Neither Landlord nor Tenant shall record this Lease or any memorandum thereof without the prior written consent of the other party. At the written request of either party, Landlord and Tenant shall promptly execute and deliver a short form memorandum of this Lease in recordable form, which memorandum shall set forth the names of the parties, the description of the Premises, the Commencement Date, the Expiration Date, and the Renewal Options, but shall not set forth the rental terms or other financial provisions of this Lease. The cost of recording such memorandum shall be borne by the requesting party.

**[Section 19.10 --- Counterparts]{.underline}**

This Lease may be executed in any number of counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original and all of which together shall constitute one and the same instrument. Execution and delivery of this Lease by facsimile or electronic transmission of a signed counterpart shall be deemed effective as delivery of an originally signed counterpart.

This Lease Agreement (this \"Lease\") is entered into as of July 1, 2014 (the \"Effective Date\"), by and between:

**LANDLORD:** Thornfield Realty Holdings LP, a North Carolina limited partnership, whose general partner is Thornfield Management Corp., a North Carolina corporation, with its registered office at 500 South Tryon Street, Suite 2200, Charlotte, NC 28202 (\"Landlord\"); and

**TENANT:** Southeastern Fire & Safety Equipment Co., a North Carolina corporation, with its principal office at 770 Greystone Boulevard, Unit 12, Gastonia, NC 28052 (\"Tenant\").

**RECITALS**

**WHEREAS**, Landlord is the owner of certain real property and improvements known as Greystone Industrial Park, located in Gastonia, Gaston County, North Carolina, consisting of multiple industrial and flex-space units designed for light industrial, warehouse, and commercial uses; and

**WHEREAS**, Landlord desires to lease to Tenant, and Tenant desires to lease from Landlord, certain premises within Greystone Industrial Park, more particularly described herein, upon the terms and conditions set forth in this Lease; and

**WHEREAS**, the parties wish to memorialize their respective rights and obligations with respect to the leased premises.

**NOW, THEREFORE**, in consideration of the mutual covenants and agreements set forth herein, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the parties agree as follows:

**[ARTICLE 1 --- DEFINITIONS]{.underline}**

As used in this Lease, the following terms shall have the meanings set forth below:

**1.1 \"Premises\"** shall mean Unit 12, Greystone Industrial Park, 770 Greystone Boulevard, Gastonia, NC 28052, consisting of approximately twenty-two thousand (22,000) rentable square feet (\"RSF\") of industrial/flex space, including warehouse area, loading dock with two (2) drive-in bays, and office/flex area, as more particularly depicted on the floor plan attached hereto as **Exhibit A** and incorporated herein by reference.

**1.2 \"Building\"** shall mean the building in which the Premises are located within Greystone Industrial Park, together with all appurtenant structures, improvements, and fixtures forming a part thereof.

**1.3 \"Commencement Date\"** shall mean July 1, 2014, which is the date upon which the Term of this Lease shall commence and Tenant\'s obligation to pay Base Rent shall begin.

**1.4 \"Expiration Date\"** shall mean June 30, 2024, which is the date upon which the initial Term of this Lease shall expire, unless the Term is sooner terminated or extended in accordance with the provisions of this Lease.

**1.5 \"Lease Term\" or \"Term\"** shall mean the period commencing on the Commencement Date and ending on the Expiration Date, unless sooner terminated or extended as provided herein. The Term shall consist of ten (10) Lease Years.

**1.6 \"Lease Year\"** shall mean each successive twelve (12) month period during the Term. The first Lease Year shall commence on July 1, 2014 and end on June 30, 2015, and each subsequent Lease Year shall commence on the anniversary thereof and end on the day immediately preceding the next anniversary of the Commencement Date.

**1.7 \"Base Rent\"** shall mean the annual base rental amount payable by Tenant to Landlord during each Lease Year, as set forth in Article 4 and in the Rent Schedule attached hereto as **Exhibit B**.

**1.8 \"Common Areas\"** shall mean all areas and facilities within Greystone Industrial Park that are designated by Landlord for common use by tenants and their respective employees, agents, customers, and invitees, including without limitation parking areas, driveways, access roads, loading areas, sidewalks, landscaped areas, trash enclosures, and signage areas.

**1.9 \"Operating Expenses\"** shall mean all costs and expenses of operating, maintaining, repairing, replacing, and managing the Building and Greystone Industrial Park, including but not limited to real estate taxes and assessments, property insurance premiums, utilities for Common Areas, landscaping and grounds maintenance, snow and ice removal, security services, management fees (not to exceed five percent (5%) of gross rental income), common area maintenance and repair, and reasonable reserves for capital replacements.

**1.10 \"Hazardous Materials\"** shall have the meaning set forth in Article 14 of this Lease.

**1.11 \"Applicable Law\"** shall mean all federal, state, and local laws, statutes, regulations, rules, ordinances, codes, permits, and orders applicable to the Premises, the Building, Greystone Industrial Park, or Tenant\'s use and occupancy thereof, including without limitation all environmental laws and regulations, zoning ordinances, building codes, fire codes, and health and safety regulations.

**1.12 \"Landlord\'s Address\"** shall mean the address set forth in Article 17 for the delivery of notices to Landlord, or such other address as Landlord may designate from time to time in accordance with Article 17.

**[ARTICLE 2 --- PREMISES]{.underline}**

**2.1** Landlord hereby leases to Tenant, and Tenant hereby leases from Landlord, the Premises described as Unit 12, Greystone Industrial Park, 770 Greystone Boulevard, Gastonia, NC 28052, together with the non-exclusive right to use the Common Areas of Greystone Industrial Park in common with other tenants and occupants, subject to the rules and regulations established by Landlord from time to time.

**2.2** The Premises consist of approximately twenty-two thousand (22,000) rentable square feet of industrial/flex space, as more particularly depicted on the floor plan attached hereto as **Exhibit A** and incorporated herein by reference. The RSF measurement set forth herein shall be conclusive and binding upon both parties for all purposes under this Lease, including without limitation the calculation of Base Rent and Tenant\'s pro rata share of Operating Expenses.

**2.3** Tenant acknowledges that it has inspected and examined the Premises prior to the execution of this Lease and accepts the Premises in their \"as-is\" condition as of the Commencement Date, subject to any punch-list items identified by the parties in writing on or before the Commencement Date. Landlord makes no representations or warranties regarding the condition of the Premises, the Building, or Greystone Industrial Park, express or implied, except as expressly set forth in this Lease.

**[ARTICLE 3 --- TERM]{.underline}**

**3.1 Initial Term.** The initial Term of this Lease shall be ten (10) Lease Years, commencing on the Commencement Date (July 1, 2014) and expiring on the Expiration Date (June 30, 2024), unless sooner terminated in accordance with the provisions of this Lease.

**3.2 Renewal Option.** Tenant shall have one (1) option to renew the Term for an additional period of five (5) years (the \"Renewal Term\"), commencing on the day immediately following the Expiration Date and ending on June 30, 2029, upon all of the same terms and conditions as this Lease, except that Base Rent during the Renewal Term shall be at the then-prevailing fair market rental rate for comparable industrial/flex space in the Gastonia, North Carolina market, as determined in good faith by Landlord and Tenant. If the parties are unable to agree upon the fair market rental rate within thirty (30) days after Tenant\'s exercise of the Renewal Option, the fair market rental rate shall be determined by a licensed commercial real estate appraiser mutually selected by the parties, the cost of which shall be shared equally.

**3.3 Exercise of Renewal Option.** To exercise the Renewal Option set forth in Section 3.2, Tenant must deliver written notice of its election to renew to Landlord no later than ninety (90) days prior to the Expiration Date (i.e., by no later than April 1, 2024). Time is of the essence with respect to such notice. Failure by Tenant to timely deliver written notice of its election to renew in strict compliance with this Section 3.3 shall be deemed an irrevocable waiver of the Renewal Option, and the Term shall expire on the Expiration Date without further action by either party. The Renewal Option may not be exercised by Tenant if Tenant is in default under this Lease at the time of such exercise or at the time the Renewal Term is to commence.

**[ARTICLE 4 --- BASE RENT]{.underline}**

**Section 4.1 --- Base Rent Schedule**

Tenant shall pay to Landlord annual Base Rent in the amounts set forth in this Section 4.1 and as detailed in the Rent Schedule attached hereto as **Exhibit B** and incorporated herein by reference, payable in equal monthly installments in advance on the first (1st) day of each calendar month during the Term. Base Rent shall increase by two percent (2%) per annum on each anniversary of the Commencement Date, as set forth in the Rent Schedule attached hereto as Exhibit B.
