**Section 4.2 --- Payment**

All Base Rent and additional rent and other charges payable by Tenant under this Lease shall be due and payable on the first (1st) day of each calendar month, in advance, without notice, demand, deduction, abatement, or offset of any kind, except as expressly provided in this Lease. All payments shall be made in lawful currency of the United States by check or wire transfer to Landlord at Landlord\'s address set forth in Article 17, or to such other address or account as Landlord may designate from time to time by written notice to Tenant. If any payment of Base Rent or additional rent is not received by Landlord within five (5) days after its due date, Tenant shall pay a late charge equal to five percent (5%) of the overdue amount, which the parties agree represents a fair and reasonable estimate of the costs Landlord will incur as a result of such late payment. In addition, all amounts overdue by more than five (5) days shall bear interest from the due date until paid at the rate of one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month, or the maximum rate permitted by applicable North Carolina law, whichever is less.

**Section 4.3 --- Proration**

If the Commencement Date or the Expiration Date falls on a day other than the first or last day of a calendar month, respectively, Base Rent and additional rent for such partial month shall be prorated on a per diem basis based on the actual number of days in such calendar month. The parties acknowledge that, as of the Effective Date, the Commencement Date of July 1, 2014 and the Expiration Date of June 30, 2024 each align with the first and last days of a calendar month, respectively, and accordingly no proration is anticipated at this time.

**[ARTICLE 5 --- TRIPLE NET LEASE; OPERATING EXPENSES]{.underline}**

**Section 5.1 --- NNN Lease**

The parties acknowledge and agree that this Lease is intended to be and shall be construed as a triple net lease (\"NNN\"). Accordingly, in addition to Base Rent, Tenant shall be responsible for and shall pay, as additional rent, Tenant\'s pro rata share of all Operating Expenses, real estate taxes and assessments, and insurance premiums attributable to the Premises and the Building, as more particularly described in this Article 5. The Base Rent set forth in Article 4 shall be absolutely net to Landlord, and all costs, expenses, and obligations of every kind relating to the Premises which may arise or become due during the Term shall be paid by Tenant, except as otherwise expressly provided herein.

**Section 5.2 --- Pro Rata Share**

Tenant\'s pro rata share of Operating Expenses, real estate taxes, and insurance premiums shall be determined based on the ratio of the rentable square footage of the Premises (22,000 RSF) to the total rentable square footage of the Building or, where applicable, Greystone Industrial Park as a whole, as reasonably determined by Landlord. Landlord shall provide Tenant with a written statement of Tenant\'s pro rata share upon commencement of the Term and shall notify Tenant of any change in such pro rata share resulting from re-measurement or changes in the total rentable area of the Building or Greystone Industrial Park.

**Section 5.3 --- Real Estate Taxes**

Tenant shall pay its pro rata share of all real estate taxes, ad valorem taxes, special assessments, and governmental charges of every kind levied against the Building and/or the land on which Greystone Industrial Park is situated. Landlord shall provide Tenant with copies of applicable tax bills and reasonable supporting documentation upon Tenant\'s written request. In the event Landlord elects to contest any real estate tax assessment, Tenant shall pay its pro rata share of the reasonable costs of such contest.

**Section 5.4 --- Insurance**

Tenant shall pay its pro rata share of all premiums for property insurance, casualty insurance, and any other insurance maintained by Landlord on the Building and Common Areas of Greystone Industrial Park, as part of Operating Expenses.

**Section 5.5 --- Estimated Payments; Reconciliation**

Landlord may, at the beginning of each calendar year or Lease Year, estimate the total Operating Expenses for such year and collect from Tenant, as additional rent, one-twelfth (1/12) of Tenant\'s estimated pro rata share on a monthly basis, together with each monthly Base Rent payment. Within ninety (90) days after the end of each calendar year, Landlord shall furnish Tenant with a reasonably detailed statement of actual Operating Expenses for such year and Tenant\'s pro rata share thereof. If Tenant\'s payments on account of estimated Operating Expenses exceed Tenant\'s actual pro rata share, Landlord shall refund the overpayment to Tenant within thirty (30) days. If Tenant\'s payments are less than Tenant\'s actual pro rata share, Tenant shall pay the shortfall to Landlord within thirty (30) days of receipt of such statement.

**[ARTICLE 6 --- PERMITTED USE]{.underline}**

**6.1** Tenant shall use and occupy the Premises solely for the purposes of light industrial operations, warehousing, equipment storage, equipment testing, and the service, repair, maintenance, and reconditioning of fire safety equipment, fire extinguishers, fire suppression systems, and related safety apparatus, and for general office use incidental thereto, and for no other purpose without the prior written consent of Landlord, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed.

**6.2** Tenant shall comply with all Applicable Laws in connection with its use and occupancy of the Premises, including without limitation all applicable zoning ordinances, building codes, fire codes, health and safety regulations, and environmental laws and regulations, and shall obtain and maintain all permits and licenses required for the conduct of its business on the Premises.

**6.3** Tenant shall not use or occupy the Premises in any manner that would (a) increase the rate of or cause cancellation of any insurance policy maintained by Landlord on the Building, (b) constitute a nuisance or unreasonable disturbance to other tenants of Greystone Industrial Park, (c) violate any certificate of occupancy for the Premises or the Building, or (d) cause structural damage to the Building.

**[ARTICLE 7 --- INSURANCE]{.underline}**

**Section 7.1 --- Tenant\'s Insurance Obligations**

Tenant shall maintain at all times during the Term, at Tenant\'s sole cost and expense, the following insurance coverage:

> \(a\) **Commercial General Liability Insurance.** Commercial general liability insurance covering claims for bodily injury, death, personal injury, and property damage arising out of Tenant\'s use and occupancy of the Premises, with combined single limits of not less than Two Million Dollars (\$2,000,000) per occurrence and Five Million Dollars (\$5,000,000) in the aggregate per policy year.
>
> \(b\) **Pollution Legal Liability Insurance.** Pollution legal liability insurance with limits of not less than One Million Dollars (\$1,000,000) per occurrence, covering claims arising from the storage, handling, use, transportation, and disposal of fire suppressant chemicals, aqueous film-forming foam (\"AFFF\"), foam concentrates, and related materials on or about the Premises.
>
> \(c\) **Property Insurance.** All-risk property insurance covering Tenant\'s personal property, equipment, inventory, trade fixtures, and leasehold improvements in the Premises for their full replacement value.
>
> \(d\) **Workers\' Compensation Insurance.** Workers\' compensation insurance as required by the laws of the State of North Carolina, and employer\'s liability insurance with limits of not less than Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$500,000) per accident.

All insurance policies required under this Section 7.1 shall name Landlord, Thornfield Realty Holdings LP, Thornfield Management Corp., and their respective partners, officers, directors, employees, and agents as additional insureds (except for workers\' compensation insurance). All policies shall be written on an occurrence basis (not claims-made) by insurers licensed to do business in the State of North Carolina with an A.M. Best rating of not less than A-VII. Certificates of insurance evidencing the required coverage shall be delivered to Landlord prior to the Commencement Date and annually thereafter not later than ten (10) days prior to the expiration of each policy. Each policy shall provide that it may not be canceled or materially modified without at least thirty (30) days\' prior written notice to Landlord.

**Section 7.2 --- Landlord\'s Insurance**

Landlord shall maintain property insurance on the Building structure (excluding Tenant\'s personal property, equipment, and trade fixtures) and commercial general liability insurance covering the Common Areas of Greystone Industrial Park. The cost of such insurance shall be included in Operating Expenses and allocated to Tenant in accordance with Article 5.

**Section 7.3 --- Waiver of Subrogation**

Landlord and Tenant each hereby waive any right of recovery against the other party, and against the officers, directors, partners, employees, and agents of the other party, for any loss or damage to the extent that such loss or damage is covered by valid and collectible insurance in effect at the time of such loss or damage, or would have been covered by the insurance required to be maintained under this Lease. Each party shall cause its insurance carriers to include appropriate waiver of subrogation endorsements in all policies carried by such party in connection with the Premises and the Building.

**[ARTICLE 8 --- MAINTENANCE AND REPAIRS]{.underline}**

**Section 8.1 --- Tenant\'s Obligations**

Tenant shall, at Tenant\'s sole cost and expense, maintain the interior of the Premises in good condition, order, and repair throughout the Term, including without limitation all interior walls, floors, ceilings, doors, windows, plumbing fixtures and systems, electrical systems and wiring, lighting, interior fire suppression systems, and all HVAC equipment and systems serving the Premises. Tenant shall be responsible for all HVAC maintenance, including regular preventive maintenance service, filter replacement, coil cleaning, and all necessary repairs and replacements. Tenant shall maintain a service contract with a licensed HVAC contractor approved by Landlord (such approval not to be unreasonably withheld) and shall provide evidence of such service contract to Landlord upon request. Tenant shall keep all loading docks, bay doors, and the parking area dedicated to Unit 12 in clean, orderly, and safe condition, free of debris, obstructions, and environmental contamination.

**Section 8.2 --- Landlord\'s Obligations**

Landlord shall be responsible for the maintenance, repair, and replacement of the roof and structural elements of the Building, including the foundation, load-bearing walls, structural columns, and exterior walls (excluding glass, windows, and doors), provided that Landlord shall not be required to make any repairs or replacements necessitated by the negligence, willful misconduct, or misuse by Tenant, its employees, agents, contractors, or invitees. Landlord shall also maintain and repair Common Area infrastructure of Greystone Industrial Park, including parking lots, access drives, landscaping, exterior signage, stormwater drainage systems, and exterior lighting. The cost of such maintenance and repair shall be included in Operating Expenses and allocated in accordance with Article 5.

**[ARTICLE 9 --- ASSIGNMENT AND SUBLETTING]{.underline}**

**9.1** Tenant shall not assign, transfer, mortgage, pledge, hypothecate, or encumber this Lease or any interest therein, and shall not sublet the Premises or any part thereof, or grant any concession or license for the use of any portion of the Premises, without the prior written consent of Landlord, which consent may be withheld in Landlord\'s sole and absolute discretion. Any attempted assignment, subletting, or other transfer without Landlord\'s prior written consent shall be void and of no force or effect and shall constitute an Event of Default under this Lease.

**9.2** No assignment or subletting, whether with or without Landlord\'s consent, shall relieve Tenant of any of its obligations under this Lease, and Tenant shall remain primarily liable for the full and faithful performance of all covenants, conditions, and obligations of Tenant hereunder.

**9.3** In the event of any permitted assignment or subletting, any sublease rent, assignment consideration, or other amounts received by Tenant from the assignee or subtenant in excess of the Base Rent and additional rent then payable by Tenant under this Lease (after deducting Tenant\'s reasonable brokerage commissions and legal fees incurred in connection with such assignment or subletting) shall be paid over to Landlord promptly upon receipt.

**9.4** Landlord\'s consent to any one assignment or subletting shall not be deemed consent to any subsequent assignment or subletting, and each proposed transfer shall require a separate and independent consent.

**[ARTICLE 10 --- ALTERATIONS AND IMPROVEMENTS]{.underline}**

**10.1** Tenant shall not make any structural alterations, additions, or improvements to the Premises without Landlord\'s prior written consent, which consent may be granted or withheld in Landlord\'s reasonable discretion. All requests for consent to structural alterations shall be accompanied by detailed plans and specifications prepared by a licensed architect or engineer.

**10.2** Non-structural alterations, additions, or improvements with an estimated cost of less than Twenty-Five Thousand Dollars (\$25,000) may be made by Tenant without Landlord\'s prior written consent, provided that Tenant delivers written notice to Landlord describing the scope and estimated cost of such work at least fifteen (15) days in advance of commencing such work. All alterations shall be performed in a good and workmanlike manner, in compliance with all Applicable Laws, and shall not adversely affect the structural integrity or systems of the Building.

**10.3** All alterations, additions, and improvements made to the Premises by Tenant (excluding Tenant\'s trade fixtures, equipment, and movable personal property) shall become the property of Landlord upon installation and shall remain upon the Premises at the expiration or earlier termination of this Lease, unless Landlord elects to require their removal by written notice delivered to Tenant not later than thirty (30) days prior to the Expiration Date. Tenant\'s trade fixtures, equipment, and movable personal property shall remain the property of Tenant and shall be removed by Tenant upon the expiration or earlier termination of this Lease, provided that Tenant shall repair any damage to the Premises caused by such removal.

**[ARTICLE 11 --- INDEMNIFICATION AND LIABILITY]{.underline}**

**Section 11.1 --- Tenant\'s Indemnification**

Tenant shall indemnify, defend (with counsel reasonably acceptable to Landlord), and hold harmless Landlord and its partners, members, officers, directors, agents, employees, contractors, successors, and assigns from and against any and all claims, demands, actions, causes of action, losses, damages, liabilities, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys\' fees and court costs) arising from or related to: (a) Tenant\'s use and occupancy of the Premises; (b) any act, omission, negligence, or willful misconduct of Tenant, its employees, agents, contractors, licensees, or invitees in or about the Premises, the Building, or Greystone Industrial Park; (c) any breach or default by Tenant under this Lease; or (d) any environmental contamination of the Premises, the Building, Greystone Industrial Park, or any adjacent or nearby property caused by or attributable to Tenant\'s storage, use, handling, release, or disposal of Hazardous Materials, as more particularly described in Article 14. This indemnification obligation shall survive the expiration or earlier termination of this Lease.

**Section 11.2 --- Landlord\'s Indemnification**

Landlord shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Tenant and its officers, directors, employees, and agents from and against any and all claims, losses, damages, liabilities, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys\' fees) arising from Landlord\'s negligence or willful misconduct in connection with Landlord\'s performance of its obligations under this Lease, except to the extent such claims arise from the negligence or willful misconduct of Tenant.

**Section 11.3 --- Limitation of Liability**

In no event shall Landlord\'s liability under this Lease exceed Landlord\'s equity interest in the Building and the proceeds thereof. Tenant shall look solely to Landlord\'s interest in the Building for the satisfaction of any claim or judgment against Landlord, and no other property or assets of Landlord, its partners, members, officers, directors, or agents shall be subject to levy, execution, or other enforcement procedure for the satisfaction of Tenant\'s remedies. In no event shall either party be liable to the other for consequential, incidental, special, or punitive damages in connection with this Lease.

**[ARTICLE 12 --- DEFAULT AND REMEDIES]{.underline}**

**Section 12.1 --- Events of Default**

Each of the following shall constitute an \"Event of Default\" under this Lease:

> \(a\) Tenant fails to pay Base Rent, additional rent, or any other sum due under this Lease within five (5) days after the date on which such payment is due;
>
> \(b\) Tenant fails to perform or observe any other covenant, condition, or obligation of Tenant under this Lease and such failure continues for thirty (30) days after Landlord delivers written notice thereof to Tenant, provided that if such default is of a nature that it cannot reasonably be cured within thirty (30) days, Tenant shall not be in default if Tenant commences the cure within such thirty (30) day period and diligently and continuously pursues the cure to completion;
>
> \(c\) Tenant files a voluntary petition in bankruptcy or is adjudicated bankrupt or insolvent, or makes a general assignment for the benefit of creditors, or a receiver or trustee is appointed for all or substantially all of Tenant\'s assets, or any proceeding is filed by or against Tenant under any bankruptcy or insolvency law and is not dismissed within sixty (60) days;
>
> \(d\) Tenant abandons the Premises or vacates the Premises for a period of thirty (30) or more consecutive days without Landlord\'s prior written consent; or
>
> \(e\) Any representation or warranty made by Tenant in this Lease is materially false or misleading when made.

**Section 12.2 --- Landlord\'s Remedies**

Upon the occurrence of any Event of Default, Landlord shall have the right, at Landlord\'s sole election, to exercise one or more of the following remedies:

> \(a\) Terminate this Lease by delivering written notice of termination to Tenant, whereupon Tenant\'s right to possession of the Premises shall cease and Tenant shall immediately surrender the Premises to Landlord;
>
> \(b\) Re-enter and take possession of the Premises, with or without terminating this Lease, and remove Tenant and all persons and property therefrom, in accordance with applicable North Carolina law;
>
> \(c\) Recover from Tenant all damages incurred by Landlord as a result of such default, including without limitation all unpaid Base Rent and additional rent accrued through the date of termination, the present value of all Base Rent and additional rent that would have been payable during the remainder of the Term (discounted at the rate of six percent (6%) per annum), all costs of re-letting the Premises (including brokerage commissions, tenant improvement costs, and advertising expenses), and all other damages recoverable by Landlord at law or in equity; and
>
> \(d\) Exercise any other remedies available to Landlord at law or in equity, including the right to seek specific performance or injunctive relief.

Landlord\'s remedies under this Lease are cumulative and not exclusive, and the exercise of any one remedy shall not preclude the exercise of any other remedy.

**Section 12.3 --- Tenant\'s Remedies**

If Landlord defaults in the performance of any obligation of Landlord under this Lease, Tenant shall deliver written notice of such default to Landlord specifying the nature of the default in reasonable detail, and Landlord shall have thirty (30) days after receipt of such notice within which to cure such default (or, if the default is of a nature that cannot reasonably be cured within thirty (30) days, such longer period as is reasonably necessary, provided Landlord commences the cure within such thirty (30) day period and diligently pursues the same to completion). If Landlord fails to cure such default within the applicable cure period, Tenant may pursue any remedies available at law or in equity; provided, however, that in no event shall Tenant have the right to terminate this Lease or to withhold, abate, or offset any rent or other amounts payable under this Lease on account of any Landlord default, except as expressly permitted by applicable North Carolina law.

**[ARTICLE 13 --- HOLDOVER]{.underline}**

If Tenant remains in possession of the Premises after the Expiration Date or earlier termination of this Lease without Landlord\'s prior written consent, Tenant shall be deemed a holdover tenant on a month-to-month basis, subject to all of the terms and conditions of this Lease, except as modified by this Article 13. During any holdover period, Tenant shall pay holdover rent equal to one hundred fifty percent (150%) of the Base Rent payable during the last month of the Term. Based on the final month\'s Base Rent of \$16,958.33 per month, holdover rent shall be \$25,437.50 per month, payable in advance on the first day of each calendar month during the holdover period, together with all additional rent and other charges payable under this Lease.

All other terms and conditions of this Lease shall continue to apply during any holdover period, except that the holdover tenancy may be terminated by either party upon thirty (30) days\' prior written notice to the other party. Landlord\'s acceptance of holdover rent shall not constitute a consent to any renewal or extension of the Term and shall not waive Landlord\'s right to terminate the holdover tenancy or to recover possession of the Premises at any time. Tenant shall be liable for all damages, costs, and expenses incurred by Landlord as a result of Tenant\'s holdover occupancy, including without limitation any loss of prospective tenants or rental income.

**[ARTICLE 14 --- HAZARDOUS MATERIALS AND ENVIRONMENTAL PROVISIONS]{.underline}**

**Section 14.1 --- Definitions**

As used in this Lease, \"Hazardous Materials\" shall mean any substance, chemical, material, compound, mixture, or waste that is regulated by, or forms the basis of liability under, any federal, state, or local environmental law, regulation, ordinance, rule, or order, including but not limited to: (a) substances defined as \"hazardous substances,\" \"hazardous materials,\" \"hazardous wastes,\" or \"toxic substances\" under the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act (\"CERCLA\") (42 U.S.C. § 9601 et seq.), the Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (\"RCRA\") (42 U.S.C. § 6901 et seq.), the Toxic Substances Control Act (15 U.S.C. § 2601 et seq.), or any state equivalent thereof, including the North Carolina Hazardous Waste Management Act and the North Carolina Oil Pollution and Hazardous Substances Control Act; (b) petroleum and petroleum products, including crude oil and any fraction thereof; (c) polychlorinated biphenyls (\"PCBs\"); (d) per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (\"PFAS\"), including without limitation perfluorooctanoic acid (\"PFOA\") and perfluorooctane sulfonate (\"PFOS\"); (e) aqueous film-forming foam (\"AFFF\") and fire suppressant concentrates containing fluorinated surfactants; and (f) any other substance that is classified as hazardous, toxic, or dangerous under any Applicable Law.

**Section 14.2 --- Permitted Use of Hazardous Materials**

Notwithstanding any other provision of this Lease restricting the use of Hazardous Materials on the Premises, Tenant shall be permitted to store, handle, use, and transport fire suppressant chemicals, including aqueous film-forming foam (\"AFFF\"), foam concentrates, dry chemical agents, and related fire safety materials, on the Premises in connection with Tenant\'s business operations as described in Article 6, provided that such storage, handling, use, and transportation shall at all times be conducted in strict compliance with all Applicable Laws, including without limitation all federal, state, and local environmental laws and regulations governing the storage, handling, use, transportation, and disposal of Hazardous Materials, PFAS, and AFFF. Tenant shall obtain and maintain all permits, licenses, and approvals required by any governmental authority for the storage, handling, use, and disposal of such materials on the Premises. Tenant shall maintain a current and accurate inventory of all Hazardous Materials stored on the Premises and shall provide a copy of such inventory to Landlord upon Landlord\'s written request, but in any event not less than annually. Tenant shall also provide Landlord with copies of all Material Safety Data Sheets (\"MSDS\") or Safety Data Sheets (\"SDS\") for all Hazardous Materials stored or used on the Premises, promptly upon Landlord\'s request.

**Section 14.3 --- Tenant\'s Environmental Indemnification**

Tenant shall indemnify, defend (with counsel reasonably acceptable to Landlord), and hold harmless Landlord and its partners, officers, directors, agents, employees, successors, and assigns from and against any and all claims, demands, actions, causes of action, losses, damages, liabilities, penalties, fines, costs, and expenses (including without limitation reasonable attorneys\' fees, environmental consultant and engineering fees, investigation costs, and remediation and cleanup costs) arising from or related to any environmental contamination of the Premises, the Building, Greystone Industrial Park, or any adjacent, nearby, or downgradient property, to the extent caused by or attributable to Tenant\'s storage, use, handling, generation, release, discharge, spill, or disposal of Hazardous Materials, including without limitation AFFF, foam concentrates, and PFAS-containing materials. This environmental indemnification obligation shall survive the expiration or earlier termination of this Lease and shall not be limited by any other indemnification provisions set forth herein.

**Section 14.4 --- Remediation**

If, at any time during the Term or after the expiration or termination of this Lease, any release, discharge, spill, or contamination of Hazardous Materials is discovered on, under, or about the Premises, the Building, or Greystone Industrial Park that was caused by or attributable to Tenant, Tenant\'s employees, agents, contractors, or invitees, Tenant shall promptly, at Tenant\'s sole cost and expense, investigate, remediate, and clean up such contamination to the satisfaction of all applicable governmental authorities having jurisdiction and to the reasonable satisfaction of Landlord, in accordance with all Applicable Laws. Landlord shall have the right, at Landlord\'s cost, to conduct environmental assessments, inspections, and testing of the Premises at any reasonable time during the Term upon reasonable prior notice to Tenant; provided, however, that if any such assessment reveals contamination attributable to Tenant, Tenant shall reimburse Landlord for the reasonable cost of such assessment within thirty (30) days of Landlord\'s written demand therefor.

**Section 14.5 --- Compliance**

Tenant shall comply with all environmental laws and regulations applicable to Tenant\'s operations on the Premises throughout the Term, including without limitation all laws and regulations governing PFAS, AFFF, fire suppressant chemicals, and the storage, handling, use, and disposal thereof, as the same may be enacted, amended, or modified from time to time. Tenant shall promptly notify Landlord in writing of any known or suspected release of Hazardous Materials on or from the Premises, any notice of violation received from any governmental authority, or any environmental claim, action, or proceeding relating to the Premises.

**[ARTICLE 15 --- CASUALTY AND CONDEMNATION]{.underline}**

**Section 15.1 --- Casualty**

If the Premises are damaged or destroyed by fire or other casualty, Landlord shall promptly notify Tenant of Landlord\'s good-faith estimate of the time required to restore the Premises. If the damage is such that the Premises are rendered substantially untenantable, Landlord may, at Landlord\'s election, either (a) restore the Premises to substantially the same condition as existed immediately prior to the casualty, using commercially reasonable efforts to complete such restoration within one hundred eighty (180) days after the date of the casualty, or (b) terminate this Lease by delivering written notice of termination to Tenant within sixty (60) days after the date of the casualty. If Landlord elects to restore and restoration cannot reasonably be completed within one hundred eighty (180) days, either party may terminate this Lease by written notice to the other delivered within thirty (30) days after the expiration of such one hundred eighty (180) day period. During any period in which the Premises are untenantable as a result of casualty damage, Base Rent and additional rent shall abate in proportion to the area of the Premises rendered untenantable.

**Section 15.2 --- Condemnation**

If all or substantially all of the Premises are taken by eminent domain or condemnation by any governmental authority, this Lease shall terminate as of the date of such taking and all rent shall be apportioned as of such date. If a partial taking of the Premises does not render the remaining portion of the Premises unsuitable for Tenant\'s continued use, this Lease shall continue in effect with a proportionate reduction in Base Rent corresponding to the area taken. All condemnation awards and proceeds shall belong exclusively to Landlord, provided that Tenant shall have the right to make a separate claim against the condemning authority for the value of Tenant\'s trade fixtures and personal property and for Tenant\'s reasonable relocation expenses, to the extent such separate claim does not diminish the award otherwise payable to Landlord.

**[ARTICLE 16 --- SUBORDINATION]{.underline}**

This Lease shall be subject and subordinate to any mortgage, deed of trust, ground lease, or other lien or encumbrance now existing or hereafter placed upon the Building, the land on which the Building is situated, or Greystone Industrial Park, and to all renewals, modifications, consolidations, replacements, and extensions thereof. This subordination shall be self-operative, and no further instrument shall be required to effect such subordination. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Tenant agrees to execute promptly such documents as may be reasonably required by Landlord or any mortgagee or beneficiary under any deed of trust to evidence or confirm such subordination, and Tenant hereby irrevocably appoints Landlord as Tenant\'s attorney-in-fact to execute any such document on Tenant\'s behalf if Tenant fails to do so within ten (10) days after written request.

**[ARTICLE 17 --- NOTICES]{.underline}**

All notices, demands, consents, approvals, requests, and other communications required or permitted under this Lease shall be in writing and shall be deemed duly given and received if delivered by any of the following methods:

> \(a\) Personal delivery, in which case notice shall be deemed effective upon delivery;
>
> \(b\) Nationally recognized overnight courier service (such as FedEx, UPS, or DHL), in which case notice shall be deemed effective on the next business day following deposit with such courier; or
>
> \(c\) Certified mail, return receipt requested, postage prepaid, deposited in the United States mail, in which case notice shall be deemed effective three (3) business days after deposit.

Notices shall be addressed as follows:

**If to Landlord:**

> Thornfield Realty Holdings LP
>
> Attn: Property Manager
>
> 500 South Tryon Street, Suite 2200 Charlotte, NC 28202

**If to Tenant:**

> Southeastern Fire & Safety Equipment Co. 770 Greystone Boulevard, Unit 12 Gastonia, NC 28052

Either party may change its address for notices by delivering written notice of such change to the other party in accordance with this Article 17.

**[ARTICLE 18 --- MISCELLANEOUS]{.underline}**

**Section 18.1 --- Entire Agreement**

This Lease, together with all Exhibits attached hereto and incorporated herein by reference, constitutes the entire agreement between the parties with respect to the subject matter hereof and supersedes all prior and contemporaneous agreements, representations, warranties, and understandings, whether oral or written, between the parties relating to the Premises or the leasing thereof. No prior oral or written agreement, representation, or understanding shall have any force or effect.

**Section 18.2 --- Amendments**

This Lease may not be amended, modified, supplemented, or waived except by a written instrument executed by both Landlord and Tenant. No oral agreement or course of dealing shall operate as an amendment or modification of this Lease.

**Section 18.3 --- Governing Law**

This Lease shall be governed by, construed under, and enforced in accordance with the laws of the State of North Carolina, without regard to its conflicts of law principles. The parties consent to the exclusive jurisdiction and venue of the state and federal courts located in Gaston County or Mecklenburg County, North Carolina, for any dispute arising under or in connection with this Lease.

**Section 18.4 --- Severability**

If any provision of this Lease is held by a court of competent jurisdiction to be invalid, illegal, void, or unenforceable, such provision shall be modified to the minimum extent necessary to make it valid and enforceable, or if it cannot be so modified, it shall be severed from this Lease, and the remaining provisions of this Lease shall continue in full force and effect and shall not be affected or impaired thereby.

**Section 18.5 --- Binding Effect**

This Lease shall be binding upon and inure to the benefit of the parties hereto and their respective heirs, executors, administrators, legal representatives, successors, and permitted assigns. Nothing in this Lease shall be construed to confer any rights or benefits upon any person or entity other than the parties hereto and their respective successors and permitted assigns.

**Section 18.6 --- No Waiver**

No failure or delay by either party in exercising any right, power, or remedy under this Lease shall operate as a waiver thereof. No single or partial exercise of any right, power, or remedy shall preclude any other or further exercise thereof or the exercise of any other right, power, or remedy. No waiver of any provision of this Lease shall be effective unless made in writing and signed by the party to be charged with such waiver.

**Section 18.7 --- Quiet Enjoyment**

Landlord covenants and agrees that, so long as Tenant is not in default under this Lease beyond any applicable notice and cure period, Tenant shall peaceably and quietly hold, occupy, and enjoy the Premises during the Term, free from interference by Landlord or any person claiming by, through, or under Landlord, subject to the terms and conditions of this Lease and to any mortgage, deed of trust, or other encumbrance to which this Lease is subordinate.

**Section 18.8 --- Broker**

Each party hereby represents and warrants to the other that it has not dealt with any real estate broker, finder, or agent in connection with this Lease or the negotiation thereof, and each party shall indemnify and hold harmless the other from and against any claim for brokerage commission, finder\'s fee, or similar compensation arising from a breach of such representation.

**Section 18.9 --- Counterparts**

This Lease may be executed in two or more counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original and all of which together shall constitute one and the same instrument. Facsimile and electronic signatures shall be deemed original signatures for all purposes.

**[ARTICLE IV --- BASE RENT]{.underline}**

**Section 4.01 --- Payment of Base Rent.** Commencing on the Commencement Date, Tenant shall pay to Landlord Base Rent in equal monthly installments, in advance, on or before the first (1st) day of each calendar month during the Lease Term, without prior notice, demand, deduction, abatement, or set-off, except as expressly provided in this Lease.

**Section 4.02 --- Base Rent Amount.** Base Rent for the first Lease Year (July 1, 2022, through June 30, 2023) shall be Thirty-Four and 00/100 Dollars (\$34.00) per RSF per annum, which equals Six Hundred Thirty-Seven Thousand Five Hundred and 00/100 Dollars (\$637,500.00) per annum, payable in monthly installments of Fifty-Three Thousand One Hundred Twenty-Five and 00/100 Dollars (\$53,125.00).

**Section 4.03 --- Annual Escalation.** On each anniversary of the Commencement Date (i.e., commencing July 1, 2023), the Base Rent rate per RSF per annum shall increase by three percent (3%) over the Base Rent rate in effect for the immediately preceding Lease Year, calculated on a compounded annual basis. The full Rent Schedule, setting forth the Base Rent for each Lease Year during the Lease Term, is attached hereto as **Exhibit B** and incorporated herein by this reference.

**Section 4.04 --- Partial Month Proration.** If the Commencement Date falls on a day other than the first day of a calendar month, Base Rent for such partial month shall be prorated on a per diem basis (based on the actual number of days in such month). As the Commencement Date is July 1, 2022, no proration shall be required for the initial month.

**Section 4.05 --- Late Payment Fee.** If any installment of Base Rent or Additional Rent is not received by Landlord within five (5) business days after the date such payment is due, Tenant shall pay a late charge equal to five percent (5%) of the overdue amount. The parties agree that such late charge represents a reasonable estimate of the costs Landlord will incur as a result of late payment.

**Section 4.06 --- Interest on Past-Due Amounts.** Any amount owed by Tenant under this Lease that remains unpaid for more than ten (10) days after the date due shall bear interest from the date due until paid at the lesser of (a) one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month (18% per annum) or (b) the maximum rate permitted by the laws of the State of Georgia.

**Section 4.07 --- Place of Payment.** All rent and other sums payable by Tenant under this Lease shall be paid to Landlord at the address specified in Article I, or at such other address as Landlord may designate in writing from time to time.

**[ARTICLE V --- OPERATING EXPENSES AND EXPENSE STOP]{.underline}**

**Section 5.01 --- Full-Service Gross Lease.** This Lease is a full-service gross lease with a Base Year expense stop. Landlord shall pay all Operating Expenses for the Building during the Lease Term. However, commencing January 1, 2023, Tenant shall pay, as Additional Rent, Tenant\'s Pro Rata Share (12.50%) of the amount by which actual Operating Expenses for any calendar year exceed the Operating Expenses incurred during the Base Year (Calendar Year 2022) (the \"Expense Stop\").

**Section 5.02 --- Definition of Operating Expenses.** \"Operating Expenses\" shall mean all costs and expenses of every kind and nature incurred by Landlord in the ownership, operation, management, maintenance, and repair of the Building, the common areas, and the land upon which the Building is situated, including without limitation: (a) real estate taxes, assessments (general and special), and governmental charges levied upon the Building; (b) insurance premiums for all insurance maintained by Landlord on the Building; (c) utility costs, including electricity, gas, water, sewer, and trash removal for common areas and base building systems; (d) janitorial services and supplies; (e) landscaping and groundskeeping; (f) security services and systems; (g) management fees, not to exceed four percent (4%) of the Building\'s gross revenues; (h) repairs, maintenance, and replacement of Building systems, including HVAC, elevators, plumbing, and electrical systems; (i) common area maintenance; (j) reasonable reserves for capital replacements as determined by Landlord in its reasonable discretion; and (k) all other costs reasonably incurred in the operation of the Building consistent with the operation of comparable Class A office buildings in the Atlanta midtown submarket.

**Section 5.03 --- Exclusions from Operating Expenses.** The following shall be excluded from Operating Expenses: (a) capital improvements, except those mandated by governmental laws, codes, or regulations enacted after the Base Year or those which are reasonably expected to reduce Operating Expenses, in either case amortized over their useful life with interest at eight percent (8%) per annum; (b) leasing commissions, advertising costs, and tenant procurement expenses; (c) tenant improvement costs, allowances, or concessions for other tenants; (d) costs reimbursed by insurance proceeds or condemnation awards; (e) depreciation of the Building; (f) debt service, including mortgage principal and interest payments; (g) Landlord\'s federal, state, or local income taxes; (h) costs arising from Landlord\'s negligence or willful misconduct; (i) costs of correcting defects in original construction; and (j) legal fees incurred in disputes with tenants.

**Section 5.04 --- Estimated Payments.** Landlord shall provide Tenant with a good-faith estimate of Tenant\'s share of Operating Expense increases for each calendar year prior to or at the beginning of such year. Tenant shall pay one-twelfth (1/12) of such estimated amount monthly, concurrently with Base Rent. Landlord may revise such estimate from time to time during the calendar year upon reasonable notice to Tenant.

**Section 5.05 --- Annual Reconciliation.** Within one hundred twenty (120) days after the end of each calendar year, Landlord shall provide Tenant with a reasonably detailed statement (the \"Annual Statement\") setting forth the actual Operating Expenses for such calendar year and a calculation of Tenant\'s share. If Tenant\'s estimated payments exceed Tenant\'s actual share, Landlord shall credit the overpayment against Tenant\'s next monthly installment(s) of Additional Rent (or refund such amount if the Lease has expired). If Tenant\'s estimated payments are less than Tenant\'s actual share, Tenant shall pay the shortfall within thirty (30) days after receipt of the Annual Statement.

**Section 5.06 --- Audit Right.** Tenant shall have the right, at Tenant\'s sole cost and expense, to audit Landlord\'s books and records relating to Operating Expenses for any calendar year, upon not less than thirty (30) days\' prior written notice to Landlord, exercised within twelve (12) months after Tenant\'s receipt of the Annual Statement for such year. Such audit shall be conducted during normal business hours at Landlord\'s office or at the office of Landlord\'s property manager. If the audit reveals that Landlord has overcharged Tenant by more than five percent (5%) for the audited year, Landlord shall reimburse Tenant for Tenant\'s reasonable out-of-pocket audit costs, in addition to refunding the overpayment. In no event shall Tenant engage an auditor compensated on a contingency fee basis.

**Section 5.07 --- Controllable Expense Cap.** Landlord\'s controllable operating expenses --- defined as all Operating Expenses other than real estate taxes, insurance premiums, utilities, and snow/ice removal --- shall not increase by more than five percent (5%) per annum on a cumulative, compounding basis over the amount of such controllable operating expenses incurred during the Base Year.

**Section 5.08 --- Gross-Up Provision.** If the Building is less than ninety-five percent (95%) occupied during any calendar year (including the Base Year), Operating Expenses that vary with occupancy shall be adjusted (\"grossed up\") to reflect the Operating Expenses that would have been incurred had the Building been ninety-five percent (95%) occupied for the entire calendar year.

**[ARTICLE VI --- USE OF PREMISES]{.underline}**

**Section 6.01 --- Permitted Use.** Tenant shall use and occupy the Premises solely for general office purposes, software development, and ancillary uses reasonably related thereto (the \"Permitted Use\"), and for no other purpose without Landlord\'s prior written consent.

**Section 6.02 --- Prohibited Uses.** Tenant shall not use the Premises for any purpose that (a) violates any applicable federal, state, or local law, ordinance, regulation, or code; (b) creates a nuisance or unreasonable disturbance to other occupants of the Building; (c) increases Landlord\'s insurance premiums for the Building, unless Tenant agrees to pay any such increase; or (d) violates the Building\'s rules and regulations as set forth in Exhibit E.

**Section 6.03 --- Compliance with Laws.** Tenant shall comply with all applicable federal, state, and local laws, ordinances, regulations, and codes relating to its use and occupancy of the Premises, including without limitation the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990, as amended, and all regulations promulgated thereunder.

**Section 6.04 --- Hazardous Materials.** Tenant shall not generate, store, treat, or dispose of hazardous materials on the Premises or in the Building, except for customary office supplies and cleaning products used in the ordinary course of business in compliance with all applicable environmental laws.

**[ARTICLE VII --- TENANT IMPROVEMENTS]{.underline}**

**Section 7.01 --- Tenant Improvement Allowance.** Landlord shall provide Tenant with a tenant improvement allowance (the \"TI Allowance\") in the amount of Fifty-Five and 00/100 Dollars (\$55.00) per RSF of the Premises, for a total of One Million Thirty-One Thousand Two Hundred Fifty and 00/100 Dollars (\$1,031,250.00). The TI Allowance shall be applied toward the cost of designing and constructing Tenant\'s initial improvements to the Premises in accordance with the Work Letter attached hereto as **Exhibit C**.

**Section 7.02 --- Disbursement.** The TI Allowance shall be disbursed in accordance with the procedures set forth in the Work Letter (Exhibit C). Any costs of Tenant\'s improvements that exceed the TI Allowance shall be borne solely by Tenant.

**Section 7.03 --- Unused Allowance.** Any unused portion of the TI Allowance remaining after the completion of Tenant\'s improvements shall not be paid to Tenant as cash, credited against Base Rent or Additional Rent, or otherwise refunded. Any such unused portion shall be forfeited and retained by Landlord.

**Section 7.04 --- Amortization for Recapture.** For the purpose of calculating any recapture amounts payable by Tenant upon early termination of this Lease or contraction of the Premises pursuant to Article XIV, the TI Allowance shall be amortized over the initial ten (10) year Lease Term at a rate of seven percent (7%) per annum, with the full amount of \$1,031,250.00 as the initial principal balance. The unamortized balance at any point during the Lease Term shall be determined using a standard mortgage-style amortization schedule with equal monthly payments based on a seven percent (7%) annual interest rate and a one-hundred-twenty (120) month amortization period. For purposes of calculating the contraction fee under Article XIV, the amortization of the TI Allowance allocable to the Contraction Space shall be calculated in the same manner, using \$55.00 per RSF of the Contraction Space as the initial principal.

**Section 7.05 --- Ownership of Improvements.** All Tenant Improvements constructed with the TI Allowance, once installed, shall become the property of Landlord and shall remain upon the Premises at the expiration or earlier termination of this Lease; provided, however, that Landlord may require Tenant to remove any non-standard improvements or specialty installations designated by Landlord in writing at the time of Landlord\'s approval of Tenant\'s construction plans, and Tenant shall restore the affected areas to their condition prior to the installation of such improvements.

**[ARTICLE VIII --- MAINTENANCE AND REPAIRS]{.underline}**

**Section 8.01 --- Landlord\'s Obligations.** Landlord shall maintain and repair, at Landlord\'s expense (subject to inclusion in Operating Expenses), the structural components of the Building (including roof, foundation, and exterior walls), base building systems (including base building HVAC, elevators, plumbing, and electrical systems), common areas, and the Building\'s exterior. Landlord shall provide the following standard building services: (a) heating, ventilation, and air conditioning during business hours (8:00 AM to 6:00 PM, Monday through Friday, and 8:00 AM to 1:00 PM, Saturday, excluding Building holidays); (b) janitorial service for the Premises five (5) nights per week; and (c) passenger elevator service.

**Section 8.02 --- Tenant\'s Obligations.** Tenant shall maintain the interior of the Premises in good condition and repair throughout the Lease Term, including all of Tenant\'s furniture, fixtures, equipment, supplemental HVAC units or other specialized systems installed by or for Tenant, and any improvements or alterations constructed by Tenant. Tenant shall promptly notify Landlord of any condition in the Premises requiring repair by Landlord.

**Section 8.03 --- After-Hours HVAC.** After-hours HVAC service shall be available to Tenant upon request at a rate of Seventy-Five and 00/100 Dollars (\$75.00) per hour per zone, subject to annual adjustment by Landlord based on actual utility costs. Tenant shall request after-hours HVAC by providing reasonable advance notice to Landlord\'s building management office.

**[ARTICLE IX --- INSURANCE]{.underline}**

**Section 9.01 --- Tenant\'s Insurance.** Tenant shall, at Tenant\'s sole cost, obtain and maintain throughout the Lease Term the following insurance coverages: (a) Commercial General Liability insurance with limits of not less than \$1,000,000 per occurrence and \$3,000,000 in the aggregate; (b) Workers\' Compensation insurance as required by the laws of the State of Georgia, and Employers\' Liability insurance with a limit of not less than \$500,000; (c) Business Personal Property insurance covering Tenant\'s furniture, fixtures, equipment, and other personal property at full replacement cost; and (d) Business Interruption insurance sufficient to cover not less than twelve (12) months of Base Rent and Additional Rent.

**Section 9.02 --- Landlord\'s Insurance.** Landlord shall maintain property insurance on the Building on an all-risk or special-form basis, commercial general liability insurance, and such other insurance as Landlord deems reasonably necessary. The cost of Landlord\'s insurance shall be included in Operating Expenses.

**Section 9.03 --- Mutual Waiver of Subrogation.** Landlord and Tenant each hereby waive any right of recovery against the other party for any loss or damage to the extent covered (or required to be covered) by such party\'s property insurance policies. Each party shall cause its insurer to issue appropriate waiver of subrogation endorsements.

**Section 9.04 --- Additional Insured.** Tenant\'s commercial general liability policy shall name Landlord, Landlord\'s managing agent, and their respective officers, directors, partners, and employees as additional insureds. All policies shall be issued by carriers rated A-VII or better by A.M. Best.

**Section 9.05 --- Certificates.** Tenant shall deliver certificates of insurance to Landlord prior to the Commencement Date (or the commencement of early access) and annually thereafter, and upon each renewal or replacement of coverage.

**[ARTICLE X --- INDEMNIFICATION AND LIABILITY]{.underline}**

**Section 10.01 --- Tenant\'s Indemnification.** Tenant shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Landlord and its partners, officers, directors, agents, and employees from and against any and all claims, damages, losses, liabilities, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys\' fees) arising from (a) Tenant\'s use and occupancy of the Premises, (b) any negligence or willful misconduct of Tenant or its agents, employees, contractors, or invitees, or (c) any breach by Tenant of its obligations under this Lease.

**Section 10.02 --- Landlord\'s Indemnification.** Landlord shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Tenant and its officers, directors, agents, and employees from and against any and all claims, damages, losses, liabilities, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys\' fees) arising from Landlord\'s negligence or willful misconduct.

**Section 10.03 --- Limitation of Damages.** In no event shall either party be liable to the other for consequential, incidental, special, or punitive damages arising out of or in connection with this Lease.

**Section 10.04 --- Interruption of Services.** Landlord shall not be liable for any interruption or cessation of services or utilities provided to the Premises, except to the extent caused by Landlord\'s gross negligence or willful misconduct. Any rent abatement in connection with such interruption shall be governed by the applicable provisions of this Lease.

**[ARTICLE XI --- ASSIGNMENT AND SUBLETTING]{.underline}**

**Section 11.01 --- General Restriction.** Tenant shall not assign this Lease or sublet all or any portion of the Premises without Landlord\'s prior written consent, except as expressly provided in this Article XI. Any purported assignment or subletting in violation of this Article shall be void and of no force or effect and shall constitute an Event of Default under this Lease.

**Section 11.02 --- Subletting Without Consent (40% Threshold).** Notwithstanding Section 11.01, Tenant may sublet up to forty percent (40%) of the rentable square footage of the Premises (i.e., up to 7,500 RSF) without obtaining Landlord\'s prior written consent, provided that all of the following conditions are satisfied:

> \(a\) the proposed subtenant is engaged in a use consistent with the Permitted Use as defined in this Lease;
>
> \(b\) the proposed subtenant is not a governmental entity, and is not a person or entity that is an existing tenant of the Building or a prospective tenant with whom Landlord is then in active lease negotiations;
>
> \(c\) Tenant provides Landlord with written notice of the sublease, together with a complete copy of the executed sublease agreement and reasonable financial and background information regarding the proposed subtenant, within ten (10) business days after Tenant\'s execution of the sublease; and
>
> \(d\) Tenant shall remain fully and primarily liable under this Lease for all obligations, including the payment of all rent and the performance of all other covenants and conditions.

**Section 11.03 --- Subletting Above 40%.** Any subletting of more than forty percent (40%) of the rentable square footage of the Premises shall require Landlord\'s prior written consent, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed. Landlord shall respond to Tenant\'s written request for consent within twenty (20) business days after Landlord\'s receipt of all required information, including a copy of the proposed sublease, financial statements of the proposed subtenant, and a description of the proposed subtenant\'s intended use. Failure by Landlord to respond within such twenty (20) business day period shall be deemed consent.

**Section 11.04 --- Profit-Sharing on Subletting.** In connection with any subletting of the Premises (whether or not Landlord\'s consent is required pursuant to Sections 11.02 or 11.03), Landlord shall be entitled to receive fifty percent (50%) of all Subletting Profits realized by Tenant. For purposes of this Section, \"Subletting Profits\" shall mean the excess, if any, of (a) the aggregate rent and other monetary consideration payable by the subtenant to Tenant under the sublease, over (b) the Base Rent and Additional Rent payable by Tenant under this Lease allocable to the sublet space (determined on a per-RSF basis), after deducting Tenant\'s reasonable, documented, out-of-pocket costs actually incurred in connection with such subletting, including brokerage commissions, legal fees, and the cost of any tenant improvement work performed by Tenant in the sublet space, all amortized on a straight-line basis over the term of the sublease. Subletting Profits shall be calculated and paid to Landlord on a monthly basis. Tenant shall provide Landlord with a detailed accounting of Subletting Profits, including supporting documentation, within thirty (30) days after the end of each calendar quarter during the term of any sublease.

**Section 11.05 --- Assignment.** Any assignment of this Lease, whether voluntarily or by operation of law, shall require Landlord\'s prior written consent, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed. In the event of any approved assignment, the original Tenant named herein (as assignor) shall remain secondarily liable for all obligations under this Lease for the remainder of the Lease Term, unless Landlord agrees in writing to release Tenant from such liability.

**Section 11.06 --- Affiliate Transfers.** Notwithstanding Sections 11.01 and 11.05, Tenant may assign this Lease or sublet all or any portion of the Premises to an Affiliate without Landlord\'s prior consent. For purposes of this Section, \"Affiliate\" means any entity that controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with Tenant, where \"control\" means the direct or indirect ownership of more than fifty percent (50%) of the voting securities or equivalent ownership interests of such entity. Any such Affiliate transfer shall be subject to the following conditions: (a) the Affiliate has a tangible net worth, as of the effective date of such transfer, at least equal to Tenant\'s tangible net worth as of the Lease Date; and (b) Tenant provides Landlord with written notice of such transfer at least fifteen (15) days prior to the effective date thereof, together with reasonable evidence that the foregoing net worth condition has been satisfied.

**Section 11.07 --- No Recapture Right.** Landlord shall not have a recapture right, termination right, or right to cancel this Lease in connection with any proposed assignment or subletting under this Article XI.

**Section 11.08 --- No Release.** No subletting or assignment, whether with or without Landlord\'s consent, shall release Tenant from any of its obligations under this Lease unless Landlord expressly agrees otherwise in writing. Tenant shall remain fully liable for the performance of all terms, covenants, and conditions of this Lease.

**[ARTICLE XII --- RENEWAL OPTIONS]{.underline}**

**Section 12.01 --- Grant of Renewal Options.** Landlord hereby grants to Tenant two (2) consecutive options to renew this Lease (each, a \"Renewal Option\"), each for an additional period of five (5) years (each, a \"Renewal Term\"). The first Renewal Term, if exercised, shall commence on July 1, 2032, and expire on June 30, 2037. The second Renewal Term, if exercised, shall commence on July 1, 2037, and expire on June 30, 2042.

**Section 12.02 --- Exercise of Renewal Option.** Tenant shall exercise each Renewal Option by delivering irrevocable written notice to Landlord no later than twelve (12) months prior to the expiration of the then-current Lease Term (or Renewal Term, as applicable). The Renewal Options must be exercised consecutively and may not be exercised if an Event of Default exists at the time of exercise or at the commencement of the applicable Renewal Term.

**Section 12.03 --- Renewal Rent.** Base Rent during each Renewal Term shall be equal to ninety-five percent (95%) of the then-prevailing fair market rent for comparable Class A office space in the Atlanta midtown/Buckhead submarket, taking into account all relevant factors, including size, location, term, condition, and amenities, as determined in accordance with Section 12.04.

**Section 12.04 --- Determination of Fair Market Rent.** Within thirty (30) days after Landlord\'s receipt of Tenant\'s renewal notice, Landlord and Tenant shall endeavor in good faith to agree upon the fair market rent for the applicable Renewal Term. If the parties are unable to agree within such thirty (30) day period, each party shall, within fifteen (15) days thereafter, appoint one (1) independent MAI-certified appraiser with at least ten (10) years of experience in the Atlanta commercial office market. Within fifteen (15) days after their appointment, the two appraisers shall jointly select a third independent MAI-certified appraiser meeting the same qualifications. Each appraiser shall independently determine the fair market rent for the Premises within thirty (30) days after the appointment of the third appraiser. The fair market rent shall be the average of the two closest appraisals. Each party shall bear the cost of its own appraiser, and the cost of the third appraiser shall be shared equally.

**Section 12.05 --- Terms During Renewal.** All terms and conditions of this Lease shall apply during each Renewal Term, except that: (a) Base Rent shall be as determined pursuant to Section 12.03; (b) no additional Tenant Improvement Allowance shall be provided unless otherwise agreed in writing by the parties; and (c) the number of remaining Renewal Options shall be reduced by one for each Renewal Option exercised.

**[ARTICLE XIII --- EXPANSION OPTION]{.underline}**

**Section 13.01 --- Grant of Expansion Option.** Landlord hereby grants to Tenant the option (the \"Expansion Option\") to expand the Premises to include the 9th Floor of the Building (the \"Expansion Space\"), consisting of approximately 18,500 rentable square feet.

**Section 13.02 --- Exercise Window.** Tenant may exercise the Expansion Option at any time during Lease Years 3 through 5 (i.e., from July 1, 2024, through June 30, 2027) by delivering written notice to Landlord at least six (6) months prior to Tenant\'s desired commencement date for the Expansion Space (the \"Expansion Commencement Date\"). If Tenant does not exercise the Expansion Option on or before June 30, 2027, the Expansion Option shall terminate and be of no further force or effect.

**Section 13.03 --- Expansion Rent.** Base Rent for the Expansion Space shall be at the same rate per RSF per annum as the Base Rent rate then in effect for the original Premises (i.e., the then-current Lease Year\'s rate under the Rent Schedule), escalating thereafter on the same schedule and at the same three percent (3%) per annum compounding rate as Base Rent for the original Premises.

**Section 13.04 --- Expansion TI Allowance.** Landlord shall provide a tenant improvement allowance for the Expansion Space in the amount of Forty and 00/100 Dollars (\$40.00) per RSF (\$40.00 × 18,500 RSF = \$740,000.00), to be disbursed in accordance with the procedures set forth in the Work Letter (Exhibit C), mutatis mutandis.

**Section 13.05 --- Coterminous Term.** The term for the Expansion Space shall be coterminous with the Lease Term for the original Premises, expiring on June 30, 2032, unless extended pursuant to Article XII.

**Section 13.06 --- Lease Amendment.** Upon exercise of the Expansion Option, the parties shall execute an amendment to this Lease incorporating the Expansion Space on the terms set forth in this Article XIII and adjusting Tenant\'s Pro Rata Share and parking allocation proportionally.

**[ARTICLE XIV --- CONTRACTION OPTION]{.underline}**

**Section 14.01 --- Contraction Right.** After the expiration of Lease Year 5 (i.e., on or after July 1, 2027), Tenant shall have the one-time right to contract the Premises by surrendering up to 5,000 RSF (the \"Contraction Space\") by delivering irrevocable written notice to Landlord at least nine (9) months prior to the effective date of contraction (the \"Contraction Date\"). The location of the Contraction Space within the Premises shall be mutually agreed upon by Landlord and Tenant, and shall be a contiguous area reasonably suitable for leasing by Landlord to a third party.

**Section 14.02 --- Contraction Fee.** Tenant shall pay to Landlord a contraction fee (the \"Contraction Fee\") on or before the Contraction Date, equal to the sum of: (a) the unamortized TI Allowance allocable to the Contraction Space, calculated using a seven percent (7%) per annum amortization rate over the original ten (10) year Lease Term, with the initial principal being \$55.00 per RSF of the Contraction Space; plus (b) six (6) months of Base Rent attributable to the Contraction Space, calculated at the Base Rent rate in effect as of the Contraction Date.

**Section 14.03 --- Effect of Contraction.** Upon the Contraction Date and payment of the Contraction Fee, (a) the Premises shall be reduced by the RSF of the Contraction Space; (b) Base Rent shall be reduced proportionally based on the reduced RSF; (c) Tenant\'s Pro Rata Share shall be adjusted to reflect the reduced Premises; and (d) Tenant\'s parking allocation shall be adjusted proportionally.

**Section 14.04 --- Limitation.** Tenant may exercise the contraction option only once during the Lease Term.

**[ARTICLE XV --- PARKING]{.underline}**

Parking for the Premises shall be provided in accordance with the Parking Addendum attached hereto as **Exhibit D** and incorporated herein by this reference. In summary, Tenant shall be entitled to fifty-six (56) unreserved parking spaces in the Building\'s parking garage at no additional charge during the Lease Term, reflecting a ratio of approximately 2.99 spaces per 1,000 RSF. Tenant shall also be entitled to eight (8) reserved executive parking spaces at a monthly rate of \$175.00 per space (\$1,400.00 per month; \$16,800.00 per year), payable as Additional Rent. Reserved parking charges shall be subject to annual adjustment as set forth in Exhibit D. Parking rights are appurtenant to this Lease and may not be separately transferred except in connection with a permitted assignment or subletting. Landlord shall maintain the parking garage in good condition and provide adequate lighting and security measures.

**[ARTICLE XVI --- ALTERATIONS]{.underline}**

**Section 16.01 --- Minor Alterations.** Tenant may make non-structural interior alterations to the Premises costing less than Fifty Thousand and 00/100 Dollars (\$50,000.00) per project without Landlord\'s prior written consent, provided that Tenant gives Landlord prior written notice thereof and the alterations comply with all applicable laws, codes, and regulations and do not adversely affect the Building\'s structural integrity or base building systems.

**Section 16.02 --- Major Alterations.** Any alteration costing Fifty Thousand and 00/100 Dollars (\$50,000.00) or more, or any structural alteration, shall require Landlord\'s prior written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed. Tenant shall submit complete plans and specifications to Landlord for review.

**Section 16.03 --- Standards.** All alteration work shall be performed in a good and workmanlike manner, in compliance with all applicable building codes and regulations, using licensed and adequately insured contractors. Tenant shall obtain all necessary permits prior to commencing work.

**Section 16.04 --- Removal.** Landlord may, at the time of approving Tenant\'s alteration plans, designate any non-standard alterations that Tenant shall be required to remove at the expiration or earlier termination of this Lease. Upon removal, Tenant shall restore the affected areas to their condition prior to such alterations, reasonable wear and tear excepted.

**[ARTICLE XVII --- SUBORDINATION AND ATTORNMENT]{.underline}**

**Section 17.01 --- Subordination.** This Lease is and shall be subject and subordinate to any mortgage, deed of trust, or ground lease now or hereafter placed upon the Building or the land upon which it is situated; provided, however, that any holder of such mortgage, deed of trust, or ground lease shall, as a condition to such subordination, execute and deliver to Tenant a commercially reasonable Subordination, Non-Disturbance, and Attornment Agreement (\"SNDA\") in a form reasonably acceptable to Tenant, confirming that Tenant\'s rights under this Lease shall not be disturbed so long as Tenant is not in default hereunder.

**Section 17.02 --- Current Status.** Landlord represents and warrants that, as of the Lease Date, no mortgage, deed of trust, or ground lease encumbers the Building that would require the execution of an SNDA.

**Section 17.03 --- Attornment.** Tenant agrees to attorn to any successor to Landlord\'s interest in the Building, whether through foreclosure, deed in lieu of foreclosure, or otherwise, provided that such successor recognizes Tenant\'s rights under this Lease.

**[ARTICLE XVIII --- DAMAGE AND DESTRUCTION]{.underline}**

**Section 18.01 --- Repair Obligation.** If the Premises or the Building is damaged by fire or other casualty, Landlord shall, subject to the provisions of this Article, repair such damage with reasonable diligence, using the proceeds of Landlord\'s insurance. Landlord\'s repair obligation shall extend to the base building and any improvements originally funded by the TI Allowance, but shall not extend to Tenant\'s personal property, furniture, trade fixtures, or any improvements funded by Tenant in excess of the TI Allowance.

**Section 18.02 --- Termination Right.** If Landlord reasonably determines that the damage cannot be repaired within two hundred seventy (270) days after the date of the casualty, either party may terminate this Lease by delivering written notice to the other within thirty (30) days after Landlord\'s determination.

**Section 18.03 --- Rent Abatement.** If the Premises are rendered wholly or partially untenantable as a result of the casualty, Base Rent and Additional Rent shall abate proportionally (based on the portion of the Premises rendered untenantable) from the date of the casualty until the earlier of (a) the date the Premises are restored to a tenantable condition or (b) the date of termination of this Lease.

**[ARTICLE XIX --- CONDEMNATION]{.underline}**

**Section 19.01 --- Total Taking.** If all or substantially all of the Premises is taken by eminent domain or other governmental authority, this Lease shall terminate as of the date of the taking.

**Section 19.02 --- Partial Taking.** If a partial taking of the Premises renders the remaining Premises unsuitable for Tenant\'s continued use and occupancy, either party may terminate this Lease by delivering written notice to the other within thirty (30) days after the date of the taking. If neither party elects to terminate, the Lease shall continue in effect with respect to the remaining portion of the Premises, and Base Rent and Additional Rent shall abate proportionally.

**Section 19.03 --- Condemnation Awards.** All condemnation awards and proceeds shall belong to and be the property of Landlord, except that Tenant shall have the right to separately claim and recover from the condemning authority compensation for Tenant\'s moving expenses, the unamortized cost of Tenant-funded improvements (i.e., improvements paid for by Tenant in excess of the TI Allowance), and any loss of Tenant\'s business goodwill, to the extent such separate claim does not reduce Landlord\'s award.

**[ARTICLE XX --- DEFAULT AND REMEDIES]{.underline}**

**Section 20.01 --- Tenant Events of Default.** Each of the following shall constitute an \"Event of Default\" by Tenant under this Lease:

> \(a\) Tenant\'s failure to pay Base Rent, Additional Rent, or any other sum due under this Lease within five (5) business days after written notice from Landlord that such payment is overdue;
>
> \(b\) Tenant\'s failure to perform or observe any other covenant, condition, or obligation under this Lease within thirty (30) days after written notice from Landlord specifying the nature of the default; provided, however, that if such default is of a nature that cannot reasonably be cured within thirty (30) days, Tenant shall not be deemed in default if Tenant commences a cure within such thirty (30) day period and diligently prosecutes the cure to completion;
>
> \(c\) Tenant\'s filing of a petition in bankruptcy, making a general assignment for the benefit of creditors, or the filing of an involuntary petition against Tenant that is not dismissed within sixty (60) days; or
>
> \(d\) Tenant\'s abandonment of the Premises.

**Section 20.02 --- Landlord\'s Remedies.** Upon the occurrence of an Event of Default, Landlord may, at its option and in addition to any other remedies available at law or in equity: (i) terminate this Lease by written notice to Tenant, whereupon Tenant shall immediately surrender the Premises; (ii) re-enter the Premises and relet the same on Tenant\'s behalf on such terms as Landlord deems commercially reasonable, with Tenant remaining liable for all deficiencies; (iii) accelerate all Base Rent and Additional Rent for the remainder of the Lease Term, discounted to present value at a rate equal to the then-applicable Federal Reserve discount rate plus one percent (1%); or (iv) pursue any other remedy available under the laws of the State of Georgia.

**Section 20.03 --- Landlord\'s Default.** If Landlord fails to perform any obligation under this Lease within thirty (30) days after written notice from Tenant specifying the nature of the default (or such longer period as may be reasonably required for non-monetary defaults, provided Landlord commences cure within such thirty (30) day period and diligently pursues the same to completion), Tenant may pursue any remedies available at law or in equity; provided, however, that Tenant shall not have the right to terminate this Lease or withhold or offset rent except as expressly permitted by the laws of the State of Georgia.

**Section 20.04 --- Holdover.** If Tenant remains in possession of the Premises after the expiration or earlier termination of this Lease without Landlord\'s prior written consent, Tenant shall be deemed a tenant at sufferance, and Tenant shall pay holdover rent equal to one hundred fifty percent (150%) of the Base Rent in effect during the last month of the Lease Term (or Renewal Term, as applicable), plus all Additional Rent and other charges under this Lease. Tenant shall also be liable for all damages, costs, and expenses incurred by Landlord as a result of such holdover occupancy, including without limitation any claims by prospective tenants.

**[ARTICLE XXI --- SURRENDER AND RESTORATION]{.underline}**

**Section 21.01 --- Surrender.** Upon the expiration or earlier termination of this Lease, Tenant shall surrender the Premises to Landlord in good order and condition, ordinary wear and tear and casualty damage (to the extent Landlord is obligated to repair) excepted.

**Section 21.02 --- Removal of Property.** Tenant shall remove all of its personal property, furniture, trade fixtures, and equipment from the Premises on or before the Expiration Date (or earlier termination date). **Section 21.03 --- Abandoned Property.** Any personal property of Tenant remaining in the Premises more than ten (10) days after the expiration or earlier termination of this Lease shall be deemed abandoned by Tenant, and Landlord may dispose of such property in any manner Landlord sees fit, without liability to Tenant.

**[ARTICLE XXII --- QUIET ENJOYMENT]{.underline}**

Landlord covenants and agrees that Tenant, upon paying the Base Rent, Additional Rent, and all other sums due under this Lease and performing all of Tenant\'s obligations hereunder, shall peaceably and quietly have, hold, and enjoy the Premises during the Lease Term (and any Renewal Term) without hindrance or interference from Landlord or any person or entity lawfully claiming by, through, or under Landlord, subject to the terms and conditions of this Lease.

All notices, demands, consents, approvals, and other communications required or permitted under this Lease shall be in writing and shall be deemed duly given if delivered by (a) personal delivery, (b) a nationally recognized overnight courier service (e.g., FedEx or UPS), or (c) certified mail, return receipt requested, postage prepaid, addressed as follows:
