**[ARTICLE XXIV --- ESTOPPEL CERTIFICATES]{.underline}**

Each party shall, within fifteen (15) business days after written request by the other party, execute and deliver an estoppel certificate addressed to such persons as the requesting party may reasonably designate, certifying: (a) that this Lease is in full force and effect and has not been modified (or stating the nature of any modifications); (b) that no defaults exist under this Lease (or specifying any claimed defaults); (c) the Commencement Date and Expiration Date; (d) the current Base Rent and Additional Rent payable; (e) the amount of any security deposit held by Landlord; and (f) such other matters as may be reasonably requested. Failure by a party to deliver the estoppel certificate within such fifteen (15) business day period shall constitute an irrevocable acknowledgment that the statements set forth in the requesting party\'s proposed form of certificate are true and correct.

**[ARTICLE XXV --- BROKERS]{.underline}**

Landlord represents and warrants that Ridgeview Realty Brokers Inc. acted as Landlord\'s broker in connection with this Lease. Landlord shall be solely responsible for the payment of all brokerage commissions due to Ridgeview Realty Brokers Inc. pursuant to a separate written agreement between Landlord and such broker. Tenant represents and warrants that it has not engaged any broker or finder in connection with this Lease. Each party shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the other from and against any claims, losses, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys\' fees) arising from any breach of its representations under this Article.

**[ARTICLE XXVI --- MISCELLANEOUS]{.underline}**

**Section 26.01 --- Governing Law.** This Lease shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Georgia, without regard to its conflict of laws principles.

**Section 26.02 --- Entire Agreement.** This Lease, together with all Exhibits attached hereto and incorporated herein by reference, constitutes the entire agreement between the parties with respect to the subject matter hereof and supersedes all prior negotiations, proposals, representations, understandings, and agreements, whether oral or written.

**Section 26.03 --- Amendments.** This Lease may not be modified, amended, or supplemented except by a written instrument executed by both Landlord and Tenant.

**Section 26.04 --- Severability.** If any provision of this Lease is held to be invalid, illegal, or unenforceable by a court of competent jurisdiction, the validity, legality, and enforceability of the remaining provisions shall not in any way be affected or impaired thereby.

**Section 26.05 --- Waiver.** No waiver by either party of any breach of any term, covenant, or condition of this Lease shall be deemed a waiver of any subsequent breach of the same or any other term, covenant, or condition. No waiver shall be effective unless in writing signed by the waiving party.

**Section 26.06 --- Successors and Assigns.** This Lease shall be binding upon and inure to the benefit of the parties hereto and their respective heirs, executors, administrators, legal representatives, successors, and permitted assigns.

**Section 26.07 --- No Recording.** Tenant shall not record this Lease or any memorandum hereof in any public records without Landlord\'s prior written consent; provided, however, that upon Tenant\'s request, the parties shall execute and record a memorandum of lease in a form mutually agreed upon by the parties, which memorandum shall set forth the parties, the Premises, the Lease Term, and such other provisions as the parties may agree.

**Section 26.09 --- Authority.** Each individual executing this Lease on behalf of a party represents and warrants that he or she is duly authorized to execute and deliver this Lease on behalf of such party and that this Lease is binding upon such party in accordance with its terms.

**Section 26.10 --- Counterparts.** This Lease may be executed in two or more counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original but all of which together shall constitute one and the same instrument. Signatures transmitted by electronic means (including PDF) shall be deemed original signatures for all purposes.

**Section 26.11 --- Time of Essence.** Time is of the essence with respect to the performance of each and every obligation of the parties under this Lease.

**Section 26.12 --- Attorneys\' Fees.** In any action or proceeding arising out of or in connection with this Lease, the prevailing party shall be entitled to recover its reasonable attorneys\' fees and costs from the non-prevailing party, in addition to any other relief to which such prevailing party may be entitled.

Tenant agrees that it shall look solely to the interest of Landlord in the Building and the land upon which the Building is situated for satisfaction of any claim, judgment, or decree requiring the payment of money by Landlord arising out of or in connection with this Lease. In no event shall Tenant\'s aggregate damages against Landlord exceed the value of Landlord\'s equity interest in the Building and its proceeds.

**[Section 4.3 --- Availability of Appropriations]{.underline}**

The Government\'s obligation to make rental payments under this Lease is subject to the availability of appropriated funds. Nothing in this Lease shall be interpreted to require obligations or payments in violation of the Anti-Deficiency Act (31 U.S.C. § 1341). In the event funds are not appropriated or otherwise available for the continued performance of this Lease, the Government shall provide the Lessor with written notice of such non-availability as soon as reasonably practicable.

**[SECTION 5 --- OPERATING EXPENSES AND TAXES]{.underline}**

**[Section 5.1 --- Base Year Operating Expenses]{.underline}**

The shell rent set forth in Section 4 includes the Lessor\'s operating expenses for the Building for the calendar year 2021 (the \"Base Year\"). Operating expenses for purposes of this Lease include, without limitation: common area maintenance, utilities (including electricity, natural gas, water, and sewer), janitorial services, landscaping, pest control, property management fees, insurance premiums (including property and general liability insurance), and real estate taxes and assessments attributable to the Building and associated land. The Lessor shall provide the Government with a certified statement of actual operating expenses for the Base Year as set forth in Exhibit C.

**[Section 5.2 --- Operating Expense Escalations]{.underline}**

For each calendar year following the Base Year, the Government shall pay its pro rata share of increases in actual operating expenses above the Base Year amount. The Government\'s pro rata share shall be calculated as follows:

> Government\'s Pro Rata Share = (15,000 RSF ÷ Total Building RSF) × (Actual Operating Expenses for Current Year − Base Year Operating Expenses)

Operating expense escalation charges shall be payable in addition to the shell rent set forth in Section 4. The Lessor shall provide the Government with an annual statement of actual operating expenses within ninety (90) days following the end of each calendar year. Such statement shall set forth in reasonable detail the components of operating expenses, including an itemization of real estate taxes, insurance, utilities, janitorial, management fees, and other material categories. The Government shall pay any underpayment within thirty (30) days of receipt of such statement, and the Lessor shall credit any overpayment against the next succeeding monthly rental payment.

The Government reserves the right to audit the Lessor\'s books, records, and accounts relating to operating expenses at any time during the Lease term and for three (3) years following the expiration or earlier termination of this Lease. The Lessor shall make such records available for inspection at a mutually agreeable location within fifteen (15) business days of receiving the Government\'s written request for an audit.

**[Section 5.3 --- Real Estate Taxes]{.underline}**

Real estate taxes, including ad valorem taxes, special assessments, and any other taxes or charges levied by any governmental authority upon the Building and associated land, are included as a component of operating expenses under this Section. To the extent real estate taxes increase above the Base Year amount, the Government shall pay its pro rata share of such increase as part of the operating expense escalation described in Section 5.2. The Lessor shall use commercially reasonable efforts to contest any real estate tax assessment that the Lessor believes to be excessive or erroneous.

**[SECTION 6 --- SERVICES AND UTILITIES]{.underline}**

The Lessor shall provide the following services and utilities as part of the shell rent during normal business hours (7:00 AM to 6:00 PM, Monday through Friday, excluding Federal holidays as designated by the Office of Personnel Management):

> \(a\) Heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (\"HVAC\") sufficient to maintain comfortable temperatures and humidity levels within the Premises, consistent with ASHRAE Standard 55 and applicable GSA design standards;
>
> \(b\) Electrical service to the Premises, including 120/208V, 3-phase power, in quantities sufficient for the Government\'s office operations, including computer and telecommunications equipment;
>
> \(c\) Domestic water and sewer service;
>
> \(d\) Janitorial services, including nightly cleaning of the Premises five (5) days per week (Monday through Friday), including vacuuming, dusting, trash removal, and restroom sanitation;
>
> \(e\) Trash removal and recycling services;
>
> \(f\) Passenger and freight elevator service;
>
> \(g\) Lobby and common area maintenance, including cleaning, lighting, and general upkeep; and
>
> \(h\) Snow and ice removal from Building entrances, sidewalks, and parking areas, as applicable.

After-hours HVAC service shall be provided at the Lessor\'s then-prevailing rates upon reasonable advance notice from the Government\'s authorized representative. The Lessor shall provide the Government\'s Contracting Officer with a schedule of after-hours HVAC rates at the commencement of each calendar year.

The Lessor shall maintain the Building and all common areas in first-class condition, consistent with the standards of comparable Class A office buildings in the Atlanta, Georgia metropolitan area. The Lessor shall promptly address any deficiency in services or utilities upon receipt of written notice from the Government\'s Contracting Officer or the Government\'s authorized representative on-site.

**[SECTION 7 --- TENANT IMPROVEMENTS]{.underline}**

**[Section 7.1 --- Government-Funded Improvements]{.underline}**

All tenant improvements, alterations, and installations made to the Premises by or on behalf of the Government (collectively, \"Government Improvements\") shall be funded by the Government at the Government\'s sole cost and expense. The Lessor shall not be required to provide any tenant improvement allowance, contribution, or reimbursement in connection with the Government\'s build-out of the Premises.

Government Improvements include, without limitation, interior build-out, partitioning, wall finishes, flooring, ceiling modifications, cabling, telecommunications infrastructure, information technology systems, security systems (including access control, intrusion detection, and surveillance systems), and all fixtures, furnishings, and equipment installed by the Government.

The Lessor acknowledges that certain Government Improvements may include specialized security infrastructure, including improvements necessary to create and maintain a Sensitive Compartmented Information Facility (\"SCIF\") or SCIF-capable space within the Premises. The specific nature, design, configuration, and location of any SCIF improvements are classified and are not detailed in this Lease or any exhibit or attachment hereto. The Lessor agrees not to access, inspect, photograph, or otherwise interfere with any SCIF space or SCIF improvements without prior written authorization from the Government\'s Contracting Officer or the Government\'s designated Facility Security Officer. Lessor further acknowledges that it has no right to review or approve the plans, specifications, or construction methods for any SCIF improvements.

**[Section 7.2 --- Ownership of Government Improvements]{.underline}**

**All Government Improvements shall remain the property of the Government at all times during and after the term of this Lease.** Government Improvements shall not be deemed fixtures or part of the realty, regardless of the manner in which they are affixed to or integrated with the Premises, and shall not become the property of the Lessor by reason of their attachment to the Building.

The Government shall have the right, but not the obligation, to remove any or all Government Improvements upon the expiration or earlier termination of this Lease. Such removal shall be completed within sixty (60) calendar days following the effective date of expiration or termination, during which period the Government shall have continued access to the Premises for the purpose of removal activities. The Government shall provide the Lessor with reasonable advance notice of its intent to remove Government Improvements and shall coordinate access with the Lessor\'s property manager.

**The Government shall not be required to restore the Premises to their original or pre-improvement condition upon removal of Government Improvements**, except that the Government shall repair any damage to the Building\'s structural elements (including but not limited to load-bearing walls, floor slabs, roof deck, and exterior envelope) caused directly by such removal. For the avoidance of doubt, the Government shall have no obligation to repair or restore cosmetic finishes, non-structural partitions, ceiling systems, floor coverings, or any other non-structural elements of the Premises affected by the removal of Government Improvements.

If the Government elects not to remove certain Government Improvements, such improvements shall be deemed abandoned by the Government and shall become the property of the Lessor at no cost to the Lessor and without any obligation on the part of the Government. The Lessor acknowledges and agrees that any Government Improvements left in place may not be in a condition suitable for use by the Lessor or any subsequent tenant and that the Lessor assumes all risk associated with the condition and utility of such abandoned improvements.

**[Section 7.3 --- Lessor\'s Base Building Obligations]{.underline}**

The Lessor shall deliver the Premises in shell condition, which shall include the following base building improvements at the Lessor\'s sole cost and expense:

> \(a\) Finished main lobby and elevator lobby on the 5th floor;
>
> \(b\) Passenger elevator service from the ground floor to the 5th floor;
>
> \(c\) Base building HVAC infrastructure, including main air handling units, ductwork to the floor, and thermostatic controls;
>
> \(d\) Restrooms constructed in compliance with applicable building codes and the Americans with Disabilities Act;
>
> \(e\) Fire and life safety systems in compliance with applicable codes, including sprinklers, fire alarms, and emergency lighting;
>
> \(f\) Core and shell finishes, including concrete floor slabs, drywall to deck at the perimeter, and basic suspended ceiling grid in common areas; and
>
> \(g\) Base building electrical distribution to the floor, including a main electrical panel.

The Lessor is responsible for all structural repairs and maintenance of the Building, including the roof, exterior walls, foundation, and Building systems (mechanical, electrical, and plumbing) to the extent such systems are not part of Government Improvements.

**[SECTION 8 --- ASSIGNMENT AND SUBLETTING]{.underline}**

**Government\'s Rights.** The Government may assign this Lease or sublet all or any portion of the Premises to any agency or instrumentality of the United States Government without the prior consent of the Lessor, in accordance with applicable provisions of the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) and GSA policy. The Lessor shall recognize any such assignee or subtenant as a tenant under this Lease upon receipt of written notice from the Government\'s Contracting Officer. No assignment or subletting by the Government shall relieve the Government of its obligations under this Lease unless the Government expressly releases itself in writing.

**Lessor\'s Rights.** The Lessor shall not assign this Lease or any interest therein, nor shall the Lessor delegate any of its obligations hereunder, without the prior written consent of the Government\'s Contracting Officer. Any purported assignment by the Lessor without such consent shall be void and of no force or effect. Any permitted assignment by the Lessor shall be subject to and shall not alter, modify, or diminish the Government\'s rights under this Lease, and the assignee shall assume in writing all of the Lessor\'s obligations under this Lease.

**Successors and Assigns.** This Lease shall be binding upon and inure to the benefit of the parties hereto and their respective successors and assigns, subject to the restrictions set forth in this Section 8. In the event of a sale, transfer, or other conveyance of the Building or any portion thereof that includes the Premises, the Lessor shall provide the Government\'s Contracting Officer with written notice of the identity and contact information of the new owner or transferee not less than thirty (30) days prior to the effective date of such sale or transfer. The new owner or transferee shall automatically assume all obligations of the Lessor under this Lease from and after the date of such transfer, and the Lessor shall cause the new owner or transferee to execute such documents as the Government\'s Contracting Officer may reasonably request to evidence such assumption.

**[SECTION 9 --- INSURANCE]{.underline}**

**Government Self-Insurance.** The Government is self-insured under the Federal Tort Claims Act (28 U.S.C. §§ 2671--2680) and other applicable Federal statutes. The Government shall not be required to carry or maintain any insurance policies with respect to the Premises or its occupancy thereof, including but not limited to commercial general liability insurance, property insurance, business interruption insurance, or workers\' compensation insurance specific to this Lease.

**Lessor\'s Insurance Obligations.** The Lessor shall carry and maintain at the Lessor\'s sole expense the following insurance coverage throughout the term of this Lease, including any holdover period:

> \(a\) **Property Insurance** covering the Building and all improvements thereto (exclusive of Government Improvements) against loss or damage by fire, windstorm, and other perils customarily covered under an \"all risk\" or \"special form\" property insurance policy, in an amount not less than the full replacement cost of the Building;
>
> \(b\) **Commercial General Liability Insurance** with limits of not less than One Million Dollars (\$1,000,000) per occurrence and Three Million Dollars (\$3,000,000) in the annual aggregate, covering bodily injury, property damage, and personal injury arising out of the Lessor\'s ownership, operation, and maintenance of the Building and common areas; and
>
> \(c\) **Workers\' Compensation Insurance** as required by the laws of the State of Georgia, covering all of the Lessor\'s employees performing work at or in connection with the Building.

The Lessor shall provide the Government\'s Contracting Officer with certificates of insurance evidencing the foregoing coverage upon request and upon each renewal thereof. All insurance policies maintained by the Lessor shall be issued by insurers rated at least \"A-\" VII by A.M. Best Company or equivalent.

The Government shall not be liable for any loss or damage to the Building or the Lessor\'s property arising out of fire, flood, or other casualty, except to the extent caused by the willful misconduct of the Government\'s employees or agents acting within the scope of their employment.

**[SECTION 10 --- SECURITY AND ACCESS]{.underline}**

**[Section 10.1 --- Building Access]{.underline}**

The Government shall have access to the Premises twenty-four (24) hours per day, seven (7) days per week, three hundred sixty-five (365) days per year, including Federal holidays and weekends. The Lessor shall provide the Government with keys, access cards, security codes, and/or other credentials necessary for such unrestricted access. There shall be no additional charge for after-hours access to the Premises.

The Lessor shall provide staffed lobby security during normal business hours (7:00 AM to 6:00 PM, Monday through Friday, excluding Federal holidays) and electronic access control during non-business hours, at the Lessor\'s expense as part of operating expenses included in the shell rent. The Government may supplement Building security with its own security personnel and systems at the Government\'s expense.

**[Section 10.2 --- SCIF and Classified Space]{.underline}**

The Lessor acknowledges that portions of the Premises may be designated as a Sensitive Compartmented Information Facility (\"SCIF\") or may contain classified national security information and materials. The Lessor and its agents, employees, contractors, and subcontractors shall not enter any SCIF-designated space or any other area of the Premises designated as a restricted or secure area without prior written authorization from the Government\'s Contracting Officer or the Government\'s designated Facility Security Officer (\"FSO\").

The Lessor shall cooperate with the Government in facilitating any security clearances or background investigations required for the Lessor\'s personnel who may need access to non-SCIF portions of the Premises for maintenance, repair, and Building systems servicing purposes. The Government shall provide reasonable advance notice to the Lessor of any security clearance requirements applicable to the Lessor\'s personnel.

The Government may install additional security measures within the Premises and on the Building exterior as required for the protection of classified information and materials, including but not limited to reinforced walls and barriers, intrusion detection systems, electronic and radio frequency shielding (including TEMPEST countermeasures), sound attenuation systems, dedicated HVAC systems with isolated air handling, and supplemental power systems. All such security installations shall be treated as Government Improvements under Section 7 of this Lease and shall be subject to the ownership and removal provisions set forth therein.

**[SECTION 11 --- TELECOMMUNICATIONS]{.underline}**

The Government shall have the right, at no additional cost or charge, to install, maintain, operate, and remove telecommunications equipment on the roof of the Building and in risers, conduits, and other infrastructure pathways within the Building, for the exclusive use of the Government. Telecommunications equipment includes, without limitation, satellite dishes, microwave antennas, radio frequency antennas, cables (including fiber optic cables), junction boxes, amplifiers, and related infrastructure and support structures.

The Lessor shall provide the Government with reasonable access to the roof and to riser, chase, and conduit systems within the Building for the installation, maintenance, repair, and removal of telecommunications equipment. The Government shall coordinate roof access with the Lessor\'s property manager and shall exercise reasonable care to avoid damage to the Building\'s roofing membrane, structural components, or other Building systems during installation, maintenance, or removal activities.

All telecommunications equipment installed by the Government on the roof or within the Building shall be deemed Government Improvements under Section 7 of this Lease and shall be subject to the ownership and removal provisions set forth in Section 7.2. The Government shall have the right, but not the obligation, to remove all telecommunications equipment upon the expiration or earlier termination of this Lease.

The Lessor shall not charge the Government any fee, rental, license fee, or other consideration for the use of roof space, riser space, or Building infrastructure for telecommunications purposes. The Government\'s telecommunications installations shall not be counted against the Premises RSF or result in any additional rent or operating expense charge.

**[SECTION 12 --- ALTERATIONS AND MODIFICATIONS BY LESSOR]{.underline}**

The Lessor shall not make any alterations, modifications, or improvements to the Premises or to the Building systems serving the Premises without the prior written consent of the Government\'s Contracting Officer. This restriction includes but is not limited to alterations to the HVAC system, electrical system, plumbing system, elevators, fire and life safety systems, security systems, structural elements, and common areas directly serving or adjacent to the Premises.

Any proposed alterations to the Building that may affect the Government\'s use and occupancy of the Premises, including changes to Building access, parking, common areas, or exterior signage, shall require prior consultation with the Government and written approval from the Government\'s Contracting Officer before commencement of any such work. The Lessor shall provide the Government with at least thirty (30) days\' prior written notice of any proposed alteration, together with a description of the scope and expected duration of the work.

**[SECTION 13 --- CASUALTY AND CONDEMNATION]{.underline}**

**[Section 13.1 --- Damage or Destruction]{.underline}**

If the Premises or the Building are damaged by fire, flood, earthquake, hurricane, or other casualty to the extent that the Government is unable to use the Premises, in whole or in substantial part, for their intended purpose, the Government may, at its sole option:

> \(a\) Terminate this Lease upon thirty (30) calendar days\' written notice to the Lessor, effective as of the date specified in such notice; or
>
> \(b\) Require the Lessor to restore the Premises (exclusive of Government Improvements) to their pre-casualty condition within one hundred eighty (180) calendar days following the date of the casualty event. If the Lessor fails to complete such restoration within the 180-day period, the Government may terminate this Lease upon written notice to the Lessor.

Rent shall be abated proportionately during any period in which all or a portion of the Premises is unusable due to casualty damage, based on the ratio of unusable square footage to total RSF. The Lessor shall notify the Government promptly, and in any event within forty-eight (48) hours, of any casualty affecting the Premises or the Building.

**[Section 13.2 --- Condemnation]{.underline}**

If all or a substantial portion of the Premises is taken by eminent domain or condemnation proceedings by any governmental authority, this Lease shall terminate as of the date of such taking, and rent shall be apportioned as of such date. If only a portion of the Premises is taken and such partial taking does not materially impair the Government\'s use of the remaining Premises for their intended purpose, this Lease shall continue in full force and effect with respect to the remaining Premises, and rent shall be abated proportionally based on the ratio of the RSF taken to the total RSF of the Premises prior to such taking.

**[SECTION 14 --- DEFAULT AND REMEDIES]{.underline}**

**Lessor Default.** If the Lessor fails to perform any material obligation under this Lease and such failure continues for thirty (30) calendar days after written notice from the Government specifying the nature of the default (or such longer period as may be reasonably necessary to cure the default, provided the Lessor commences cure within such 30-day period and diligently prosecutes the same to completion), the Government may, at its sole election, exercise one or more of the following remedies:

> \(a\) Cure the default and deduct the reasonable cost thereof from rent next becoming due, together with interest thereon at the rate established by the Secretary of the Treasury pursuant to the Prompt Payment Act;
>
> \(b\) Withhold or abate rent, in whole or in part, until the default is cured to the satisfaction of the Government\'s Contracting Officer; or
>
> \(c\) Terminate this Lease upon written notice to the Lessor, effective as of the date specified in such notice.

The foregoing remedies are cumulative and are in addition to any other remedies available to the Government under applicable law or regulation.

**Government Default.** The Government shall not be deemed in default of this Lease except for non-payment of rent when due. In the event of non-payment, the Lessor\'s sole and exclusive remedy is to submit a claim in accordance with the Contract Disputes Act of 1978, as amended (41 U.S.C. § 7101 et seq.). The Lessor shall not have the right to terminate this Lease, to lock out or exclude the Government from the Premises, to withhold services, or to exercise any other self-help remedy on account of any default or alleged default by the Government.

The Lessor expressly acknowledges and agrees that the Government is immune from claims for consequential, incidental, punitive, or exemplary damages, and the Lessor waives any right to seek or recover such damages in any proceeding arising under or relating to this Lease. The Lessor further waives any right to terminate this Lease on account of any default by the Government.

**[SECTION 15 --- QUIET ENJOYMENT]{.underline}**

The Lessor covenants and warrants that the Government, upon paying the rent and performing its obligations under this Lease, shall peaceably and quietly hold, occupy, and enjoy the Premises during the term of this Lease (including any holdover period) without hindrance, disturbance, or molestation by the Lessor, or by any person or entity claiming by, through, or under the Lessor, or by any person or entity having title paramount to the Lessor. The Lessor shall defend and indemnify the Government against any claims that interfere with the Government\'s quiet enjoyment of the Premises.

**[SECTION 16 --- SUBORDINATION AND NON-DISTURBANCE]{.underline}**

This Lease shall not be subordinate to any mortgage, deed of trust, deed to secure debt, or other lien or encumbrance now or hereafter placed upon the Building, the land upon which the Building is located, or the Lessor\'s interest therein. The Lessor shall not grant any mortgage, deed of trust, or lien that would take priority over this Lease without the prior written consent of the Government\'s Contracting Officer.

In the event of any foreclosure, deed in lieu of foreclosure, or other transfer of ownership of the Building arising from the exercise of remedies under any mortgage or lien, the Lessor shall ensure that this Lease remains in full force and effect and that the Government\'s rights hereunder are not disturbed, diminished, or impaired. Any successor owner, whether by foreclosure, deed in lieu, or otherwise, shall be bound by all terms and conditions of this Lease and shall recognize the Government as tenant hereunder. The Lessor shall obtain from any existing or future mortgagee or lien holder a subordination, non-disturbance, and attornment agreement in form and substance satisfactory to the Government\'s Contracting Officer, if requested by the Government.

**[SECTION 17 --- ENVIRONMENTAL COMPLIANCE]{.underline}**

The Lessor represents and warrants that, to the best of the Lessor\'s knowledge after due inquiry, the Building and the Premises are free from hazardous substances, toxic materials, mold, asbestos-containing materials, lead-based paint, and other environmental contaminants in concentrations or conditions that violate applicable federal, state, or local environmental laws, regulations, or standards.

The Lessor shall comply with all applicable federal, state, and local environmental laws and regulations throughout the term of this Lease, including without limitation the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act (CERCLA), the Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (RCRA), and the regulations of the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency and the Georgia Environmental Protection Division.

The Lessor shall promptly notify the Government\'s Contracting Officer, in writing, of any environmental condition at the Building or on the property on which the Building is situated that may affect the health or safety of the Government\'s employees or visitors, or that may affect the Government\'s use and occupancy of the Premises. Such notice shall be provided within twenty-four (24) hours of the Lessor\'s discovery of or notification regarding such condition.

The Government shall be responsible for the proper handling, storage, and disposal of any hazardous materials generated by the Government in connection with its use and occupancy of the Premises, in accordance with applicable law.

**[LEASE AGREEMENT]{.underline}**

**Haywood Village Shops --- Unit 4** **92 Haywood Street, Asheville, North Carolina 28801**

This Lease Agreement (this \"Lease\") is made and entered into as of the 15th day of May, 2020 (the \"Lease Date\"), by and between:

**LANDLORD:** Thornfield Realty Holdings LP, a North Carolina limited partnership, whose general partner is Thornfield Management Corp., a North Carolina corporation, with its principal office located at 500 South Tryon Street, Suite 2200, Charlotte, North Carolina 28202 (hereinafter referred to as \"Landlord\");

and

**TENANT:** The Pint & Platter Restaurant Group LLC, a North Carolina limited liability company, whose sole member is Lance Whitford, an individual, with its principal office located at 92 Haywood Street, Unit 4, Asheville, North Carolina 28801 (hereinafter referred to as \"Tenant\").

**RECITALS**

**WHEREAS**, Landlord is the fee simple owner of that certain retail shopping center commonly known as Haywood Village Shops, located at 92 Haywood Street, Asheville, Buncombe County, North Carolina 28801, containing approximately 62,000 rentable square feet of leasable retail and commercial space, together with all improvements, common areas, and appurtenances thereto; and

**WHEREAS**, Tenant desires to lease a portion of Haywood Village Shops for the operation of a full-service restaurant, bar, and related food-and-beverage establishment; and

**WHEREAS**, Landlord is willing to lease such space to Tenant upon the terms and conditions set forth herein;

**NOW, THEREFORE**, in consideration of the mutual covenants and agreements contained herein, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, Landlord and Tenant agree as follows:

**[ARTICLE 1 --- DEFINITIONS]{.underline}**

As used in this Lease, the following terms shall have the meanings set forth below:

**\"Additional Rent\"** shall mean all sums payable by Tenant to Landlord under this Lease other than Base Rent and Percentage Rent, including without limitation Tenant\'s Pro Rata Share of Operating Expenses, real estate taxes, insurance premiums, and CAM Expenses, as well as any late charges, interest, and other amounts due hereunder.

**\"Base Rent\"** shall mean the annual base rental amount payable by Tenant as set forth in the Rent Schedule attached hereto as Exhibit B and incorporated herein by this reference, subject to escalation as provided in Section 3.2 of this Lease.

**\"Breakpoint\"** shall have the meaning set forth in Section 3.3 of this Lease.

**\"Buildout Period\"** shall mean the period commencing on the Lease Date and ending on the day immediately preceding the Commencement Date, during which Tenant shall design, permit, and construct its leasehold improvements within the Premises in accordance with plans approved by Landlord.

**\"Commencement Date\"** shall mean October 1, 2020.

**\"Common Area Maintenance (CAM) Expenses\"** shall mean all costs and expenses incurred by Landlord in operating, maintaining, repairing, replacing, and managing the common areas of Haywood Village Shops, including but not limited to parking areas, sidewalks, driveways, access roads, landscaping, irrigation, exterior lighting, signage (excluding tenant-specific signage), stormwater management systems, utilities serving common areas, janitorial and cleaning services for common areas, snow and ice removal, security services, and a management fee not to exceed four percent (4%) of gross rental revenue of the Shopping Center.

**\"Expiration Date\"** shall mean September 30, 2030, unless the Term is sooner terminated or extended as provided herein.

**\"Gross Sales\"** shall mean all revenues from the sale of food, beverages (including alcoholic beverages), merchandise, and services of any kind made in, upon, or from the Premises, whether for cash, credit, or otherwise, including catering orders and delivery orders originating from the Premises, and revenues from online or mobile orders fulfilled at or from the Premises. The following items shall be excluded from Gross Sales: (i) tips and gratuities received by employees; (ii) sales tax, meals tax, or any other tax collected from customers and remitted to a governmental authority; (iii) the amount of any cash or credit refunds made to customers for goods or services previously included in Gross Sales; (iv) employee meals provided at cost; (v) proceeds from the sale of gift cards or gift certificates (provided, however, that the redemption of such gift cards or certificates shall be included in Gross Sales at the time of redemption); and (vi) proceeds from the sale of trade fixtures or equipment not in the ordinary course of business.

**\"Haywood Village Shops\"** or **\"Shopping Center\"** shall mean the retail shopping center located at 92 Haywood Street, Asheville, North Carolina 28801, containing approximately 62,000 rentable square feet of leasable space, together with all improvements, common areas, parking areas, and appurtenances, as more particularly depicted on the site plan attached hereto as Exhibit A.

**\"Lease Date\"** shall mean May 15, 2020.

**\"Lease Term\"** or **\"Term\"** shall mean the period of ten (10) years commencing on the Commencement Date and expiring on the Expiration Date, unless sooner terminated or extended pursuant to the terms of this Lease, including any Renewal Term exercised by Tenant in accordance with Article 11.

**\"Lease Year\"** shall mean each successive twelve (12) month period during the Term. Lease Year 1 shall commence on October 1, 2020 and expire on September 30, 2021. Lease Year 2 shall commence on October 1, 2021 and expire on September 30, 2022, and so forth for each successive Lease Year during the Term.

**\"Natural Breakpoint\"** shall mean, with respect to Percentage Rent, the quotient obtained by dividing the annual Base Rent for the applicable Lease Year by the Percentage Rent Rate (i.e., Base Rent ÷ 0.06). The Natural Breakpoint shall be recalculated for each Lease Year to reflect changes in Base Rent resulting from CPI adjustments or other modifications. Gross Sales in excess of the Natural Breakpoint during any Lease Year shall be subject to Percentage Rent as set forth in Section 3.3 of this Lease.

**\"Operating Expenses\"** shall mean the aggregate of all real estate taxes and assessments, property insurance premiums, and CAM Expenses.

**\"Percentage Rent\"** shall mean an amount equal to six percent (6%) of Tenant\'s annual Gross Sales in excess of the Breakpoint, as more particularly described in Section 3.3 of this Lease.

**\"Percentage Rent Rate\"** shall mean six percent (6%).

**\"Permitted Use\"** shall mean the operation of a full-service restaurant, bar, and related food-and-beverage service, together with such ancillary uses as are customarily associated therewith, including on-premises and off-premises catering, private event hosting, and delivery services.

**\"Premises\"** shall mean approximately 4,400 rentable square feet (\"RSF\") of ground-floor retail space, including the patio area, designated as Unit 4, Haywood Village Shops, 92 Haywood Street, Asheville, North Carolina 28801, as more particularly depicted on the floor plan attached hereto as Exhibit A.

**\"Pro Rata Share\"** shall mean Tenant\'s proportionate share of Operating Expenses, calculated as the ratio of the RSF of the Premises (4,400 RSF) to the total leasable RSF of Haywood Village Shops (62,000 RSF), which is approximately 7.10%.

**\"Security Deposit\"** shall mean the sum of Nineteen Thousand Eight Hundred Dollars (\$19,800.00) deposited by Tenant with Landlord pursuant to Article 4 of this Lease.

**[ARTICLE 2 --- PREMISES, TERM, AND DELIVERY]{.underline}**

**Section 2.1 --- Premises**

Landlord hereby leases to Tenant, and Tenant hereby leases from Landlord, the Premises consisting of approximately 4,400 RSF of ground-floor retail space, together with the adjacent patio area, designated as Unit 4, Haywood Village Shops, 92 Haywood Street, Asheville, North Carolina 28801, as more particularly depicted on the floor plan attached hereto as Exhibit A and incorporated herein by this reference. The Premises shall include all improvements, fixtures, and appurtenances constructed or installed therein by Tenant in accordance with this Lease.

**Section 2.2 --- Term**

The Lease Term shall be ten (10) years, commencing on October 1, 2020 (the \"Commencement Date\") and expiring on September 30, 2030 (the \"Expiration Date\"), unless sooner terminated or extended as provided herein. The Buildout Period shall run from May 15, 2020 through September 30, 2020 (approximately four and one-half (4.5) months), during which Tenant shall design, permit, and construct its leasehold improvements in accordance with plans and specifications approved by Landlord. No Base Rent or Percentage Rent shall accrue or be due during the Buildout Period; provided, however, that Tenant shall be responsible for all utility charges, insurance premiums, and any costs associated with the construction of its improvements during such period.

**Section 2.3 --- Delivery and Condition**

Landlord shall deliver the Premises to Tenant in broom-clean, shell condition on or before the Lease Date. Tenant acknowledges that it has inspected the Premises and, subject to Landlord\'s obligation to deliver all base building systems (including electrical, plumbing, HVAC, and fire/life safety systems) in good working order, Tenant accepts the Premises in its \"as-is\" condition. Landlord makes no representations or warranties concerning the condition of the Premises except as expressly set forth in this Lease.

**Section 2.4 --- Holdover**

If Tenant holds over and remains in possession of the Premises after the expiration or earlier termination of this Lease without Landlord\'s prior written consent, Tenant shall be deemed a tenant-at-sufferance and shall pay holdover rent equal to one hundred fifty percent (150%) of the Base Rent in effect during the last month of the Term, plus all Additional Rent and other charges due hereunder. Such holdover tenancy shall not constitute a renewal or extension of this Lease, and Landlord shall have the right to terminate such holdover tenancy at any time upon thirty (30) days\' written notice.

**[ARTICLE 3 --- RENT]{.underline}**

**Section 3.1 --- Base Rent**

Commencing on the Commencement Date, Tenant shall pay to Landlord Base Rent in equal monthly installments, in advance, on the first (1st) day of each calendar month during the Term. Base Rent for Lease Year 1 shall be Eighteen Dollars (\$18.00) per RSF per annum, which, based on 4,400 RSF, equals Seventy-Nine Thousand Two Hundred Dollars (\$79,200.00) per annum, or Six Thousand Six Hundred Dollars (\$6,600.00) per month. All Base Rent shall be due and payable without notice, demand, deduction, setoff, or abatement, except as expressly provided in this Lease. If the Commencement Date or Expiration Date falls on a date other than the first or last day of a calendar month, Base Rent for such partial month shall be prorated on a per diem basis.

**Section 3.2 --- Rent Escalation (CPI Adjustment)**

Commencing on October 1, 2021 (the first day of Lease Year 2) and on each anniversary thereof during the Term (each, an \"Adjustment Date\"), the Base Rent shall be adjusted based on the percentage increase in the Consumer Price Index --- All Urban Consumers (CPI-U), U.S. City Average, All Items (1982--84 = 100), as published by the Bureau of Labor Statistics of the United States Department of Labor. The CPI adjustment shall be calculated by comparing the CPI-U index published for the month that is three (3) months prior to the applicable Adjustment Date (the \"Current Index\") to the CPI-U index for the corresponding month of the immediately preceding year (the \"Base Index\"), and the percentage increase shall equal (Current Index − Base Index) ÷ Base Index × 100. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the annual CPI adjustment shall be subject to (a) a minimum floor adjustment of two percent (2%) per annum, and (b) a maximum cap adjustment of four percent (4%) per annum. If the CPI-U is discontinued or substantially modified, Landlord shall select a comparable index.

The Base Rent for the first five (5) Lease Years, as adjusted in accordance with this Section 3.2, is as follows:

  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Lease Year**   **Period**                    **Base Rent (\$/RSF)**   **Annual Base Rent**   **Monthly Base Rent**
  ---------------- ----------------------------- ------------------------ ---------------------- -----------------------
  1                Oct 1, 2020 -- Sep 30, 2021   \$18.000                 \$79,200.00            \$6,600.00

  2                Oct 1, 2021 -- Sep 30, 2022   \$18.684                 \$82,209.60            \$6,850.80

  3                Oct 1, 2022 -- Sep 30, 2023   \$19.431                 \$85,496.40            \$7,124.70

  4                Oct 1, 2023 -- Sep 30, 2024   \$19.917                 \$87,634.80            \$7,302.90

  5                Oct 1, 2024 -- Sep 30, 2025   \$20.315                 \$89,386.00            \$7,448.83
  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

For Lease Years 6 through 10, Base Rent shall be determined annually in accordance with this Section 3.2, applying the applicable CPI adjustment with the two percent (2%) floor and four percent (4%) cap. Landlord shall provide written notice to Tenant of the adjusted Base Rent not less than thirty (30) days prior to the applicable Adjustment Date. In the event Landlord fails to provide timely notice, Tenant shall continue to pay the prior Lease Year\'s Base Rent until notice is given, and Tenant shall pay any resulting deficiency within thirty (30) days of receipt of such notice.

**Section 3.3 --- Percentage Rent**

In addition to Base Rent, commencing in Lease Year 2, Tenant shall pay to Landlord Percentage Rent equal to six percent (6%) of Tenant\'s annual Gross Sales in excess of the Breakpoint. For purposes of calculating Percentage Rent, the Breakpoint shall be One Million Three Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars (\$1,350,000) for each Lease Year during the Term. For clarity, Percentage Rent for any Lease Year shall be calculated as follows: Percentage Rent = (Gross Sales − \$1,350,000) × 0.06, provided that if Gross Sales for such Lease Year do not exceed \$1,350,000, no Percentage Rent shall be due for such Lease Year.

Percentage Rent shall be calculated and paid annually within sixty (60) days after the end of each Lease Year. Tenant shall submit to Landlord a certified statement of Gross Sales for the preceding Lease Year, prepared in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles, within thirty (30) days after the end of such Lease Year.

Landlord shall have the right, at Landlord\'s expense (except as provided below), to audit Tenant\'s books and records relating to Gross Sales during normal business hours upon not less than fifteen (15) days\' prior written notice. Such audit right may be exercised no more than once per Lease Year and shall cover the three (3) most recent completed Lease Years. If any such audit reveals an understatement of Gross Sales by more than three percent (3%) for any audited Lease Year, Tenant shall (a) pay the cost of such audit, (b) pay the resulting deficiency in Percentage Rent, and (c) pay interest on the deficiency at the rate of one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month from the date such Percentage Rent was originally due until the date of payment.

**Section 3.4 --- Reporting of Gross Sales**

Tenant shall maintain complete and accurate books and records of all Gross Sales in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles, consistently applied. Tenant shall furnish to Landlord monthly sales reports, in a form reasonably satisfactory to Landlord, within fifteen (15) days after the end of each calendar month, reflecting the Gross Sales for such month. In addition, Tenant shall furnish an annual certified statement of Gross Sales for each Lease Year within thirty (30) days after the end of such Lease Year, which statement shall be certified by an authorized officer of Tenant. Landlord\'s audit rights with respect to Gross Sales records shall be as set forth in Section 3.3 above.

**Section 3.5 --- Additional Rent / NNN Charges**

In addition to Base Rent and Percentage Rent, Tenant shall pay as Additional Rent its Pro Rata Share of the following Operating Expenses: (a) all real estate taxes, assessments, and governmental charges levied against the Shopping Center (including Landlord\'s reasonable costs of contesting such taxes); (b) all premiums for property and liability insurance maintained by Landlord for the Shopping Center; and (c) all CAM Expenses as defined in Article 1 hereof. Landlord shall provide Tenant with an annual estimate of Additional Rent prior to or at the beginning of each calendar year, and Tenant shall pay one-twelfth (1/12) of the estimated annual amount on the first day of each calendar month. Within ninety (90) days after the end of each calendar year, Landlord shall provide Tenant with a reconciliation statement showing actual Operating Expenses for the preceding year. Any overpayment by Tenant shall be credited against the next monthly installment(s) of Additional Rent; any underpayment shall be due and payable by Tenant within thirty (30) days of receipt of the reconciliation statement.

**Section 3.6 --- Late Charge and Interest**

Any payment of Base Rent, Percentage Rent, Additional Rent, or any other sum due under this Lease that is not received by Landlord within five (5) days after the date when due shall bear a late charge equal to five percent (5%) of the overdue amount. In addition, all overdue amounts shall accrue interest at the rate of one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month (eighteen percent (18%) per annum), or the maximum rate permitted by applicable North Carolina law, whichever is less, from the due date until paid in full.

**[ARTICLE 4 --- SECURITY DEPOSIT]{.underline}**

Tenant has deposited with Landlord the sum of Nineteen Thousand Eight Hundred Dollars (\$19,800.00) as a security deposit (the \"Security Deposit\"), which amount is equal to three (3) months of Lease Year 1 Base Rent. The Security Deposit shall be held by Landlord as security for the faithful performance by Tenant of all terms, covenants, and conditions of this Lease. Landlord shall not be required to hold the Security Deposit in a separate account or to pay interest thereon. In the event of any default by Tenant hereunder, Landlord may, without prejudice to any other remedy, apply all or any portion of the Security Deposit to cure such default or to compensate Landlord for any loss or damage resulting therefrom. Tenant shall replenish any amounts so applied within ten (10) days of written notice from Landlord. Provided Tenant is not then in default, the Security Deposit (less any amounts properly applied) shall be returned to Tenant within thirty (30) days following the expiration or earlier termination of this Lease and Tenant\'s delivery of the Premises in accordance with Article 16 hereof.

**[ARTICLE 5 --- USE OF PREMISES]{.underline}**

**Section 5.1 --- Permitted Use**

Tenant shall use and occupy the Premises solely for the Permitted Use, which is the operation of a full-service restaurant, bar, and related food-and-beverage service (including dine-in, takeout, delivery, and catering services), and for no other purpose without Landlord\'s prior written consent, which consent may be withheld in Landlord\'s sole and absolute discretion. Tenant shall operate its business in the Premises during customary operating hours for the Shopping Center and shall maintain a level of staffing, inventory, and service consistent with the operation of a first-class full-service restaurant.

**Section 5.2 --- Exclusive Use**

Landlord hereby grants to Tenant the exclusive right to operate a full-service restaurant within Haywood Village Shops during the Term (the \"Exclusive Use Right\"). For purposes of this Section 5.2, \"full-service restaurant\" shall mean an establishment primarily engaged in the sale of food and beverages for on-premises consumption, offering table service by waitstaff, and maintaining a menu of entrées, appetizers, and desserts. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the Exclusive Use Right shall not restrict Landlord from leasing space within the Shopping Center to quick-service or fast-casual restaurant operators, coffee shops, bakeries, ice cream or frozen dessert shops, or specialty food retailers, provided that any such quick-service or fast-casual restaurant operator occupies premises of less than 2,000 RSF within the Shopping Center. In the event Landlord violates the Exclusive Use Right by leasing to or permitting the operation of a competing full-service restaurant within the Shopping Center, Tenant shall be entitled to (i) specific performance and injunctive relief to enforce the Exclusive Use Right, and (ii) abatement of Base Rent for the period during which such violation continues.

**Section 5.3 --- Radius Restriction**

During the Term and for a period of twelve (12) months following the expiration or earlier termination of this Lease, Tenant shall not, directly or indirectly, whether as owner, partner, member, shareholder, officer, director, employee, consultant, or otherwise, open, operate, manage, or have any ownership interest in any restaurant or food-and-beverage establishment within a three (3) mile radius of the Premises (the \"Restricted Area\"). The foregoing restriction shall not apply to any restaurant that is open and operating as of the Lease Date. In the event Tenant violates this radius restriction, Landlord shall be entitled, in addition to any other remedies available at law or in equity, to include in Gross Sales hereunder all revenues from any such competing restaurant operated by Tenant or its affiliates within the Restricted Area, for purposes of calculating Percentage Rent under Section 3.3.

**Section 5.4 --- Compliance with Laws; Licenses and Permits**

Tenant shall, at its sole cost and expense, comply with all applicable federal, state, and local laws, ordinances, rules, regulations, and orders in connection with its use and occupancy of the Premises. Tenant shall obtain and maintain at its sole cost all licenses, permits, and approvals required for the operation of the Premises, including without limitation health department permits, fire and safety permits, building permits, certificates of occupancy, and ABC permits for the sale and service of alcoholic beverages.

**Section 5.5 --- Liquor License / ABC Permits**

Landlord covenants to cooperate reasonably with Tenant\'s application for and maintenance of all Alcoholic Beverage Control (\"ABC\") permits and licenses necessary for Tenant\'s operation, including executing such landlord consents and certifications as may be required by the North Carolina ABC Commission. The parties acknowledge that the execution of this Lease was contingent upon Tenant obtaining an ABC permit within one hundred twenty (120) days of the Commencement Date, and the parties further acknowledge that such condition has been satisfied as of the date hereof.

**[ARTICLE 6 --- OPERATING EXPENSES AND TAXES]{.underline}**

**Section 6.1 --- Triple Net Structure**

This Lease is intended to be a \"triple net\" (NNN) lease, and Tenant acknowledges that the Base Rent set forth herein is a net amount to Landlord. Accordingly, in addition to Base Rent and Percentage Rent, Tenant shall pay its Pro Rata Share of (a) all real estate taxes and assessments levied against the Shopping Center, (b) all premiums for property and liability insurance maintained by Landlord for the Shopping Center, and (c) all CAM Expenses, all as more particularly set forth in Section 3.5 above. In no event shall Operating Expenses include costs attributable to Landlord\'s financing, depreciation, capital improvements (except to the extent amortized over their useful life as required to comply with applicable law or to reduce Operating Expenses), or leasing commissions.

**Section 6.2 --- Estimates and Reconciliation**

Landlord shall furnish Tenant with a written estimate of Tenant\'s Pro Rata Share of Operating Expenses for each calendar year prior to or at the beginning of such year. Tenant shall pay one-twelfth (1/12) of the estimated amount on the first day of each calendar month. Within ninety (90) days following the end of each calendar year, Landlord shall provide a reconciliation statement showing actual Operating Expenses, and any overpayment or underpayment shall be adjusted as set forth in Section 3.5 above. Tenant shall have the right, upon not less than thirty (30) days\' prior written notice and at Tenant\'s expense, to audit Landlord\'s books and records relating to Operating Expenses for the preceding calendar year.

**[ARTICLE 7 --- MAINTENANCE AND REPAIRS]{.underline}**

**Section 7.1 --- Tenant\'s Obligations**

Tenant shall, at its sole cost and expense, maintain the interior of the Premises in good order, condition, and repair, including without limitation the HVAC systems exclusively serving the Premises, plumbing fixtures and connections, grease traps and interceptors, kitchen exhaust and ventilation systems, interior walls, ceilings, and floor coverings, electrical systems within the Premises, patio area (including furniture, railings, and surfaces), and all trade fixtures and equipment. Tenant shall enter into and maintain a preventive maintenance contract for the HVAC systems serving the Premises with a qualified contractor reasonably approved by Landlord.

**Section 7.2 --- Landlord\'s Obligations**

Landlord shall maintain and repair the structural elements of the building in which the Premises are located, including the foundation, exterior load-bearing walls, and roof structure, as well as the common areas of the Shopping Center (including parking areas, sidewalks, landscaping, and exterior lighting) and shared building systems (such as main utility lines and fire suppression systems) to the extent such systems are not exclusively serving the Premises. The cost of such maintenance and repair to the extent constituting CAM Expenses shall be included in Operating Expenses and allocated to tenants in accordance with their Pro Rata Shares.

**[ARTICLE 8 --- INSURANCE]{.underline}**

**Section 8.1 --- Tenant\'s Insurance**

Tenant shall obtain and maintain at its sole cost and expense throughout the Term the following insurance coverage: (a) Commercial General Liability insurance, including coverage for bodily injury, property damage, personal injury, and products/completed operations liability, with limits of not less than One Million Dollars (\$1,000,000) per occurrence and Two Million Dollars (\$2,000,000) in the aggregate; (b) Liquor Liability insurance with limits of not less than One Million Dollars (\$1,000,000) per occurrence; (c) Property insurance covering Tenant\'s trade fixtures, equipment, inventory, and leasehold improvements at full replacement cost; (d) Workers\' Compensation insurance as required by the laws of the State of North Carolina, and Employer\'s Liability insurance with limits of not less than Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$500,000); and (e) Business Interruption insurance covering not less than twelve (12) months of rent obligations under this Lease. All policies shall name Landlord and Landlord\'s mortgagee(s) as additional insureds and shall provide for not less than thirty (30) days\' prior written notice to Landlord of cancellation or material modification.

**Section 8.2 --- Landlord\'s Insurance**

Landlord shall maintain property insurance on the Shopping Center (building shell and common areas) on a replacement cost basis and Commercial General Liability insurance with commercially reasonable limits. The cost of such insurance shall be included in Operating Expenses and allocated to tenants in accordance with their respective Pro Rata Shares.

**Section 8.3 --- Waiver of Subrogation**

Landlord and Tenant each hereby waive all rights of recovery against the other party for any loss or damage to the extent such loss or damage is covered by the waiving party\'s insurance policies (or would have been covered had the waiving party maintained the insurance required under this Lease). Each party shall cause its respective insurance carriers to issue appropriate waiver of subrogation endorsements in favor of the other party.

**[ARTICLE 9 --- ASSIGNMENT AND SUBLETTING]{.underline}**

**Section 9.1 --- Restriction**

Tenant shall not assign, transfer, mortgage, pledge, or encumber this Lease, or sublet all or any portion of the Premises, without the prior written consent of Landlord, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed. Any attempted assignment or subletting without Landlord\'s consent shall be void and of no force or effect and shall constitute an Event of Default under this Lease.

**Section 9.2 --- Conditions to Consent**

In evaluating any proposed assignment or subletting, Landlord may consider the proposed assignee\'s or subtenant\'s (a) financial condition and creditworthiness, (b) business reputation and character, (c) proposed use of the Premises (which must conform to the Permitted Use), and (d) restaurant operating experience. Landlord may also require that Tenant remain liable for all obligations under this Lease and that the assignee or subtenant execute an assumption agreement in form satisfactory to Landlord.

**Section 9.3 --- No Release**

No assignment or subletting, whether or not consented to by Landlord, shall release Tenant from its obligations under this Lease. The assignee or subtenant shall assume in writing all obligations of Tenant under this Lease for the benefit of Landlord, and a copy of such assumption agreement shall be delivered to Landlord prior to the effective date of the assignment or subletting.

**[ARTICLE 10 --- CO-TENANCY]{.underline}**

If the aggregate occupancy of Haywood Village Shops falls below seventy percent (70%) of the total leasable area of the Shopping Center for more than one hundred eighty (180) consecutive days (a \"Co-Tenancy Failure\"), Tenant shall have the right, upon thirty (30) days\' prior written notice to Landlord, to elect either of the following remedies: (a) **Reduced Rent**: Tenant may pay Base Rent equal to seventy-five percent (75%) of the then-applicable Base Rent, plus Percentage Rent (without adjustment to the Breakpoint), until such time as occupancy of the Shopping Center is restored to seventy percent (70%) or above, at which point Base Rent shall revert to the full amount then in effect; or (b) **Termination**: Tenant may terminate this Lease upon sixty (60) days\' prior written notice to Landlord, provided that such Co-Tenancy Failure is then continuing and has not been cured as of the date Tenant delivers such termination notice. If the occupancy of the Shopping Center is restored to seventy percent (70%) or above prior to the effective date of any termination notice, the termination notice shall be deemed withdrawn and of no further effect. The Co-Tenancy Failure must be continuous; if occupancy is restored to seventy percent (70%) or above before Tenant exercises either remedy, the right shall lapse until a new Co-Tenancy Failure occurs.

**[ARTICLE 11 --- RENEWAL OPTIONS]{.underline}**

Tenant shall have two (2) options to renew this Lease, each for an additional term of five (5) years (each, a \"Renewal Term\"), upon the following terms and conditions: (a) Tenant shall deliver irrevocable written notice of exercise to Landlord not less than nine (9) months prior to the then-current Expiration Date (or the expiration of the first Renewal Term, as applicable); (b) the Base Rent during each Renewal Term shall be the then-prevailing fair market rent for comparable restaurant space in the Asheville, North Carolina metropolitan area, as mutually determined by Landlord and Tenant in good faith; provided, however, that in no event shall the Base Rent during any Renewal Term be less than the Base Rent payable during the final Lease Year of the immediately preceding Term or Renewal Term; (c) all other terms and conditions of this Lease shall remain in full force and effect during each Renewal Term unless otherwise mutually agreed in writing; and (d) Tenant shall not be in default under this Lease, and no Event of Default shall be continuing, both at the time Tenant delivers its exercise notice and at the commencement of the applicable Renewal Term. If the parties are unable to agree upon fair market rent within sixty (60) days after Tenant\'s exercise notice, the determination shall be made by a single MAI-certified appraiser mutually selected by the parties, whose determination shall be binding.

**[ARTICLE 12 --- SUBORDINATION, NON-DISTURBANCE, AND ATTORNMENT]{.underline}**

This Lease shall be subject and subordinate to any mortgage, deed of trust, or other security instrument now or hereafter placed upon the Shopping Center or any portion thereof, and to all renewals, modifications, consolidations, replacements, and extensions thereof. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Landlord shall use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain from each existing and future mortgagee or beneficiary a subordination, non-disturbance, and attornment agreement (\"SNDA\") in commercially reasonable form, which shall provide that, so long as Tenant is not in default under this Lease, Tenant\'s possession and rights under this Lease shall not be disturbed by the mortgagee or any successor in a foreclosure proceeding. Tenant agrees to attorn to any successor landlord, whether by foreclosure, deed in lieu of foreclosure, or otherwise, and to recognize such successor as Landlord under this Lease.

**[ARTICLE 13 --- INDEMNIFICATION AND LIABILITY]{.underline}**

Tenant shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Landlord and its partners, officers, directors, employees, agents, and affiliates from and against all claims, actions, damages, losses, liabilities, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys\' fees) arising out of or in connection with (a) Tenant\'s use and occupancy of the Premises, (b) any act or omission of Tenant or its employees, agents, contractors, or invitees, (c) any breach by Tenant of its obligations under this Lease, or (d) any injury to or death of any person or damage to any property occurring in, on, or about the Premises. Landlord shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Tenant from and against all claims, actions, damages, losses, liabilities, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys\' fees) arising out of or in connection with Landlord\'s negligence in maintaining the common areas and structural elements of the Shopping Center. Notwithstanding anything to the contrary herein, neither party shall be liable to the other for any consequential, incidental, indirect, special, or punitive damages arising under or in connection with this Lease.

**[ARTICLE 14 --- DEFAULT AND REMEDIES]{.underline}**

**Section 14.1 --- Events of Default**

Each of the following shall constitute an \"Event of Default\" under this Lease: (a) Tenant\'s failure to pay Base Rent, Percentage Rent, Additional Rent, or any other monetary obligation due hereunder within ten (10) days after written notice from Landlord that such payment is past due; (b) Tenant\'s failure to perform or observe any non-monetary covenant, condition, or obligation of this Lease within thirty (30) days after written notice from Landlord specifying the nature of such failure, provided that if such failure is of a nature that cannot reasonably be cured within thirty (30) days, Tenant shall not be in default if Tenant commences to cure within such thirty (30) day period and thereafter diligently prosecutes such cure to completion; (c) Tenant\'s filing of a petition in bankruptcy, making an assignment for the benefit of creditors, or the appointment of a receiver or trustee for all or substantially all of Tenant\'s assets; or (d) Tenant\'s abandonment of the Premises for more than thirty (30) consecutive days.

**Section 14.2 --- Landlord\'s Remedies**

Upon the occurrence and during the continuance of an Event of Default, Landlord may, at its option, exercise any one or more of the following remedies: (a) terminate this Lease by written notice to Tenant and recover from Tenant all damages incurred by Landlord, including unamortized tenant improvement allowances, the present value (discounted at six percent (6%) per annum) of the excess of rent due for the remainder of the Term over the fair market rental value of the Premises for such period, and reasonable attorneys\' fees; (b) re-enter the Premises and relet all or any portion thereof on such terms and conditions as Landlord deems advisable, with Tenant remaining liable for the deficiency; or (c) pursue any other remedy available at law or in equity. All remedies of Landlord are cumulative and non-exclusive, and the exercise of any remedy shall not preclude the exercise of any other remedy.

**[ARTICLE 15 --- DAMAGE AND DESTRUCTION; CONDEMNATION]{.underline}**

In the event the Premises are damaged by fire, casualty, or other cause, Landlord shall promptly notify Tenant of the estimated time to repair. If the damage renders more than fifty percent (50%) of the RSF of the Premises untenantable, either party may terminate this Lease upon sixty (60) days\' written notice to the other, delivered within ninety (90) days of the date of damage. If the damage renders fifty percent (50%) or less of the RSF untenantable, Landlord shall repair the Premises to substantially its condition prior to the casualty (excluding Tenant\'s trade fixtures, equipment, and personal property) within one hundred eighty (180) days from the date of damage. Base Rent and Additional Rent shall be equitably abated during the period of repair in proportion to the area rendered untenantable. In the event of a taking of all or substantially all of the Premises by eminent domain or condemnation, this Lease shall terminate as of the date of such taking. In the event of a partial taking that does not render the Premises unsuitable for Tenant\'s use, the Lease shall continue and Base Rent shall be equitably reduced in proportion to the area taken. Upon the expiration or earlier termination of this Lease, Tenant shall peaceably surrender and deliver the Premises to Landlord in good condition, ordinary wear and tear excepted, and shall remove all of Tenant\'s trade fixtures, equipment, signage, and personal property. Tenant shall repair any damage to the Premises caused by such removal. Any property not removed by Tenant within ten (10) days following the expiration or termination date shall be deemed abandoned and may be retained, disposed of, or removed by Landlord at Tenant\'s expense.

This Lease, together with all Exhibits attached hereto (Exhibits A, B, C, and D), constitutes the entire agreement between Landlord and Tenant with respect to the subject matter hereof, and supersedes all prior and contemporaneous negotiations, representations, warranties, understandings, and agreements, whether written or oral, between the parties relating to the Premises and the transactions contemplated hereby.

          'The arithmetic is sound; the portfolio\'s risk is not in the arithmetic but in the structure of the income.', size=10.5)

          'approximately 9.6 months after the target closing date — and the Government holds no renewal obligation and may thereafter terminate on 120 days\' notice. '

          'which has no security deposit and no guaranty but holds a live right to expand onto an additional 18,500 RSF and a right to contract by up to 5,000 RSF. '
