{"command": "cd "$WORKSPACE_DIR" && cat > work/build3.py <<'PY'
# 1.5 prioritized findings
h2(doc, '1.5', 'Prioritized risk summary')
para(doc, 'The findings below are ordered by a combination of (i) the quantum of rent or value affected, (ii) whether the issue can be cured or mitigated before closing, and (iii) the time within which '
          'Galleon must act. Each is cross-referenced to the risk register in Section 7, where all twenty-six flagged items are set out with severity and timing ratings.')

def finding(n, head, body):
    p = doc.add_paragraph(); pf=p.paragraph_format
    pf.left_indent=Inches(0.32); pf.first_line_indent=Inches(-0.32); pf.space_after=Pt(4)
    r=p.add_run(f'{n}  '); r.bold=True; r.font.size=Pt(10); r.font.color.rgb=DKRED
    r2=p.add_run(head + '  '); r2.bold=True; r2.font.size=Pt(10)
    r3=p.add_run(body); r3.font.size=Pt(9.8)

finding('F1', 'GSA firm term expires 9.6 months after closing and there is no renewal option.',
        'The GSA lease (20.12% of current rent; $472,500 per annum) has a firm term ending December 31, 2025 and a soft term to December 31, 2030 during which the Government may terminate on 120 days\' notice '
        'with no fee. The lease grants no renewal option of any kind, and the soft-term rent of $484,350 to $534,600 per annum is expressly contingent. Post-2025 income from the 5th floor should be underwritten '
        'as a re-leasing opportunity, not as contracted rent. [R-01, R-02]')
finding('F2', 'The Acquisition itself triggers Apex\'s right of first refusal over Building C.',
        'Apex holds a ROFR over Building C that expressly applies where Building C is sold as part of a portfolio transaction, on Building C\'s allocable share of the purchase price, with the allocation fixed by the '
        'Seller and subject only to an MAI appraisal dispute. Thornfield must deliver a ROFR notice and give Apex 30 days to elect before it can sell. Building C represents 23.74% of current rent and 87,500 RSF. '
        'The PSA, the title file and the Seller\'s disclosure must be checked for compliance with, or a waiver of, this right. [R-04]')
finding('F3', 'Southeastern Fire & Safety is in holdover: there is no lease term to acquire.',
        'The lease expired June 30, 2024 and the single five-year renewal option lapsed unexercised on April 1, 2024. The tenant occupies 22,000 RSF (14.0% of RSF) month-to-month, terminable by either party on '
        '30 days\' notice, at 150% of the final month\'s rent ($25,437.50 per month; $305,250 per annum annualised). Galleon would acquire no term. The 150% premium may also be vulnerable if the landlord has, by '
        'accepting it for five months, been taken to have consented to a month-to-month tenancy at ordinary rent. We recommend underwriting this space as vacancy and negotiating an extension or new lease before closing. [R-05, R-06, R-09]')
finding('F4', 'Soto can terminate 46 days after closing.',
        'Dr. Soto may terminate effective October 31, 2025 on notice given by April 30, 2025 — that is, 46 days after the target closing and 89 days before the due diligence period expires — against payment of '
        '$40,657.14, which we have recomputed and confirmed (unamortised TI $16,457.14 plus three months\' rent $24,200.00). The lease covers 4.12% of current rent. Tenant intention should be established by estoppel before closing. [R-03]')
finding('F5', 'Verdana is the largest tenant and carries the most optionality and the least credit support.',
        'Verdana accounts for 28.81% of current rent with no deposit and no guaranty. It holds (i) a live expansion option over the 9th floor (approximately 18,500 RSF) exercisable to June 30, 2027 at the then-current '
        'rate with a $740,000 TI allowance — a contingent landlord obligation of roughly $740,000 plus abatement of a floor that may otherwise be leasable; (ii) a one-time right to contract by up to 5,000 RSF on or after '
        'July 1, 2027; and (iii) a right to sublease up to 40% (7,500 RSF) without consent, with no recapture right in the landlord. [R-17, R-18, R-19, R-20]')
finding('F6', 'No estoppel certificates have been delivered, and five of the seven tenants are not obliged to give one.',
        'The lease file contains no estoppel certificate for any tenant. Only the Apex and Verdana leases contain an estoppel covenant (10 and 15 business days respectively, each with a deemed-acknowledgment provision). '
        'The Soto, BrightPath, Southeastern, Pint & Platter and GSA leases contain no estoppel provision, so certificates must be obtained through the PSA, tenant cooperation or, for GSA, a Contracting Officer acknowledgment. [R-10]')
finding('F7', 'The GSA lease cannot be subordinated, which constrains debt placement on the largest property.',
        'Section 16 provides that the lease is not subordinate to any mortgage, and that the Lessor may not grant any mortgage or lien taking priority over it without the Contracting Officer\'s prior consent; any successor '
        'owner is bound. Concord Office Tower carries 48.93% of portfolio rent, so this provision will affect the terms on which Fieldstone can place debt against that property. Separately, no SNDA with Highpoint National Bank '
        '(the lender on Thornfield Distribution Center) is in the file for the Apex lease, and the Verdana lease records a representation that no mortgage encumbered Concord Office Tower at the lease date — which needs to be '
        'confirmed against current title. [R-11, R-13]')
finding('F8', 'Apex\'s exclusive use covenant restricts re-leasing across three buildings, and the Apex lease has drafting gaps.',
        'Apex\'s exclusive use right bars the landlord from permitting fulfilment, logistics, distribution or warehousing use in Buildings A, B or C — a restriction over approximately 152,500 RSF of the Property that '
        'is not confined to Apex\'s own premises, and which may already be breached depending on the use of Buildings A and B. The Apex lease also contains no casualty or condemnation article (so the allocation of risk on '
        'a casualty is left to the common law and to North Carolina statute) and no security deposit or guaranty, despite representing 23.74% of rent. [R-14, R-15, R-16]')
finding('F9', 'Pint & Platter carries a co-tenancy right, an internally inconsistent percentage rent breakpoint, and credit support that expires shortly after closing.',
        'If occupancy at Haywood Village Shops falls below 70% for more than 180 consecutive days the tenant may reduce Base Rent to 75% or terminate on 60 days\' notice. The 62,000 RSF centre\'s actual occupancy is not '
        'evidenced anywhere in the file and must be certified by the Seller. The lease fixes the percentage rent breakpoint at $1,350,000 in Section 3.3 but separately defines a "Natural Breakpoint" of Base Rent ÷ 0.06, which '

# ---------- SECTION 4 : INDIVIDUAL ABSTRACTIONS ----------
new_section(doc, landscape=False, title='Lease Abstraction Report — Thornfield Portfolio (7 Leases)')
h1(doc, '4', 'Individual Lease Abstractions')
para(doc, 'Each abstraction below follows the twelve categories mandated by Section 2(e) of the engagement letter. Section references are to the lease concerned. The "Verification notes" record our independent '
          'arithmetic and any term that could not be verified from the documents provided; the "Risk flags" record our characterisation and cross-refer to the risk register at Section 7.', size=9.5)

def snapshot_lease(items):
    t = doc.add_table(rows=1, cols=len(items)); t.autofit=False
    set_borders(t, sz=4, color='C9D3E4'); cell_margins(t, 50,50,80,80)
    for i,(k,v) in enumerate(items):
        c = t.rows[0].cells[i]; c.width = Inches(6.6/len(items)); c.text=''
        p=c.paragraphs[0]; p.paragraph_format.space_after=Pt(0)
        r=p.add_run(k.upper()); r.bold=True; r.font.size=Pt(6.8); r.font.color.rgb=NAVY
        p2=c.add_paragraph(); p2.paragraph_format.space_after=Pt(0); p2.paragraph_format.space_before=Pt(0)
        r2=p2.add_run(v); r2.font.size=Pt(8)
        shade(c,'F2F5FA')
    para(doc,'',space_after=6)

def abstract_lease(num, heading, snapshot, rows, verification, risks):
    h2(doc, num, heading)
    snapshot_lease(snapshot)
    table(doc, ['Category','Abstracted terms'], rows, widths=[1.45,5.15], font_size=8.0, bold_cols=(0,))
    rich(doc, [('Verification notes.  ',True,False),(verification,False,False)], size=8.8, space_before=6, space_after=4)
    rich(doc, [('Risk flags.  ',True,False),(risks,False,False)], size=8.8, space_before=0, space_after=10)
    return

# ---------- SECTION 4 : INDIVIDUAL ABSTRACTIONS ----------
new_section(doc, landscape=False, title='Lease Abstraction Report — Thornfield Portfolio (7 Leases)')
h1(doc, '4', 'Individual Lease Abstractions')
para(doc, 'Each abstraction below follows the twelve categories mandated by Section 2(e) of the engagement letter. Section references are to the lease concerned. The "Verification notes" record our independent '
          'arithmetic and any term that could not be verified from the documents provided; the "Risk flags" record our characterisation and cross-refer to the risk register at Section 7.', size=9.5)

def snapshot_lease(items):
    t = doc.add_table(rows=1, cols=len(items)); t.autofit=False
    set_borders(t, sz=4, color='C9D3E4'); cell_margins(t, 50,50,80,80)
    for i,(k,v) in enumerate(items):
        c = t.rows[0].cells[i]; c.width = Inches(6.6/len(items)); c.text=''
        p=c.paragraphs[0]; p.paragraph_format.space_after=Pt(0)
        r=p.add_run(k.upper()); r.bold=True; r.font.size=Pt(6.8); r.font.color.rgb=NAVY
        p2=c.add_paragraph(); p2.paragraph_format.space_after=Pt(0); p2.paragraph_format.space_before=Pt(0)
        r2=p2.add_run(v); r2.font.size=Pt(8)
        shade(c,'F2F5FA')
    para(doc,'',space_after=6)

def abstract_lease(num, heading, snapshot, rows, verification, risks):
    h2(doc, num, heading)
    snapshot_lease(snapshot)
    table(doc, ['Category','Abstracted terms'], rows, widths=[1.45,5.15], font_size=8.0, bold_cols=(0,))
    rich(doc, [('Verification notes.  ',True,False),(verification,False,False)], size=8.8, space_before=6, space_after=4)
    rich(doc, [('Risk flags.  ',True,False),(risks,False,False)], size=8.8, space_before=0, space_after=10)
    return

 'Every figure in Exhibit B was rebuilt from $5.500 at 3% compounding. Lease Years 1–4 and 7–10 reproduce exactly. Lease Year 5 is stated at $6.180 but 3% compounding from $6.010 produces $6.190; '
 'Lease Year 6 is stated at $6.370, which is $0.005 above a 3% step from the erroneous $6.180 and $0.006 below the correct compounding path of $6.376 (implied Year 5→6 step 3.074%). '
 'Annual and monthly amounts throughout tie to the stated per-RSF rates ($6.180 × 87,500 = $540,750; $6.370 × 87,500 = $557,375). Pro Rata Share recomputed: 87,500 ÷ 240,000 = 36.458%, consistent with the 36.46% stated. '
 'The TI allowance, the $131,250 annual amortisation and the recapture window all recompute correctly. The Property RSF of 240,000 is stated as "approximately" and is used only to derive the Pro Rata Share; it should be confirmed.',
 'The right of first refusal is the single most time-sensitive issue in the Portfolio: the Acquisition is itself the triggering event, and Building C cannot be conveyed to Galleon if Apex elects to purchase at its allocable price (§13.3–13.4). '
 'The exclusive use covenant is an encumbrance on the landlord\'s ability to lease Buildings A and B that survives closing and binds successors; if Buildings A or B are currently occupied by logistics users the covenant may already be in breach. '
 'The absence of entity credit support, of any casualty or condemnation mechanic, and of an SNDA with the mortgagee are each material gaps for a lease representing almost a quarter of portfolio rent.')

 'The fixed $0.75/RSF step reproduces exactly in each of the seven Lease Years, and every annual and monthly figure ties to the per-RSF rate (for example $30.25 × 3,200 = $96,800.00; ÷ 12 = $8,066.67). '

  'Effective Date and Commencement Date July 1, 2014; Expiration Date June 30, 2024; initial term of ten (10) Lease Years (§§1.3–1.5; §3.1).\n'
  'The lease has expired. The tenant has remained in possession since July 1, 2024 and is, per the rent roll, a month-to-month holdover.\n'
  'Remaining contractual term at January 1, 2025: nil. The monthly tenancy is terminable by either party on 30 days\' written notice (Art. 13).'],
 ['(3) Rent',
  'Lease Year 1: $7.50/RSF = $165,000.00 per annum = $13,750.00 per month.\n'
  'Contract escalation: 2% per annum on each anniversary of the Commencement Date (§4.1; Exhibit B).\n'
  'Final Lease Year 10: $9.25/RSF = $203,500.00 per annum = $16,958.33 per month.\n'
  'Holdover rent: 150% of the Base Rent in effect during the final month = $25,437.50 per month (Art. 13; Exhibit B). Annualised, $305,250.00 — the figure the rent roll carries as "current annual base rent" and as $13.875/RSF effective.\n'
  'Late charge 5% after five days; interest 1.5% per month (§4.2).'],
 ['(4) Lease Type',
  'Triple net (NNN) (§5.1). Base Rent is expressed to be "absolutely net" to the landlord, with the tenant responsible for its pro rata share of Operating Expenses, real estate taxes and insurance. Because the term has expired, the NNN machinery operates only as part of the month-to-month holdover terms.'],
 ['(5) Operating Expenses',
  'Pro Rata Share = 22,000 RSF ÷ total RSF of the Building or, where applicable, Greystone Industrial Park as a whole, "as reasonably determined by Landlord"; the denominator is not stated (§5.2).\n'
  'Included: taxes and assessments, property insurance, common-area utilities, landscaping, snow and ice removal, security, management fees not exceeding 5% of gross rental income, common-area maintenance and reasonable capital reserves (§1.9).\n'
  'Mechanics: annual estimates collected monthly; statement within 90 days; overpayment refunded within 30 days, shortfall payable within 30 days (§5.5).\n'
  'No audit right is granted to the tenant.'],
 ['(6) Renewal Options',
  'One five-year option (July 1, 2024 – June 30, 2029) at the then-prevailing fair market rental rate determined in good faith, with a single mutually selected appraiser if not agreed within 30 days (§3.2).\n'
  'Notice: not less than 90 days before expiration — i.e. by April 1, 2024, which is 90 days before June 30, 2024 (§3.3). Time is of the essence, and failure was expressed to be an irrevocable waiver.\n'
  'The rent roll states that the option was not exercised and has lapsed. There is no evidence of exercise in the documents provided, and no correspondence confirming non-exercise.'],
 ['(7) Termination Rights',
  'No tenant termination right. On default the landlord may recover, among other things, the present value of rent for the balance of the term discounted at 6% per annum (§12.2(c)).\n'
  'Holdover tenancy is terminable by either party on 30 days\' notice (Art. 13). Casualty: landlord may restore or terminate within 60 days of the casualty (Art. 15.1). Condemnation (Art. 15.2).'],
 ['(8) Assignment and Subletting',
  'Consent required and may be withheld in the landlord\'s sole and absolute discretion (§9.1) — the most restrictive consent standard in the Portfolio.\n'
  'No affiliate carve-out. No release of the tenant (§9.2). Any consideration received in excess of the rent payable, net of reasonable brokerage and legal fees, is payable over to the landlord (§9.3). Each transfer requires separate consent (§9.4).'],
 ['(9) Security Deposit / Guaranty',
  'None. There is no security deposit provision in the lease and no guaranty. The rent roll\'s deposit field is blank.'],
 ['(10) Tenant Improvements',
  'No TI allowance. Structural alterations require consent; non-structural alterations under $25,000 may be made on 15 days\' notice (§§10.1–10.2).\n'
  'Alterations vest in the landlord on installation unless the landlord requires removal by notice not later than 30 days before expiration; trade fixtures and movable equipment remain the tenant\'s and are removable subject to repair (§10.3).'],
 ['(11) Special Provisions',
  'Environmental: the tenant is expressly permitted to store, handle, use and transport fire suppressant chemicals, AFFF, foam concentrates and dry chemical agents, subject to strict compliance with environmental law, permits, an inventory updated at least annually and delivery of safety data sheets (Art. 14.2). The tenant indemnity expressly extends to PFAS and AFFF contamination and survives termination (§§14.3–14.5). The tenant must carry Pollution Legal Liability insurance of not less than $1,000,000 per occurrence and CGL of $2,000,000/$5,000,000 (§7.1).\n'
  'Landlord liability is limited to its equity interest in the Building and the proceeds of it (§11.3).\n'
  'Subordination is self-operative, with an irrevocable power of attorney in favour of the landlord to execute subordination documents if the tenant fails to do so within ten days (Art. 16).\n'
  'No estoppel provision, no audit right, no broker (§18.8). Governing law North Carolina, venue Gaston or Mecklenburg County (§18.3).'],
 ['(12) Risk Flags',
  'R-05 — no term: month-to-month holdover at 150%; 13.00% of portfolio rent and 22,000 RSF at risk.\n'
  'R-06 — renewal option lapsed unexercised on April 1, 2024; no evidence of non-exercise beyond the rent roll note.\n'
  'R-09 — Year 10 rate of $9.25 represents a 5.23% step against the recited 2% and sets the holdover base; potential overcharge claim and reduced holdover rate.\n'
  'R-28 — AFFF and PFAS permitted use; tenant indemnity is only as good as the tenant\'s balance sheet.\n'
  'R-16 — no deposit, no guaranty, no credit support.\n'
  'R-10 — no estoppel provision.']],
 'The 2% schedule reproduces for Lease Years 1–9 with one- or two-cent rounding in Years 4–9 as the lease rounds each step to the cent. Lease Year 10 is stated at $9.25, but 2% from $8.79 is $8.9658 ($8.97) — an implied step of 5.233% against a recited 2%. '
 'The stated annual figure ties to the stated rate ($9.25 × 22,000 = $203,500.00) and the holdover figure ties to that ($16,958.33 × 150% = $25,437.50; × 12 = $305,250.00), so the documents are internally consistent with each other, but the final step is not consistent with the escalation formula in the same lease. '
 'If 2% had been applied, Year 10 rent would have been $197,247.60 per annum ($16,437.30 per month) and holdover would have been $24,655.95 per month ($295,871.40 per annum) — $9,378.54 less than the figure carried in the rent roll ($9,240.00 less on a lease-rounded $8.97 basis). '
 'The Year 10 period ran from July 1, 2023 to June 30, 2024, so the discrepancy also gives rise to a potential historical overcharge of approximately $6,252.40 for that year.',
 'This is the most significant single risk in the Portfolio after the GSA rollover. Galleon would be buying 22,000 RSF of occupied industrial space with no lease: the tenant can leave on 30 days\' notice, and the landlord can end the tenancy on 30 days\' notice. '
 'The 150% holdover premium is only a contractual entitlement while the landlord treats the occupancy as an unconsented holdover; a tenant faced with a claim could argue that five months of accepted payments evidences consent to a month-to-month tenancy at the ordinary rate, '
 'and that contention would also be available if the landlord sought to enforce a premium computed on an inflated Year 10 base. The AFFF and PFAS permitted use is a genuine environmental exposure of a kind that a Phase I will not detect; '
 'the tenant\'s indemnity and pollution insurance are the only protections, and both depend on the tenant\'s continued solvency and the policy remaining in force.')
PY

# ---------------- 4.5 VERDANA ----------------
abstract_lease('4.5', 'Verdana Software Solutions Inc. — Concord Office Tower, 8th Floor, Atlanta, GA',
 [('Premises','8th floor (entire), 18,750 RSF'),('Term','7/1/2022 – 6/30/2032 (10 yrs)'),('Current rent','$676,312.50 p.a. ($36.07/RSF)'),('Type','Full-service gross, BY 2022')],
 [['(1) Tenant and Premises',
  'Landlord: Thornfield Realty Holdings LP. Tenant: Verdana Software Solutions Inc., a Delaware corporation qualified to do business in Georgia.\n'
  'Premises: the entire 8th floor, Concord Office Tower, 300 Concord Plaza Drive, Atlanta, Fulton County, Georgia 30309; approximately 18,750 RSF measured under ANSI/BOMA Z65.1-2017 and stipulated conclusive absent written agreement (§2.02). The floor plate is the whole floor.\n'
  'Building: approximately 150,000 RSF; Pro Rata Share 12.50% (18,750 ÷ 150,000) (Art. I).\n'
  'Permitted use: general office, software development and ancillary uses (§6.01). Parking: 56 unreserved spaces free of charge (approximately 2.99 per 1,000 RSF) plus 8 reserved executive spaces on Level P1 at $175.00 per space per month (Art. XV; Exhibit D).'],
 ['(2) Term',
  'Lease Date February 28, 2022; Commencement Date July 1, 2022; Expiration Date June 30, 2032; term of ten (10) years (§3.02).\n'
  'Early access from April 1, 2022 to construct improvements, without Base Rent and without affecting the Expiration Date (§3.03). A Commencement Date Memorandum was to be executed within 30 days of commencement (§3.04) — none is in the file.\n'
  'Current Lease Year: Year 3 (July 1, 2024 – June 30, 2025). Remaining term at January 1, 2025: 7.49 years (2,737 days).'],
 ['(3) Rent',
  'Base Rent monthly in advance on the first day of each month (§4.01).\n'
  'Lease Year 1: $34.00/RSF = $637,500.00 per annum = $53,125.00 per month (§4.02).\n'
  'Escalation: three percent (3%) per annum compounded annually from each anniversary of the Commencement Date (§4.03; Exhibit B).\n'
  'Current (Year 3): $36.07/RSF = $676,312.50 per annum = $56,359.38 per month. Scheduled Year 10 (July 1, 2031 – June 30, 2032): $44.35/RSF = $831,562.50.\n'
  'Additional Rent: 8 reserved spaces at $175.00 = $1,400.00 per month ($16,800.00 per annum), adjustable annually by up to 5% (Exhibit D §2).\n'
  'Late charge 5% after five business days; interest at 1.5% per month (18% per annum) or the maximum lawful rate on amounts unpaid for more than ten days (§§4.05–4.06).'],
 ['(4) Lease Type',
  'Full-service gross with a Base Year 2022 expense stop (§5.01). Landlord pays all Building operating expenses; the tenant pays only its share of increases above the Base Year.'],
 ['(5) Operating Expenses',
  'Tenant pays 12.50% of the excess of actual Operating Expenses over calendar 2022 actuals, commencing January 1, 2023 (§5.01).\n'
  'Controllable expense cap: controllable operating expenses (all expenses other than real estate taxes, insurance, utilities and snow/ice removal) may not increase by more than 5% per annum on a cumulative compounding basis over the Base Year (§5.07). Gross-up to 95% occupancy for occupancy-variable expenses (§5.08). Management fee not exceeding 4% of gross revenues (§5.02(g)).\n'
  'Exclusions include capital improvements except law-mandated or cost-reducing items amortised at 8%, leasing commissions and advertising, other tenants\' improvements and concessions, insurance and condemnation recoveries, depreciation, debt service, landlord income taxes, costs of landlord negligence and construction defects, and legal fees in tenant disputes (§5.03).\n'
  'Mechanics: monthly estimates, revisable during the year; annual statement within 120 days; audit within 12 months on 30 days\' notice, with auditor fees reimbursed where overcharge exceeds 5% and a prohibition on contingency-fee auditors (§§5.04–5.06).'],
 ['(6) Renewal Options',
  'Two consecutive five-year options: July 1, 2032 – June 30, 2037 and July 1, 2037 – June 30, 2042 (Art. XII).\n'
  'Rent: 95% of the then-prevailing fair market rent for comparable Class A Atlanta midtown/Buckhead office space, determined by a three-appraiser process (average of the two closest appraisals) (§§12.03–12.04).\n'
  'Notice: not less than twelve months before expiration — by June 30, 2031 for the first option. The options must be exercised consecutively (§12.02).\n'
  'No further TI allowance on renewal; no default condition (§12.05).'],
 ['(7) Termination Rights',
  'Contraction right (Art. XIV): after the expiration of Lease Year 5, i.e. on or after July 1, 2027, the tenant may once surrender up to 5,000 RSF on nine months\' notice. The contraction fee is the unamortised TI allocable to that space at 7% mortgage-style amortisation on $55.00/RSF, plus six months\' Base Rent on the space at the then-current rate (§§14.01–14.04). Base Rent and the Pro Rata Share reduce pro rata.\n'
  'Casualty: either party may terminate if the landlord determines that restoration cannot be completed within 270 days (§18.02). Condemnation: total taking terminates; partial taking permits termination if the remainder is unsuitable (Art. XIX).\n'
  'On default the landlord may accelerate all remaining rent, discounted at the Federal Reserve discount rate plus 1% (§20.02(iii)).'],
 ['(8) Assignment and Subletting',
  'Assignment: consent required, not unreasonably withheld; the original tenant remains secondarily liable for the remainder of the term unless released in writing (§11.05).\n'
  'Subletting up to 40% of the RSF (7,500 RSF) is permitted WITHOUT consent, subject to conditions — permitted use, no governmental entity, not an existing tenant or a prospect in active negotiation, ten business days\' post-execution notice with a copy of the sublease and financial information, and continuing tenant liability (§11.02). Subletting above 40% requires consent, not unreasonably withheld, with deemed consent if the landlord does not respond within 20 business days (§11.03).\n'
  'Profit sharing: 50% of Subletting Profits to the landlord, calculated monthly, with quarterly accounting (§11.04).\n'
  'No recapture right, termination right or cancellation right arises on any assignment or subletting (§11.07). Permitted affiliate transfers without consent, subject to a tangible net worth test and 15 days\' notice (§11.06). No release (§11.08).'],
 ['(9) Security Deposit / Guaranty',
  'None. The Section I summary states "Security Deposit: None"; the rent roll field is blank. There is no guaranty and no letter of credit. The landlord\'s protection is the lease, the acceleration remedy and the tenant\'s covenant strength.'],
 ['(10) Tenant Improvements',
  'TI Allowance of $55.00/RSF = $1,031,250.00 (§7.01; Exhibit C).\n'
  'Disbursement monthly against AIA G702/G703 applications, unconditional lien waivers for prior amounts and conditional waivers for the current draw, with 10% retainage released on substantial completion and receipt of a certificate of occupancy (Exhibit C §4). Unused allowance is forfeited and confers no credit (§7.03).\n'
  'For recapture the allowance amortises at 7% per annum over 120 months on a mortgage-style schedule (§7.04). Improvements vest in the landlord; designated non-standard items may be removed (§7.05).'],
 ['(11) Special Provisions',
  'Expansion option (Art. XIII): the tenant may expand onto the 9th floor (approximately 18,500 RSF) at any time during Lease Years 3 to 5, i.e. July 1, 2024 to June 30, 2027, on six months\' notice. Rent is at the then-current per-RSF rate for the Premises, escalating on the same 3% schedule, coterminous to June 30, 2032, with a TI allowance of $40.00/RSF ($740,000.00 for 18,500 RSF).\n'
  'Estoppel: certificate within 15 business days; failure is an irrevocable acknowledgment of the requesting party\'s form (Art. XXIV).\n'
  'Subordination: subordinate only if the mortgagee delivers a commercially reasonable SNDA (17.01); landlord represented that no mortgage encumbered the Building at the Lease Date (17.02).\n'
  'Landlord liability limited to its interest in the Building (Art. XXVII). Holdover at 150%, tenant at sufferance (20.04). No recording without consent, memorandum permitted (26.07). After-hours HVAC at $75.00 per hour per zone (8.03). Prevailing-party attorneys\' fees (26.12). Georgia law (26.01).'],
 ['(12) Risk Flags',
  'R-17 — live expansion option over 18,500 RSF with a $740,000 TI obligation, exercisable to June 30, 2027.\n'
  'R-18 — contraction right of up to 5,000 RSF from July 1, 2027.\n'
  'R-19 — 40% sublease without consent and no landlord recapture right.\n'
  'R-20 — no deposit or guaranty for the largest tenant exposure (28.81%).\n'
  'Concentration — Concord Office Tower carries 48.93% of portfolio rent across this lease and the GSA lease.']],
 'All ten lease years recompute exactly at 3% compounding, and every annual and monthly figure ties to the stated per-RSF rate ($36.07 × 18,750 = $676,312.50; ÷ 12 = $56,359.38). The Pro Rata Share recomputes at exactly 12.50% (18,750 ÷ 150,000); the TI allowance at $1,031,250.00 (18,750 × $55.00); the reserved parking at $16,800.00 per annum (8 × $175 × 12); '
 'and the parking ratio at 2.987 per 1,000 RSF against the stated 2.99. The expansion TI allowance recomputes at $740,000.00 (18,500 × $40.00). No arithmetic exception arises in this lease. The unquantified items are the contraction fee (which depends on the amortisation schedule, the contraction date and the rent then in effect) and the 9th-floor expansion rent.',
 'Verdana is the Portfolio\'s largest tenant and its least protected exposure: 28.81% of current rent with no deposit, no guaranty and no letter of credit. The lease is, however, structured in the landlord\'s favour on transfers — a 40% free-sublease right is unusual for a tenant of this size, and the absence of any recapture right (§11.07) removes the landlord\'s principal protection, although the 50% profit share partly compensates. '
 'The expansion option is a live, dated liability: it must be exercised, if at all, by June 30, 2027, and if exercised obliges the landlord to fund up to $740,000 of improvements while letting 18,500 RSF at the 8th-floor rate rather than market. It also constrains the landlord\'s ability to pre-let the 9th floor on better terms during the option window. '
 'The contraction right from July 2027 is a smaller but real value leak on a fully leased floor plate.')

abstract_lease('4.6', 'The Pint & Platter Restaurant Group LLC — Haywood Village Shops, Unit 4, Asheville, NC',
 [('Premises','Unit 4 + patio, 4,400 RSF'),('Term','10/1/2020 – 9/30/2030 (10 yrs)'),('Current rent','$89,386.00 p.a. ($20.315/RSF)'),('Type','NNN + 6% percentage rent')],
 [['(1) Tenant and Premises',
  'Landlord: Thornfield Realty Holdings LP. Tenant: The Pint & Platter Restaurant Group LLC, a North Carolina limited liability company whose sole member is Lance Whitford; Guarantor: Lance Whitford, individually (Exhibit D).\n'
  'Premises: Unit 4, ground floor retail space including the adjacent patio area, Haywood Village Shops, 92 Haywood Street, Asheville, Buncombe County, North Carolina 28801; approximately 4,400 RSF (§2.1).\n'
  'Shopping Center: approximately 62,000 RSF of leasable retail and commercial space; Pro Rata Share approximately 7.10% (§1; recomputed at 7.097%).\n'
  'Permitted use: full-service restaurant, bar and related food and beverage service, including on-premises and off-premises catering, private events and delivery (§5.1).'],
 ['(2) Term',
  'Lease Date May 15, 2020; Commencement Date October 1, 2020; Expiration Date September 30, 2030; term of ten (10) years (§2.2).\n'
  'Buildout Period from May 15, 2020 to September 30, 2020 (approximately 4.5 months) with no Base Rent or percentage rent, tenant paying utilities and insurance (§2.2).\n'
  'Current Lease Year: Year 5 (October 1, 2024 – September 30, 2025). Remaining term at January 1, 2025: 5.74 years (2,098 days).'],
 ['(3) Rent',
  'Base Rent monthly in advance on the first day of each month (§3.1).\n'
  'Lease Year 1: $18.00/RSF = $79,200.00 per annum = $6,600.00 per month.\n'
  'Escalation: CPI adjustment on each October 1, calculated as the percentage change in CPI-U (U.S. City Average, All Items, 1982–84 = 100) for the month three months before the adjustment date against the same month of the prior year, subject to a 2.00% floor and a 4.00% cap (§3.2).\n'
  'Stated adjustments, Lease Years 2–5: 3.800%, 3.998%, 2.501% and 1.998% — i.e. $18.684, $19.431, $19.917 and $20.315 per RSF. Current (Year 5): $89,386.00 per annum = $7,448.83 per month.\n'
  'Lease Years 6–10 are not fixed: the lease requires annual CPI determination, and Exhibit B records them as "TBD" (§3.2).\n'
  'Percentage Rent: 6.00% of annual Gross Sales above the Breakpoint, commencing Lease Year 2, payable annually within 60 days after each Lease Year against a certified annual statement delivered within 30 days; monthly sales reports within 15 days; landlord audit once per Lease Year covering the three most recent years, with costs, deficiency and 1.5% monthly interest payable if gross sales are understated by more than 3% (§§3.3–3.4).\n'
  'Late charge 5% after five days; interest 1.5% per month (§3.6).'],
 ['(4) Lease Type',
  'Triple net plus percentage rent (Art. 6). Tenant pays Base Rent, Percentage Rent and its Pro Rata Share of taxes, insurance and CAM.'],
 ['(5) Operating Expenses',
  'Operating Expenses are defined as real estate taxes and assessments, property insurance premiums and CAM Expenses (Art. 1; §3.5).\n'
  'CAM management fee not exceeding 4% of gross rental revenue of the Shopping Center (Art. 1). Operating Expenses exclude landlord financing costs, depreciation, capital improvements except as amortised where required by law or to reduce expenses, and leasing commissions (§6.1).\n'
  'Mechanics: annual estimate paid in twelfths; reconciliation within 90 days; overpayment credited, underpayment due within 30 days (§§3.5, 6.2). Tenant audit right for the preceding year on 30 days\' notice at its own expense (§6.2).'],
 ['(6) Renewal Options',
  'Two five-year options (Art. 11). Rent is the then-prevailing fair market rent for comparable Asheville restaurant space, but in no event less than the Base Rent payable in the final year of the preceding term — a contractual floor.\n'
  'Notice: not less than nine months before expiration — by December 31, 2029 for the first option.\n'
  'If fair market rent is not agreed within 60 days, a single mutually selected MAI appraiser determines it, binding on both parties. Condition: no default at exercise or commencement.'],
 ['(7) Termination Rights',
  'Co-tenancy (Art. 10): if aggregate occupancy of the Shopping Center falls below 70% of total leasable area for more than 180 consecutive days, the tenant may elect either (a) Base Rent reduced to 75% of the then-applicable rent plus percentage rent (with no breakpoint adjustment) until occupancy is restored, or (b) termination on 60 days\' notice, which is withdrawn if occupancy is restored before the effective date.\n'
  'Casualty: either party may terminate where more than 50% of the RSF is rendered untenantable, on 60 days\' notice delivered within 90 days of the damage (Art. 15). Condemnation: termination on a total or substantial taking (Art. 15).\n'
  'No other tenant or landlord termination right; no early termination fee mechanism.'],
 ['(8) Assignment and Subletting',
  'Consent required, not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed; attempted transfer without consent is void and an Event of Default (Art. 9).\n'
  'Landlord may consider the assignee\'s financial condition and creditworthiness, business reputation, proposed use and restaurant operating experience; may require the tenant to remain liable and the assignee to assume in writing (§9.2). No release in any event (§9.3).\n'
  'No recapture right, no profit-sharing obligation and no affiliate carve-out.'],
 ['(9) Security Deposit / Guaranty',
  'Cash Security Deposit of $19,800.00, equal to three (3) months of Lease Year 1 Base Rent (Art. 4); no interest; replenishment within ten days of application; returnable within 30 days after expiration and surrender.\n'
  'Personal Guaranty of Lance Whitford, the tenant\'s sole member (Exhibit D), unconditional and with broad waivers including any statute of limitations defence.\n'
  'Burn-off: the guaranty expires on the earliest of (a) September 30, 2025 (the last day of Lease Year 5) or (b) the date trailing-twelve-month Gross Sales reach $2,000,000 (Exhibit D §2). Accrued obligations survive. September 30, 2025 is 199 days after the target closing date.'],
 ['(10) Tenant Improvements',
  'No TI allowance is provided. The tenant funded its own build-out during the 4.5-month rent-free buildout period (§2.2), including kitchen, exhaust, grease interceptor and patio works.\n'
  'Tenant must maintain grease traps and interceptors at least quarterly with service records available to the landlord (Exhibit C, item 3).'],
 ['(11) Special Provisions',
  'Exclusive use (Art. 5.2): the tenant has the exclusive right to operate a full-service restaurant in the Shopping Center, subject to carve-outs permitting quick-service and fast-casual operators occupying less than 2,000 RSF, coffee shops, bakeries, ice cream and dessert shops and specialty food retailers. Remedies for breach are specific performance, injunctive relief and Base Rent abatement.\n'
  'Radius restriction (§5.3): the tenant may not operate a competing restaurant within three miles of the Premises during the term and for twelve months after, subject to a grandfathering carve-out; breach entitles the landlord to include the competing restaurant\'s revenues in Gross Sales.\n'
  'Liquor licensing: landlord must cooperate with ABC permit applications; the permit condition precedent was satisfied (§5.5).\n'
  'Breakpoint: Section 3.3 fixes the Breakpoint at $1,350,000 for each Lease Year, while Article 1 separately defines a "Natural Breakpoint" as annual Base Rent ÷ 0.06, recalculated annually — an internal conflict (R-22).\n'
  'SNDA on a commercially reasonable efforts basis (Art. 12). Holdover at 150% (Art. 2.4). No estoppel provision. Broker Ridgeview Realty Brokers Inc. (§18.7). North Carolina law, exclusive venue Buncombe County (§18.3).'],
 ['(12) Risk Flags',
  'R-21 — co-tenancy right: 25% rent reduction or termination if occupancy falls below 70% for 180 days.\n'
  'R-22 — fixed breakpoint of $1,350,000 conflicts with the defined "Natural Breakpoint" of Base Rent ÷ 0.06.\n'
  'R-23 — guaranty burns off on September 30, 2025, 199 days after closing.\n'
  'R-24 — Lease Years 6–10 rent is CPI-determined and unfixed; the CPI applied is unverifiable from the documents.\n'
  'R-10 — no estoppel provision. Percentage rent is unquantified for want of sales data.']],
 'Every stated Lease Year reproduces arithmetically: $18.000, $18.684, $19.431, $19.917 and $20.315 per RSF, each annual figure tying to the rate (for example $20.315 × 4,400 = $89,386.00; ÷ 12 = $7,448.83). '
 'The implied adjustments of 3.800%, 3.998%, 2.501% and 1.998% are all inside the 2%–4% band, the last being the floor applied with rounding. What cannot be verified is whether those were the correct CPI-U movements, because no index values are in the file and the leases do not identify the reference month figures; we can test band compliance only. '
 'The Pro Rata Share recomputes at 7.097% against the stated 7.10%, and the deposit at exactly three months of Year 1 rent ($6,600.00 × 3 = $19,800.00). '
 'The breakpoint conflict is quantified at Section 6.5: on the "Natural Breakpoint" definition the Year 5 threshold would be $1,489,766.67 rather than $1,350,000, a difference of $139,766.67, and the spread widens each year as Base Rent rises.',
 'The lease gives the tenant two substantial protections that reduce the value of the income stream. The co-tenancy right is the more serious: a 70% threshold in a 62,000 RSF centre is not demanding, the shortfall can arise from a single anchor vacancy, and the remedy — a 25% rent cut or outright termination — would remove or reduce 3.81% of portfolio rent. '
 'Because the lease requires monthly and annual sales reporting, the Seller should hold the data needed to test both the co-tenancy threshold and the percentage rent history, and its absence from the file is itself a diligence finding. '
 'The breakpoint conflict is a drafting error that favours the landlord on the fixed reading and the tenant on the defined reading; it should be resolved in the estoppel. The guaranty is of limited value given that it expires within seven months of closing.')

abstract_lease('4.7', 'United States of America (GSA), Lease No. GS-04B-15678 — Concord Office Tower, 5th Floor, Atlanta, GA',
 [('Premises','5th floor (entire), 15,000 RSF'),('Term','Firm 1/1/2021 – 12/31/2025; soft to 12/31/2030'),('Current rent','$472,500.00 p.a. ($31.50/RSF)'),('Type','GSA Form L201D, gross + base year')],
 [['(1) Tenant and Premises',
  'Lessor: Thornfield Realty Holdings LP, acting through its general partner Thornfield Management Corp. Lessee: the United States of America, acting by and through the General Services Administration, Region 4 (Southeast Sunbelt), Contracting Officer James Hua. Instrument: GSA Form L201D, Lease No. GS-04B-15678.\n'
  'Premises: the entire 5th floor, Concord Office Tower, 300 Concord Plaza Drive, Atlanta, Georgia 30309; 15,000 RSF measured under ANSI/BOMA Z65.1-2017, with any measurement dispute finally determined by the Contracting Officer (Section 2).\n'
  'SCIF: portions of the Premises may be designated a Sensitive Compartmented Information Facility or contain classified material; those areas are deliberately not shown on Exhibit A (Sections 2, 7.1, 10.2).\n'
  'Parking: non-exclusive, unreserved, at no charge, subject to availability (Section 20).'],
 ['(2) Term',
  'Execution Date September 30, 2020; Occupancy Date January 1, 2021.\n'
  'Firm Term: five years, January 1, 2021 to December 31, 2025 (Section 3.1). Soft Term: five years, January 1, 2026 to December 31, 2030 (Section 3.2). Total term ten years.\n'
  'Current Lease Year: Year 5 (January 1, 2025 – December 31, 2025), the final firm year.\n'
  'Remaining term at January 1, 2025: 1.00 year to the end of the firm term; 6.00 years to the nominal expiration at the end of the soft term.'],
 ['(3) Rent',
  'Shell rent of $31.50/RSF = $472,500.00 per annum = $39,375.00 per month, FIXED for the entire Firm Term (Section 4.1) — there is no escalation within the firm term.\n'
  'Soft Term escalation of 2.50% per annum compounding from $31.50 (Section 4.2; Exhibit B): Year 6 $32.29 ($484,350.00), Year 7 $33.10 ($496,500.00), Year 8 $33.93 ($508,950.00), Year 9 $34.78 ($521,700.00), Year 10 $35.64 ($534,600.00).\n'
  'Total Firm Term rent $2,362,500.00; total Soft Term rent $2,546,100.00; total $4,908,600.00 (Exhibit B — all three totals verified).\n'
  'Rent is payable monthly IN ARREARS by electronic funds transfer under the Prompt Payment Act (Section 4.1) — unusual for a commercial lease and relevant to receivables modelling.\n'
  'There is no late fee, default interest or acceleration mechanism. The Lessor\'s sole remedy for non-payment is a claim under the Contract Disputes Act (Sections 4.1, 14).'],
 ['(4) Lease Type',
  'Government lease on GSA Form L201D with a gross shell rent and a base-year operating expense escalation, structured as a firm term with a conditional soft term.'],
 ['(5) Operating Expenses',
  'The shell rent includes all Building operating expenses for the Base Year of calendar 2021 (Section 5.1). From calendar 2022 the Government pays its pro rata share of increases over the Base Year, computed as (15,000 ÷ total Building RSF) × (current-year expenses − Base Year expenses) (Section 5.2).\n'
  'Seasoned inclusions: common area maintenance, all utilities, janitorial, landscaping, pest control, management fees, insurance and real estate taxes (Sections 5.1, 5.3).\n'
  'Mechanics: annual statement within 90 days; underpayment within 30 days; overpayment credited to the next rent payment; a broad Government audit right exercisable during the term and for three years afterwards (Section 5.2).\n'
  'The certified Base Year 2021 operating expense statement was due by March 31, 2022 (Exhibit C) and is not in the file, so the contractual baseline is unevidenced.'],
 ['(6) Renewal Options',
  'None. The lease grants no renewal option or extension right of any kind. The Soft Term is not an option: it is the second five years of the ten-year term, during which the Government may remain subject to its unilateral termination right (Sections 3.1–3.2).\n'
  'This is the only lease in the Portfolio with no rollover mechanism in favour of the landlord.'],
 ['(7) Termination Rights',
  'Government termination right (Section 3.2): at any time after the Firm Term Expiration Date of December 31, 2025, on not less than 120 calendar days\' prior written notice, absolute and unilateral, without cause, and with no termination fee, penalty, liquidated damages or other consideration.\n'
  'Appropriations (Section 4.3): the Government\'s payment obligation is subject to the availability of appropriated funds and the Anti-Deficiency Act; the Government must give notice of non-availability.\n'
  'Casualty (Section 13.1): the Government may terminate on 30 days\' notice or require restoration within 180 days. Condemnation (Section 13.2).\n'
  'The Lessor has no termination right and no self-help remedy; the Government cannot be in default other than for non-payment (Section 14).'],
 ['(8) Assignment and Subletting',
  'The Government may assign the lease or sublet all or part of the Premises to any agency or instrumentality of the United States without the Lessor\'s consent, on written notice from the Contracting Officer (Section 8).\n'
  'The Lessor may not assign the lease or any interest in it, nor delegate any obligation, without the Contracting Officer\'s prior written consent (Section 8).\n'
  'On any sale or conveyance of the Building the Lessor must give the Contracting Officer at least 30 days\' prior written notice identifying the new owner, which automatically assumes the Lessor\'s obligations and must execute such documents as the Contracting Officer reasonably requires (Section 8).'],
 ['(9) Security Deposit / Guaranty',
  'None. No deposit, guaranty or letter of credit is provided or customary.\n'
  'The Government is self-insured under the Federal Tort Claims Act and carries no insurance; conversely the Lessor must carry property insurance at full replacement cost, commercial general liability of $1,000,000/$3,000,000 and workers\' compensation, with certificates on request (Section 9).'],
 ['(10) Tenant Improvements',
  'No Lessor allowance. All Government Improvements are funded by the Government at its sole cost (Section 7.1).\n'
  'All Government Improvements remain Government property at all times, are expressly not fixtures, and may be removed within 60 calendar days after expiration or termination (Section 7.2). The Government has no restoration obligation beyond repairing structural elements damaged by removal; cosmetic and non-structural elements need not be restored. Improvements not removed are abandoned and become the Lessor\'s property at no cost, with the Lessor assuming all risk as to their condition.\n'
  'Security installations — reinforced barriers, intrusion detection, TEMPEST shielding, sound attenuation, dedicated HVAC and supplemental power — are treated as Government Improvements (Section 10.2).'],
 ['(11) Special Provisions',
  'Classified space: the Lessor and its agents may not enter, inspect, photograph or interfere with SCIF areas without written authorisation from the Contracting Officer or Facility Security Officer, and must cooperate with security clearance processes (Sections 7.1, 10.2).\n'
  'Access and services: 24 hours a day, 365 days a year, with staffed lobby security during business hours at the Lessor\'s expense within operating expenses (Section 10.1); HVAC to ASHRAE 55, electrical, janitorial five nights weekly, elevator, common-area maintenance and snow removal (Section 6).\n'
  'Telecommunications: roof, riser and conduit rights at no charge, with no fee or rent, and installations not counted against the RSF (Section 11).\n'
  'Alterations by Lessor: the Lessor may not alter the Premises or the Building systems serving them — including HVAC, electrical, plumbing, elevators, life safety, security, structural elements and adjacent common areas — without the Contracting Officer\'s prior written consent, on 30 days\' notice (Section 12).\n'
  'Subordination: the lease is expressly NOT subordinate to any mortgage, deed of trust or other lien, and the Lessor may not grant any mortgage or lien that would take priority over the lease without the Contracting Officer\'s prior written consent; on foreclosure the lease remains in effect and any successor is bound (Section 16).\n'
  'Holdover: tenant at sufferance at the prior rent, with the Lessor expressly waiving any holdover premium or damages (Section 3.3).\n'
  'Disputes: Contract Disputes Act; appeal to the Civilian Board of Contract Appeals within 90 days or action in the Court of Federal Claims within 12 months (Sections 14, 19.2). Governing law: federal law (FAR/GSAR), with Georgia law to the extent not preempted (Section 19.1).'],
 ['(12) Risk Flags',
  'R-01 — firm term expires December 31, 2025, 9.6 months after the target closing; 120-day termination right thereafter.\n'
  'R-02 — no renewal option; no landlord rollover mechanism.\n'
  'R-11 — lease non-subordinate; priority liens prohibited without Contracting Officer consent.\n'
  'R-12 — change of ownership requires notice and Contracting Officer consent to assignment or delegation.\n'
  'SCIF and classified improvements constrain access, alteration and re-letting, and may leave unrestorable space (moderate).\n'
  'Anti-deficiency funding risk (low, given the nature of the tenancy).']],
 'The firm and soft term schedules were rebuilt and verified: the five firm years are flat at $31.50 ($472,500.00 per annum; $39,375.00 per month), and the soft term compounds at 2.5% from $31.50. Soft-term rates in Years 7, 8 and 9 are stated at $33.10, $33.93 and $34.78, whereas the unrounded formula produces $33.0947, $33.9221 and $34.7701 — differences of less than one cent per RSF ($79.69, $119.18 and $148.41 per annum respectively) which arise from compounding rounded rates rather than the formula. '
 'These are immaterial. The exhibit totals recompute exactly: firm $2,362,500.00; soft $2,546,100.00; total $4,908,600.00. The Government\'s pro rata share cannot be computed because the lease states the formula against total Building RSF without stating that figure; Verdana\'s lease puts the Building at approximately 150,000 RSF, which would produce a 10.00% share, but the GSA lease does not adopt that number.',
 'The GSA lease is the strongest covenant in the Portfolio and the weakest term. The Government tenant is effectively judgment-proof in the ordinary sense and the lease cannot be terminated for its default, but neither can the landlord rely on it beyond December 31, 2025: there is no renewal right, no holdover premium, and no compensation for termination. '
 'Three provisions have consequences beyond the tenancy itself. The non-subordination clause and the prohibition on priority liens constrain how Fieldstone can finance Concord Office Tower, which carries 48.93% of portfolio rent. '
 'The restriction on Lessor alterations to building systems serving the 5th floor limits capital works on the property without Contracting Officer approval. And the SCIF regime means that part of the Premises may be neither inspected by the landlord nor easily re-let, and that substantial Government Improvements may either be stripped at the end of the term or left behind in a condition the landlord must accept. '
 'The transfer provisions require notice to, and in our view consent from, the Contracting Officer — a closing condition that should be addressed early.')
PY
echo ok"}

# ---------------- 4.5 VERDANA ----------------
abstract_lease('4.5', 'Verdana Software Solutions Inc. — Concord Office Tower, 8th Floor, Atlanta, GA',
 [('Premises','8th floor (entire), 18,750 RSF'),('Term','7/1/2022 – 6/30/2032 (10 yrs)'),('Current rent','$676,312.50 p.a. ($36.07/RSF)'),('Type','Full-service gross, BY 2022')],
 [['(1) Tenant and Premises',
  'Landlord: Thornfield Realty Holdings LP. Tenant: Verdana Software Solutions Inc., a Delaware corporation qualified to do business in Georgia.\n'
  'Premises: the entire 8th floor, Concord Office Tower, 300 Concord Plaza Drive, Atlanta, Fulton County, Georgia 30309; approximately 18,750 RSF measured under ANSI/BOMA Z65.1-2017 and stipulated conclusive absent written agreement (§2.02). The floor plate is the whole floor.\n'
  'Building: approximately 150,000 RSF; Pro Rata Share 12.50% (18,750 ÷ 150,000) (Art. I).\n'
  'Permitted use: general office, software development and ancillary uses (§6.01). Parking: 56 unreserved spaces free of charge (approximately 2.99 per 1,000 RSF) plus 8 reserved executive spaces on Level P1 at $175.00 per space per month (Art. XV; Exhibit D).'],
 ['(2) Term',
  'Lease Date February 28, 2022; Commencement Date July 1, 2022; Expiration Date June 30, 2032; term of ten (10) years (§3.02).\n'
  'Early access from April 1, 2022 to construct improvements, without Base Rent and without affecting the Expiration Date (§3.03). A Commencement Date Memorandum was to be executed within 30 days of commencement (§3.04) — none is in the file.\n'
  'Current Lease Year: Year 3 (July 1, 2024 – June 30, 2025). Remaining term at January 1, 2025: 7.49 years (2,737 days).'],
 ['(3) Rent',
  'Base Rent monthly in advance on the first day of each month (§4.01).\n'
  'Lease Year 1: $34.00/RSF = $637,500.00 per annum = $53,125.00 per month (§4.02).\n'
  'Escalation: three percent (3%) per annum compounded annually from each anniversary of the Commencement Date (§4.03; Exhibit B).\n'
  'Current (Year 3): $36.07/RSF = $676,312.50 per annum = $56,359.38 per month. Scheduled Year 10 (July 1, 2031 – June 30, 2032): $44.35/RSF = $831,562.50.\n'
  'Additional Rent: 8 reserved spaces at $175.00 = $1,400.00 per month ($16,800.00 per annum), adjustable annually by up to 5% (Exhibit D §2).\n'
  'Late charge 5% after five business days; interest at 1.5% per month (18% per annum) or the maximum lawful rate on amounts unpaid for more than ten days (§§4.05–4.06).'],
 ['(4) Lease Type',
  'Full-service gross with a Base Year 2022 expense stop (§5.01). Landlord pays all Building operating expenses; the tenant pays only its share of increases above the Base Year.'],
 ['(5) Operating Expenses',
  'Tenant pays 12.50% of the excess of actual Operating Expenses over calendar 2022 actuals, commencing January 1, 2023 (§5.01).\n'
  'Controllable expense cap: controllable operating expenses (all expenses other than real estate taxes, insurance, utilities and snow/ice removal) may not increase by more than 5% per annum on a cumulative compounding basis over the Base Year (§5.07). Gross-up to 95% occupancy for occupancy-variable expenses (§5.08). Management fee not exceeding 4% of gross revenues (§5.02(g)).\n'
  'Exclusions include capital improvements except law-mandated or cost-reducing items amortised at 8%, leasing commissions and advertising, other tenants\' improvements and concessions, insurance and condemnation recoveries, depreciation, debt service, landlord income taxes, costs of landlord negligence and construction defects, and legal fees in tenant disputes (§5.03).\n'
  'Mechanics: monthly estimates, revisable during the year; annual statement within 120 days; audit within 12 months on 30 days\' notice, with auditor fees reimbursed where overcharge exceeds 5% and a prohibition on contingency-fee auditors (§§5.04–5.06).'],
 ['(6) Renewal Options',
  'Two consecutive five-year options: July 1, 2032 – June 30, 2037 and July 1, 2037 – June 30, 2042 (Art. XII).\n'
  'Rent: 95% of the then-prevailing fair market rent for comparable Class A Atlanta midtown/Buckhead office space, determined by a three-appraiser process (average of the two closest appraisals) (§§12.03–12.04).\n'
  'Notice: not less than twelve months before expiration — by June 30, 2031 for the first option. The options must be exercised consecutively (§12.02).\n'
  'No further TI allowance on renewal; no default condition (§12.05).'],
 ['(7) Termination Rights',
  'Contraction right (Art. XIV): after the expiration of Lease Year 5, i.e. on or after July 1, 2027, the tenant may once surrender up to 5,000 RSF on nine months\' notice. The contraction fee is the unamortised TI allocable to that space at 7% mortgage-style amortisation on $55.00/RSF, plus six months\' Base Rent on the space at the then-current rate (§§14.01–14.04). Base Rent and the Pro Rata Share reduce pro rata.\n'
  'Casualty: either party may terminate if the landlord determines that restoration cannot be completed within 270 days (§18.02). Condemnation: total taking terminates; partial taking permits termination if the remainder is unsuitable (Art. XIX).\n'
  'On default the landlord may accelerate all remaining rent, discounted at the Federal Reserve discount rate plus 1% (§20.02(iii)).'],
 ['(8) Assignment and Subletting',
  'Assignment: consent required, not unreasonably withheld; the original tenant remains secondarily liable for the remainder of the term unless released in writing (§11.05).\n'
  'Subletting up to 40% of the RSF (7,500 RSF) is permitted WITHOUT consent, subject to conditions — permitted use, no governmental entity, not an existing tenant or a prospect in active negotiation, ten business days\' post-execution notice with a copy of the sublease and financial information, and continuing tenant liability (§11.02). Subletting above 40% requires consent, not unreasonably withheld, with deemed consent if the landlord does not respond within 20 business days (§11.03).\n'
  'Profit sharing: 50% of Subletting Profits to the landlord, calculated monthly, with quarterly accounting (§11.04).\n'
  'No recapture right, termination right or cancellation right arises on any assignment or subletting (§11.07). Permitted affiliate transfers without consent, subject to a tangible net worth test and 15 days\' notice (§11.06). No release (§11.08).'],
 ['(9) Security Deposit / Guaranty',
  'None. The Section I summary states "Security Deposit: None"; the rent roll field is blank. There is no guaranty and no letter of credit. The landlord\'s protection is the lease, the acceleration remedy and the tenant\'s covenant strength.'],
 ['(10) Tenant Improvements',
  'TI Allowance of $55.00/RSF = $1,031,250.00 (§7.01; Exhibit C).\n'
  'Disbursement monthly against AIA G702/G703 applications, unconditional lien waivers for prior amounts and conditional waivers for the current draw, with 10% retainage released on substantial completion and receipt of a certificate of occupancy (Exhibit C §4). Unused allowance is forfeited and confers no credit (§7.03).\n'
  'For recapture the allowance amortises at 7% per annum over 120 months on a mortgage-style schedule (§7.04). Improvements vest in the landlord; designated non-standard items may be removed (§7.05).'],
 ['(11) Special Provisions',
  'Expansion option (Art. XIII): the tenant may expand onto the 9th floor (approximately 18,500 RSF) at any time during Lease Years 3 to 5, i.e. July 1, 2024 to June 30, 2027, on six months\' notice. Rent is at the then-current per-RSF rate for the Premises, escalating on the same 3% schedule, coterminous to June 30, 2032, with a TI allowance of $40.00/RSF ($740,000.00 for 18,500 RSF).\n'
  'Estoppel: certificate within 15 business days; failure is an irrevocable acknowledgment of the requesting party\'s form (Art. XXIV).\n'
  'Subordination: subordinate only if the mortgagee delivers a commercially reasonable SNDA (17.01); landlord represented that no mortgage encumbered the Building at the Lease Date (17.02).\n'
  'Landlord liability limited to its interest in the Building (Art. XXVII). Holdover at 150%, tenant at sufferance (20.04). No recording without consent, memorandum permitted (26.07). After-hours HVAC at $75.00 per hour per zone (8.03). Prevailing-party attorneys\' fees (26.12). Georgia law (26.01).'],
 ['(12) Risk Flags',
  'R-17 — live expansion option over 18,500 RSF with a $740,000 TI obligation, exercisable to June 30, 2027.\n'
  'R-18 — contraction right of up to 5,000 RSF from July 1, 2027.\n'
  'R-19 — 40% sublease without consent and no landlord recapture right.\n'
  'R-20 — no deposit or guaranty for the largest tenant exposure (28.81%).\n'
  'Concentration — Concord Office Tower carries 48.93% of portfolio rent across this lease and the GSA lease.']],
 'All ten lease years recompute exactly at 3% compounding, and every annual and monthly figure ties to the stated per-RSF rate ($36.07 × 18,750 = $676,312.50; ÷ 12 = $56,359.38). The Pro Rata Share recomputes at exactly 12.50% (18,750 ÷ 150,000); the TI allowance at $1,031,250.00 (18,750 × $55.00); the reserved parking at $16,800.00 per annum (8 × $175 × 12); '
 'and the parking ratio at 2.987 per 1,000 RSF against the stated 2.99. The expansion TI allowance recomputes at $740,000.00 (18,500 × $40.00). No arithmetic exception arises in this lease. The unquantified items are the contraction fee (which depends on the amortisation schedule, the contraction date and the rent then in effect) and the 9th-floor expansion rent.',
 'Verdana is the Portfolio\'s largest tenant and its least protected exposure: 28.81% of current rent with no deposit, no guaranty and no letter of credit. The lease is, however, structured in the landlord\'s favour on transfers — a 40% free-sublease right is unusual for a tenant of this size, and the absence of any recapture right (§11.07) removes the landlord\'s principal protection, although the 50% profit share partly compensates. '
 'The expansion option is a live, dated liability: it must be exercised, if at all, by June 30, 2027, and if exercised obliges the landlord to fund up to $740,000 of improvements while letting 18,500 RSF at the 8th-floor rate rather than market. It also constrains the landlord\'s ability to pre-let the 9th floor on better terms during the option window. '
 'The contraction right from July 2027 is a smaller but real value leak on a fully leased floor plate.')

# ---------------- 4.6 PINT & PLATTER ----------------
abstract_lease('4.6', 'The Pint & Platter Restaurant Group LLC — Haywood Village Shops, Unit 4, Asheville, NC',
 [('Premises','Unit 4 + patio, 4,400 RSF'),('Term','10/1/2020 – 9/30/2030 (10 yrs)'),('Current rent','$89,386.00 p.a. ($20.315/RSF)'),('Type','NNN + 6% percentage rent')],
 [['(1) Tenant and Premises',
  'Landlord: Thornfield Realty Holdings LP. Tenant: The Pint & Platter Restaurant Group LLC, a North Carolina limited liability company whose sole member is Lance Whitford; Guarantor: Lance Whitford, individually (Exhibit D).\n'
  'Premises: Unit 4, ground floor retail space including the adjacent patio area, Haywood Village Shops, 92 Haywood Street, Asheville, Buncombe County, North Carolina 28801; approximately 4,400 RSF (§2.1).\n'
  'Shopping Center: approximately 62,000 RSF of leasable retail and commercial space; Pro Rata Share approximately 7.10% (§1; recomputed at 7.097%).\n'
  'Permitted use: full-service restaurant, bar and related food and beverage service, including on-premises and off-premises catering, private events and delivery (§5.1).'],
 ['(2) Term',
  'Lease Date May 15, 2020; Commencement Date October 1, 2020; Expiration Date September 30, 2030; term of ten (10) years (§2.2).\n'
  'Buildout Period from May 15, 2020 to September 30, 2020 (approximately 4.5 months) with no Base Rent or percentage rent, tenant paying utilities and insurance (§2.2).\n'
  'Current Lease Year: Year 5 (October 1, 2024 – September 30, 2025). Remaining term at January 1, 2025: 5.74 years (2,098 days).'],
 ['(3) Rent',
  'Base Rent monthly in advance on the first day of each month (§3.1).\n'
  'Lease Year 1: $18.00/RSF = $79,200.00 per annum = $6,600.00 per month.\n'
  'Escalation: CPI adjustment on each October 1, calculated as the percentage change in CPI-U (U.S. City Average, All Items, 1982–84 = 100) for the month three months before the adjustment date against the same month of the prior year, subject to a 2.00% floor and a 4.00% cap (§3.2).\n'
  'Stated adjustments, Lease Years 2–5: 3.800%, 3.998%, 2.501% and 1.998% — i.e. $18.684, $19.431, $19.917 and $20.315 per RSF. Current (Year 5): $89,386.00 per annum = $7,448.83 per month.\n'
  'Lease Years 6–10 are not fixed: the lease requires annual CPI determination, and Exhibit B records them as "TBD" (§3.2).\n'
  'Percentage Rent: 6.00% of annual Gross Sales above the Breakpoint, commencing Lease Year 2, payable annually within 60 days after each Lease Year against a certified annual statement delivered within 30 days; monthly sales reports within 15 days; landlord audit once per Lease Year covering the three most recent years, with costs, deficiency and 1.5% monthly interest payable if gross sales are understated by more than 3% (§§3.3–3.4).\n'
  'Late charge 5% after five days; interest 1.5% per month (§3.6).'],
 ['(4) Lease Type',
  'Triple net plus percentage rent (Art. 6). Tenant pays Base Rent, Percentage Rent and its Pro Rata Share of taxes, insurance and CAM.'],
 ['(5) Operating Expenses',
  'Operating Expenses are defined as real estate taxes and assessments, property insurance premiums and CAM Expenses (Art. 1; §3.5).\n'
  'CAM management fee not exceeding 4% of gross rental revenue of the Shopping Center (Art. 1). Operating Expenses exclude landlord financing costs, depreciation, capital improvements except as amortised where required by law or to reduce expenses, and leasing commissions (§6.1).\n'
  'Mechanics: annual estimate paid in twelfths; reconciliation within 90 days; overpayment credited, underpayment due within 30 days (§§3.5, 6.2). Tenant audit right for the preceding year on 30 days\' notice at its own expense (§6.2).'],
 ['(6) Renewal Options',
  'Two five-year options (Art. 11). Rent is the then-prevailing fair market rent for comparable Asheville restaurant space, but in no event less than the Base Rent payable in the final year of the preceding term — a contractual floor.\n'
  'Notice: not less than nine months before expiration — by December 31, 2029 for the first option.\n'
  'If fair market rent is not agreed within 60 days, a single mutually selected MAI appraiser determines it, binding on both parties. Condition: no default at exercise or commencement.'],
 ['(7) Termination Rights',
  'Co-tenancy (Art. 10): if aggregate occupancy of the Shopping Center falls below 70% of total leasable area for more than 180 consecutive days, the tenant may elect either (a) Base Rent reduced to 75% of the then-applicable rent plus percentage rent (with no breakpoint adjustment) until occupancy is restored, or (b) termination on 60 days\' notice, which is withdrawn if occupancy is restored before the effective date.\n'
  'Casualty: either party may terminate where more than 50% of the RSF is rendered untenantable, on 60 days\' notice delivered within 90 days of the damage (Art. 15). Condemnation: termination on a total or substantial taking (Art. 15).\n'
  'No other tenant or landlord termination right; no early termination fee mechanism.'],
 ['(8) Assignment and Subletting',
  'Consent required, not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed; attempted transfer without consent is void and an Event of Default (Art. 9).\n'
  'Landlord may consider the assignee\'s financial condition and creditworthiness, business reputation, proposed use and restaurant operating experience; may require the tenant to remain liable and the assignee to assume in writing (§9.2). No release in any event (§9.3).\n'
  'No recapture right, no profit-sharing obligation and no affiliate carve-out.'],
 ['(9) Security Deposit / Guaranty',
  'Cash Security Deposit of $19,800.00, equal to three (3) months of Lease Year 1 Base Rent (Art. 4); no interest; replenishment within ten days of application; returnable within 30 days after expiration and surrender.\n'
  'Personal Guaranty of Lance Whitford, the tenant\'s sole member (Exhibit D), unconditional and with broad waivers including any statute of limitations defence.\n'
  'Burn-off: the guaranty expires on the earliest of (a) September 30, 2025 (the last day of Lease Year 5) or (b) the date trailing-twelve-month Gross Sales reach $2,000,000 (Exhibit D §2). Accrued obligations survive. September 30, 2025 is 199 days after the target closing date.'],
 ['(10) Tenant Improvements',
  'No TI allowance is provided. The tenant funded its own build-out during the 4.5-month rent-free buildout period (§2.2), including kitchen, exhaust, grease interceptor and patio works.\n'
  'Tenant must maintain grease traps and interceptors at least quarterly with service records available to the landlord (Exhibit C, item 3).'],
 ['(11) Special Provisions',
  'Exclusive use (Art. 5.2): the tenant has the exclusive right to operate a full-service restaurant in the Shopping Center, subject to carve-outs permitting quick-service and fast-casual operators occupying less than 2,000 RSF, coffee shops, bakeries, ice cream and dessert shops and specialty food retailers. Remedies for breach are specific performance, injunctive relief and Base Rent abatement.\n'
  'Radius restriction (§5.3): the tenant may not operate a competing restaurant within three miles of the Premises during the term and for twelve months after, subject to a grandfathering carve-out; breach entitles the landlord to include the competing restaurant\'s revenues in Gross Sales.\n'
  'Liquor licensing: landlord must cooperate with ABC permit applications; the permit condition precedent was satisfied (§5.5).\n'
  'Breakpoint: Section 3.3 fixes the Breakpoint at $1,350,000 for each Lease Year, while Article 1 separately defines a "Natural Breakpoint" as annual Base Rent ÷ 0.06, recalculated annually — an internal conflict (R-22).\n'

para(doc, 'Section 4.1 and Exhibit B state that Base Rent increases by 2% per annum on each anniversary. Lease Years 1 to 9 comply within cent-level rounding. Lease Year 10 is stated at $9.25, but $8.79 × 1.02 = $8.9658 — an implied step of 5.233%. '
          'This is the most consequential of the three exceptions for two reasons.           'Second, the holdover rent now being paid is 150% of a monthly figure derived from the overstated $9.25 rate, so the error is being carried forward and compounded at 150%.', size=9.6)

          'A valuation that capitalises the full $2.35 million across a blended 5.25-year term will overstate value; the income should be modelled lease by lease with the rollover and termination rights applied.', size=9.5)

          'every figure used in this Report traces to a row below, and every departure between the two sources is identified rather than netted away. Where the rent roll contains no field for the data point, the ledger says so.', size=9.3)

def ledger(entries, widths=(1.05,1.4,2.6,2.4,2.35), font_size=7.0):
    ncol = len(widths)
    t = doc.add_table(rows=1, cols=ncol); t.autofit=False
    set_borders(t, sz=4, color='BFBFBF'); cell_margins(t, 35,35,60,60)
    tblPr = t._tbl.tblPr
    layout = OxmlElement('w:tblLayout'); layout.set(qn('w:type'),'fixed'); tblPr.append(layout)
    hdr = ['Data point','Controlling source','Lease document','Rent roll','Status / reconciliation basis']
    for i,h in enumerate(hdr):
        c = t.rows[0].cells[i]; c.width = Inches(widths[i]); c.text=''
        p=c.paragraphs[0]; p.paragraph_format.space_before=Pt(1); p.paragraph_format.space_after=Pt(1)
        r=p.add_run(h); r.bold=True; r.font.size=Pt(font_size); r.font.color.rgb=WHITE
        shade(c,'1F3864')
    repeat_header(t.rows[0]); cant_split(t.rows[0])
    for e in entries:
        if e[0]=='GROUP':
            row = t.add_row(); cant_split(row)
            merged = row.cells[0].merge(row.cells[ncol-1])
            merged.text=''
            p=merged.paragraphs[0]; p.paragraph_format.space_before=Pt(2); p.paragraph_format.space_after=Pt(1)
            r=p.add_run(e[1]); r.bold=True; r.font.size=Pt(font_size+0.4); r.font.color.rgb=NAVY

                if i==0: rr.bold=True

"Rate variance" shows the stated rate less the recomputed rate; a bracketed figure means the lease understates what the formula produces. '
          'Annual variances are computed on the recomputed rate multiplied by the rentable area.', size=9.3)

def fmt(v, dp=3):
    s = f'{abs(v):,.{dp}f}'
    return f'({s})' if v < -0.0000001 else s

def rebuild(title, rsf, years, base, formula, dp_rate=3, note=''):
    caption(doc, title)
    rows=[]
    prev = None
    for (y, period, stated, ann) in years:
        comp = base if prev is None else formula(prev)
        rv = round(stated - comp, dp_rate+1)
        a_comp = round(comp*rsf, 2); a_stated = ann
        rows.append([str(y), period, f'{stated:,.{dp_rate}f}', f'{comp:,.{dp_rate}f}', fmt(rv, dp_rate),
                     f'${a_stated:,.2f}', f'${a_comp:,.2f}', fmt(a_comp - a_stated, 2)])
        prev = stated
    table(doc, ['Year','Period','Stated\n$/RSF','Recomputed\n$/RSF','Rate\nvariance','Stated\nannual','Recomputed\nannual','Annual\nvariance'],
          rows, widths=[0.5,2.35,0.95,1.05,0.9,1.3,1.35,1.2], font_size=7.6, right_cols=(2,3,4,5,6,7))
    if note: source_note(doc, note)
    para(doc,'',space_after=6)

doc.add_page_break()
h1(doc, 'Appendix B', 'Rent Schedule Recomputation')
para(doc, 'Each schedule was rebuilt from its Lease Year 1 rate using the escalation formula recited in the lease, at the rounding precision the lease specifies, and compared to the stated rate and stated annual rent. "Rate variance" shows the stated rate less the recomputed rate; a bracketed figure means the lease understates what the formula produces. '
          'Annual variances are computed on the recomputed rate multiplied by the rentable area.', size=9.3)

def fmt(v, dp=3):
    s = f'{abs(v):,.{dp}f}'
    return f'({s})' if v < -0.0000001 else s

def rebuild(title, rsf, years, base, formula, dp_rate=3, note=''):
    caption(doc, title)
    rows=[]
    prev = None
    for (y, period, stated, ann) in years:
        comp = base if prev is None else formula(prev)
        rv = round(stated - comp, dp_rate+1)
        a_comp = round(comp*rsf, 2); a_stated = ann
        rows.append([str(y), period, f'{stated:,.{dp_rate}f}', f'{comp:,.{dp_rate}f}', fmt(rv, dp_rate),
                     f'${a_stated:,.2f}', f'${a_comp:,.2f}', fmt(a_comp - a_stated, 2)])
        prev = stated
    table(doc, ['Year','Period','Stated\n$/RSF','Recomputed\n$/RSF','Rate\nvariance','Stated\nannual','Recomputed\nannual','Annual\nvariance'],
          rows, widths=[0.5,2.35,0.95,1.05,0.9,1.3,1.35,1.2], font_size=7.6, right_cols=(2,3,4,5,6,7))
    if note: source_note(doc, note)
    para(doc,'',space_after=6)

{"file_path": "response.md", "content": "# Lease Abstraction Report — completed

**Deliverable:** `lease-abstraction-report.docx` (76 pages, 55 tables, Birchwood & Hale LLP work product, dated December 20, 2024)

All seven leases, the rent roll and the engagement letter were read in full (including exhibits, signature blocks and acknowledgments), and every figure was independently recomputed before drafting.

## What the report contains

| Section | Content |
|---|---|
| 1 | Executive summary — portfolio metrics, aggregate rent, WALT, tenant/property concentration, ten prioritized findings (F1–F10), priority action table, limitations |
| 2 | Scope, source inventory, methodology/conventions, the twelve-category schema, separation of fact/verification/characterization/recommendation, document deficiencies |
| 3 | Portfolio overview (landscape) — consolidated lease table, recovery-structure comparison, expiration ladder, composition of the aggregate |
| 4 | Seven individual abstractions, each in the twelve mandated categories (1)–(12), with verification notes and risk flags |
| 5 | Rent roll cross-check — 16 exceptions quantified, 15 fields verified as consistent, WALT methodology reconciliation |
| 6 | Escalation verification — recomputation results, three exceptions quantified, CPI gap, de minimis items, effect on aggregate rent |
| 7 | Risk matrix — 31 items rated by severity (Critical/High/Moderate/Low) and timing (Immediate/Pre-closing/Post-closing/Closed), with quantified exposure and commentary |
| 8 | Action plan (14 actions), lease-by-lease estoppel and closing-deliverable schedule, post-closing watch list with day counts |
| 9 | Open items and information requests |
| A–D | Controlling-value reconciliation ledger (70+ data points traced to source), year-by-year rent schedule recomputations, source inventory, abbreviations and basis notes |

## Principal findings

- **Aggregate rent ties exactly:** $2,347,843.50 (arithmetic verified against the rent roll and the engagement estimate). Verified figure after correcting three escalation errors: **$2,340,578.50**.
- **$305,250.00 of that total is not contractual.** Southeastern Fire & Safety expired 6/30/2024 and the renewal option lapsed 4/1/2024; the tenant holds over month-to-month at 150%. Contractual base rent is $2,042,593.50.
- **37.25% of rent is at risk within 24 months:** Southeastern (at will), GSA (firm term ends 12/31/2025, no renewal right), Soto (termination notice due 4/30/2025 — 46 days after closing).
- **The Acquisition itself triggers the Apex ROFR** over Building C (portfolio-transaction wording, allocable price, 30-day election) — 23.74% of rent.
- **Three leases breach their own escalation formulas:** Apex Year 5/6 (−$525 p.a.), BrightPath Year 8 (−$1,450 p.a.; −$12,529 over term), Southeastern Year 10 (+$6,252 historical, and it inflates the holdover rate by ~$9,240 p.a.).
- **No estoppels exist in the file, and five of seven leases contain no estoppel covenant.**
- **GSA lease is expressly non-subordinate** and bars priority liens without Contracting Officer consent — constrains debt on the building carrying 48.93% of portfolio rent.
- **WALT is 5.25 years**, not the 5.7 reported; the rent roll figure is reconcilable only on a whole-lease-year convention (5.60).

## Validation

- `validate.py` → `OK: lease-abstraction-report.docx valid` (ZIP integrity, XML well-formedness, ECMA-376 schema, content types, relationships).
- Rendered to PDF (76 pages) and inspected page by page; table-of-contents page numbers are generated from the rendered output and verified to match (zero mismatches).
"}
